# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

<h1 id="openai-api-assistants">Assistants</h1>

Build Assistants that can call models and use tools.

## List assistants

<a id="opIdlistAssistants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/assistants \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /assistants`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns a list of assistants.

<h3 id="list-assistants-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 20.<br>|
|order|query|string|false|Sort order by the `created_at` timestamp of the objects. `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include after=obj_foo in order to fetch the next page of the list.<br>|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include before=obj_foo in order to fetch the previous page of the list.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "object": "assistant",
      "created_at": 0,
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "model": "string",
      "instructions": "string",
      "tools": [],
      "tool_resources": {
        "code_interpreter": {
          "file_ids": []
        },
        "file_search": {
          "vector_store_ids": [
            "string"
          ]
        }
      },
      "metadata": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "temperature": 1,
      "top_p": 1,
      "response_format": "auto"
    }
  ],
  "first_id": "asst_abc123",
  "last_id": "asst_abc456",
  "has_more": false
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "misalignment": {
      "review_target": "string",
      "error_type": "string",
      "detailed_explanation": "string",
      "steer": {
        "message": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-assistants-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ListAssistantsResponse](#schemalistassistantsresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The request was rejected because a rate limit was exceeded.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|429|Retry-After|integer||The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted for 429 responses that require user action.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## Create assistant

<a id="opIdcreateAssistant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/assistants \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4.1",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "instructions": "string",
    "reasoning_effort": "medium",
    "tools": [],
    "tool_resources": {
      "code_interpreter": {
        "file_ids": []
      },
      "file_search": {
        "vector_store_ids": [
          "string"
        ],
        "vector_stores": [
          {
            "file_ids": [
              "string"
            ],
            "chunking_strategy": {
              "type": "auto"
            },
            "metadata": {
              "property1": "string",
              "property2": "string"
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "temperature": 1,
    "top_p": 1,
    "response_format": "auto"
  }'
```

`POST /assistants`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Create an assistant with a model and instructions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4.1",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "instructions": "string",
  "reasoning_effort": "medium",
  "tools": [],
  "tool_resources": {
    "code_interpreter": {
      "file_ids": []
    },
    "file_search": {
      "vector_store_ids": [
        "string"
      ],
      "vector_stores": [
        {
          "file_ids": [
            "string"
          ],
          "chunking_strategy": {
            "type": "auto"
          },
          "metadata": {
            "property1": "string",
            "property2": "string"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "temperature": 1,
  "top_p": 1,
  "response_format": "auto"
}
```

Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).<br><br>Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.<br><br>**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. > Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/assistants/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "string",
    "reasoning_effort": "medium",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "instructions": "string",
    "tools": [],
    "tool_resources": {
      "code_interpreter": {
        "file_ids": []
      },
      "file_search": {
        "vector_store_ids": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    },
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "temperature": 1,
    "top_p": 1,
    "response_format": "auto"
  }'
```

`GET /threads/{thread_id}/messages`

Returns a list of messages for a given thread.

<h3 id="list-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|thread_id|path|string|true|The ID of the [thread](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) the messages belong to.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 20.<br>|
|order|query|string|false|Sort order by the `created_at` timestamp of the objects. `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include after=obj_foo in order to fetch the next page of the list.<br>|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include before=obj_foo in order to fetch the previous page of the list.<br>|
|run_id|query|string|false|Filter messages by the run ID that generated them.<br>|

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include after=obj_foo in order to fetch the next page of the list.<br>|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include before=obj_foo in order to fetch the previous page of the list.<br>|

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

|» additional_instructions|body|string \| null|false|Appends additional instructions at the end of the instructions for the run. This is useful for modifying the behavior on a per-run basis without overriding other instructions.|
|» additional_messages|body|[[CreateMessageRequest](#schemacreatemessagerequest)]|false|Adds additional messages to the thread before creating the run.|
|» tools|body|[[AssistantToolsCode](#schemaassistanttoolscode) \| [AssistantToolsFileSearch](#schemaassistanttoolsfilesearch) \| [AssistantToolsFunction](#schemaassistanttoolsfunction)]|false|Override the tools the assistant can use for this run. This is useful for modifying the behavior on a per-run basis.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AssistantToolsCode](#schemaassistanttoolscode)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AssistantToolsFileSearch](#schemaassistanttoolsfilesearch)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AssistantToolsFunction](#schemaassistanttoolsfunction)|false|none|
|» metadata|body|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.<br>|
|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.<br><br>We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.<br>|
|» stream|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, returns a stream of events that happen during the Run as server-sent events, terminating when the Run enters a terminal state with a `data: [DONE]` message.<br>|
|» max_prompt_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of prompt tokens that may be used over the course of the run. The run will make a best effort to use only the number of prompt tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run. If the run exceeds the number of prompt tokens specified, the run will end with status `incomplete`. See `incomplete_details` for more info.<br>|
|» max_completion_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of completion tokens that may be used over the course of the run. The run will make a best effort to use only the number of completion tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run. If the run exceeds the number of completion tokens specified, the run will end with status `incomplete`. See `incomplete_details` for more info.<br>|
|» truncation_strategy|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|The truncation strategy to use for the thread. The default is `auto`. If set to `last_messages`, the thread will be truncated to the n most recent messages in the thread. When set to `auto`, messages in the middle of the thread will be dropped to fit the context length of the model, `max_prompt_tokens`.|
|» » last_messages|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|The number of most recent messages from the thread when constructing the context for the run.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tool_choice|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|`none` means the model will not call any tools and instead generates a message. `auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. `required` means the model must call one or more tools before responding to the user.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AssistantsNamedToolChoice](#schemaassistantsnamedtoolchoice)|false|Specifies a tool the model should use. Use to force the model to call a specific tool.|
|» parallel_tool_calls|body|[ParallelToolCalls](#schemaparalleltoolcalls)|false|Whether to enable [parallel function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#parallel-function-calling) during tool use.|
|» response_format|body|[AssistantsApiResponseFormatOption](#schemaassistantsapiresponseformatoption)|false|Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with [GPT-4o](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o), [GPT-4 Turbo](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4-turbo), and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`.<br><br>Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).<br><br>Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.<br><br>**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. Without this, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace until the generation reaches the token limit, resulting in a long-running and seemingly "stuck" request. Also note that the message content may be partially cut off if `finish_reason="length"`, which indicates the generation exceeded `max_tokens` or the conversation exceeded the max context length.<br>|

## Submit tool outputs to run

<a id="opIdsubmitToolOuputsToRun"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/threads/string/runs/string/submit_tool_outputs \

      }
    ],
    "stream": true
  }'
```

`POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs/{run_id}/submit_tool_outputs`

When a run has the `status: "requires_action"` and `required_action.type` is `submit_tool_outputs`, this endpoint can be used to submit the outputs from the tool calls once they're all completed. All outputs must be submitted in a single request.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tool_outputs": [
    {
      "tool_call_id": "string",
      "output": "string"
    }
  ],
  "stream": true
}
```

<h3 id="submit-tool-outputs-to-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|thread_id|path|string|true|The ID of the [thread](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) to which this run belongs.|
|run_id|path|string|true|The ID of the run that requires the tool output submission.|
|body|body|[SubmitToolOutputsRunRequest](#schemasubmittooloutputsrunrequest)|true|none|
|» tool_outputs|body|[object]|true|A list of tools for which the outputs are being submitted.|
|» » tool_call_id|body|string|false|The ID of the tool call in the `required_action` object within the run object the output is being submitted for.|
|» » output|body|string|false|The output of the tool call to be submitted to continue the run.|
|» stream|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|If `true`, returns a stream of events that happen during the Run as server-sent events, terminating when the Run enters a terminal state with a `data: [DONE]` message.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

<h1 id="openai-api-audio">Audio</h1>

Turn audio into text or text into audio.

## Create speech

<a id="opIdcreateSpeech"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "string",
    "input": "string",
    "instructions": "string",
    "voice": "ash",
    "response_format": "mp3",
    "speed": 1,
    "stream_format": "audio"
  }'
```

`POST /audio/speech`

Generates audio from the input text.

Returns the audio file content, or a stream of audio events.

The `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-03-20`, and
`gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15` models are deprecated and scheduled to shut down
on January 6, 2027. These examples use the existing Speech API; for new
integrations, migrate to `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` through the
[Realtime API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime). See the
[deprecation schedule](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) for migration details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "instructions": "string",
  "voice": "ash",
  "response_format": "mp3",
  "speed": 1,
  "stream_format": "audio"
}
```

<h3 id="create-speech-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateSpeechRequest](#schemacreatespeechrequest)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|One of the available [TTS models](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text-to-speech): `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, or `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15`.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» input|body|string|true|The text to generate audio for. The maximum length is 4096 characters.|
|» instructions|body|string|false|Control the voice of your generated audio with additional instructions. Does not work with `tts-1` or `tts-1-hd`.|
|» voice|body|[VoiceIdsShared](#schemavoiceidsshared) \| string \| object|true|The voice to use when generating the audio. Supported built-in voices are `alloy`, `ash`, `ballad`, `coral`, `echo`, `fable`, `onyx`, `nova`, `sage`, `shimmer`, `verse`, `marin`, and `cedar`. You may also provide a custom voice object with an `id`, for example `{ "id": "voice_1234" }`. Previews of the voices are available in the [Text to speech guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text-to-speech#voice-options). Custom voices must be created from audio samples. Voices created from text prompts are supported only in Live.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[VoiceIdsShared](#schemavoiceidsshared) \| string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[VoiceIdsShared](#schemavoiceidsshared)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Custom voice reference.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The custom voice ID, e.g. `voice_1234`.|
|» response_format|body|string|false|The format to audio in. Supported formats are `mp3`, `opus`, `aac`, `flac`, `wav`, and `pcm`.|
|» speed|body|number|false|The speed of the generated audio. Select a value from `0.25` to `4.0`. `1.0` is the default.|
|» stream_format|body|string|false|The format to stream the audio in. Supported formats are `sse` and `audio`. `sse` is not supported for `tts-1` or `tts-1-hd`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|tts-1|
|» » *anyOf*|tts-1-hd|
|» » *anyOf*|gpt-4o-mini-tts|
|» » *anyOf*|gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15|
|» » *anyOf*|fable|
|» » *anyOf*|onyx|
|» » *anyOf*|nova|
|» response_format|mp3|
|» response_format|opus|
|» response_format|aac|
|» response_format|flac|
|» response_format|wav|
|» response_format|pcm|
|» stream_format|sse|
|» stream_format|audio|

## Create transcription

<a id="opIdcreateTranscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'model=gpt-4o-transcribe' \
  -F 'language=string' \
  -F 'languages=["string"]' \
  -F 'keywords=["string"]' \
  -F 'prompt=string' \
  -F 'response_format=json' \
  -F 'temperature=0' \
  -F 'include=["logprobs"]' \
  -F 'timestamp_granularities=["segment"]' \
  -F 'stream=false' \
  -F 'chunking_strategy=auto' \
  -F 'known_speaker_names=["string"]' \
  -F 'known_speaker_references=["string"]'
```

`POST /audio/transcriptions`

Transcribes audio into the input language.

Returns a transcription object in `json`, `diarized_json`, or `verbose_json`
format, plain text in `text`, `srt`, or `vtt` format, or a stream of
transcript events. Supported formats depend on the model.


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
model: gpt-4o-transcribe
language: string
languages:
  - string
keywords:
  - string
prompt: string
response_format: json
temperature: 0
include:
  - logprobs
timestamp_granularities:
  - segment
stream: false
chunking_strategy: auto
known_speaker_names:
  - string
known_speaker_references:
  - string
```

<h3 id="create-transcription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateTranscriptionRequest](#schemacreatetranscriptionrequest)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The audio file object (not file name) to transcribe, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm.<br>The request must include enough format metadata for the file to be identified. We recommend an extension-bearing filename and an appropriate content type.<br>|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to use. The options are `gpt-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`, `whisper-1` (which is powered by our open source Whisper V2 model), and `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» language|body|string|false|The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) (e.g. `en`) format will improve accuracy and latency.<br>|
|» languages|body|[string]|false|Possible languages of the input audio, in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) format. Supported by `gpt-transcribe`.<br>|
|» keywords|body|[string]|false|Words or phrases to guide transcription of the input audio. Supported by `gpt-transcribe`.<br>|
|» prompt|body|string|false|An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The [prompt](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text#prompting) should match the audio language. This field is not supported when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|» response_format|body|[AudioResponseFormat](#schemaaudioresponseformat)|false|The format of the output, in one of these options: `json`, `text`, `srt`, `verbose_json`, `vtt`, or `diarized_json`. For `gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, the only supported format is `json`. For `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`, the supported formats are `json`, `text`, and `diarized_json`, with `diarized_json` required to receive speaker annotations.<br>|
|» temperature|body|number|false|The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use [log probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability) to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.<br>|
|» include|body|[[TranscriptionInclude](#schematranscriptioninclude)]|false|Additional information to include in the transcription response.<br>`logprobs` will return the log probabilities of the tokens in the<br>response to understand the model's confidence in the transcription.<br>`logprobs` only works with response_format set to `json` and only with<br>the models `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`. This field is not supported when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|» timestamp_granularities|body|[string]|false|The timestamp granularities to populate for this transcription. `response_format` must be set `verbose_json` to use timestamp granularities. Either or both of these options are supported: `word`, or `segment`. Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.<br>This option is not available for `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|» stream|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|If set to true, the model response data will be streamed to the client<br>as it is generated using [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events#Event_stream_format).<br>See the [Streaming section of the Speech-to-Text guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text?lang=curl#streaming)<br>for more information.<br><br>Note: Streaming is not supported for the `whisper-1` model and will be ignored.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» chunking_strategy|body|string \| [VadConfig](#schemavadconfig) \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string \| [VadConfig](#schemavadconfig)|false|Controls how the audio is cut into chunks. When set to `"auto"`, the server first normalizes loudness and then uses voice activity detection (VAD) to choose boundaries. `server_vad` object can be provided to tweak VAD detection parameters manually. If unset, the audio is transcribed as a single block. Required when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` for inputs longer than 30 seconds. |
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|Automatically set chunking parameters based on the audio. Must be set to `"auto"`.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[VadConfig](#schemavadconfig)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» known_speaker_names|body|[string]|false|Optional list of speaker names that correspond to the audio samples provided in `known_speaker_references[]`. Each entry should be a short identifier (for example `customer` or `agent`). Up to 4 speakers are supported.<br>|
|» known_speaker_references|body|[string]|false|Optional list of audio samples (as [data URLs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/Data_URLs)) that contain known speaker references matching `known_speaker_names[]`. Each sample must be between 2 and 10 seconds, and can use any of the same input audio formats supported by `file`.<br>|

`POST /audio/translations`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Translates audio into English.

This endpoint supports only `whisper-1`. The endpoint and model are deprecated
and scheduled to shut down on February 26, 2027. Migrate to
`/v1/realtime/translations`, which requires a separate integration. See the
[deprecation schedule](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
for details.


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
model: whisper-1
prompt: string
response_format: json
temperature: 0
```

<h3 id="create-translation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateTranslationRequest](#schemacreatetranslationrequest)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The audio file object (not file name) translate, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm. The request must include enough format metadata for the file to be identified. We recommend an extension-bearing filename and an appropriate content type.<br>|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to use. Only `whisper-1` (which is powered by our open source Whisper V2 model) is currently available.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» prompt|body|string|false|An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The [prompt](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text#prompting) should be in English.<br>|
|» response_format|body|string|false|The format of the output, in one of these options: `json`, `text`, `srt`, `verbose_json`, or `vtt`.<br>|
|» temperature|body|number|false|The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use [log probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability) to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.<br>|

## Create voice

<a id="opIdcreateVoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/voices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "prompt",
    "name": "string",
    "prompt": "string",
    "script_hint": "string",
    "model": "auto"
  }'
```

`POST /audio/voices`

Creates a voice from a text prompt or from a consent recording and an audio sample.

For prompt-based creation, send `type: "prompt"` with a `name` and `prompt` as JSON or multipart form data. For creation from an audio sample, send `type: "audio_sample"` with a `name`, `audio_sample`, and `consent` recording ID as multipart form data. The type defaults to `audio_sample` when omitted.

Returns the saved voice's metadata. Voices created from text prompts are supported only in Live, not in Realtime or the speech endpoint. The response does not include preview audio.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "prompt",
  "name": "string",
  "prompt": "string",
  "script_hint": "string",
  "model": "auto"
}
```

<h3 id="create-voice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateVoicePromptRequest](#schemacreatevoicepromptrequest)|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Set to `prompt` to create a voice from a text description.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new voice.|
|» prompt|body|string|true|A description of the desired voice. Must not contain only whitespace.|
|» script_hint|body|string|false|Optional text for the voice to speak during creation. If omitted, a script is generated from the prompt. Must not be blank after trimming whitespace; scripts that are too short are rejected.|
|» model|body|string|false|The voice creation model to use. Defaults to `auto`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|prompt|
|» » *anyOf*|auto|
|» » *anyOf*|2026-10-08|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "audio.voice",
  "id": "string",
  "type": "audio_sample",
  "prompt": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "created_at": 0
}
```

`DELETE /audio/voices/{voice_id}`

Deletes a voice created from a text prompt or an audio sample.

Requires voice write permission and access to the voice's project. Access to voices created from recordings is limited to eligible customers. See the [custom voices guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-voices).

Deleting a voice does not delete its consent recording. Deleting an already deleted voice returns a 404 error.

`POST /chat/completions`

**Starting a new project?** We recommend trying [Responses](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses)
to take advantage of the latest OpenAI platform features. Compare
[Chat Completions with Responses](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses?api-mode=responses).

---

Creates a model response for the given chat conversation. Learn more in the
[text generation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text), [vision](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision),
and [audio](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/audio) guides.

Parameter support can differ depending on the model used to generate the
response, particularly for newer reasoning models. Parameters that are only
supported for reasoning models are noted below. For the current state of
unsupported parameters in reasoning models,
[refer to the reasoning guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning).

Returns a chat completion object, or a streamed sequence of chat completion
chunk objects if the request is streamed.

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The model is temporarily overloaded. Please retry your request after a brief delay.",
    "type": "service_unavailable_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "server_is_overloaded"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-chat-completion-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a Chat Completion object for a non-streaming request.<br><br>If `stream` is `true`, returns server-sent events (`text/event-stream`).<br>Successful chunk frames contain a JSON Chat Completion chunk matching<br>`CreateChatCompletionStreamResponse`. On normal completion, the final<br>frame is:<br><br>```text<br>data: [DONE]<br><br>```<br><br>The final frame ends with a blank line. `[DONE]` is literal text, not a<br>JSON chunk, and this frame has no `event: done` field.<br><br>If a failure occurs after streaming has started, a data frame may<br>contain a JSON object with an `error` field instead of a completion<br>chunk. The streaming schema describes successful JSON chunks, not<br>error frames or the completion marker. An interrupted stream may end<br>without the marker.<br>|[CreateChatCompletionResponse](#schemacreatechatcompletionresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid chat completion request or incompatible request parameters.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication failed because the API key is missing or revoked, or the client IP is not authorized.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Access to a personal API organization is blocked by the organization policy.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The requested model or a referenced resource was not found or is unavailable to this caller.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The request was rejected because a rate limit was exceeded. A slow_down error means traffic increased too quickly; reduce your request rate, then increase it gradually.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|The chat completion could not be processed due to an internal error.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The service is temporarily unavailable. A server_is_overloaded error means the requested model is temporarily overloaded; retry after a brief delay.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|429|Retry-After|integer||The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted.|
|503|Retry-After|integer||The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="openai-api-conversations">Conversations</h1>

Manage conversations and conversation items.

## List items

<a id="opIdlistConversationItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/conversations/conv_123/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/items`

List all items for a conversation with the given ID.

<h3 id="list-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|conversation_id|path|string|true|The ID of the conversation to list items for.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between<br>1 and 100, and the default is 20.<br>|
|order|query|string|false|The order to return the input items in. Default is `desc`.<br>- `asc`: Return the input items in ascending order.<br>- `desc`: Return the input items in descending order.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|An item ID to list items after, used in pagination.<br>|
|include|query|[[IncludeEnum](#schemaincludeenum)]|false|Specify additional output data to include in the model response. Currently supported values are:<br>- `web_search_call.action.sources`: Include the sources of the web search tool call.<br>- `code_interpreter_call.outputs`: Includes the outputs of python code execution in code interpreter tool call items.<br>- `computer_call_output.output.image_url`: Include image urls from the computer call output.<br>- `file_search_call.results`: Include the search results of the file search tool call.<br>- `message.input_image.image_url`: Include image urls from the input message.<br>- `message.output_text.logprobs`: Include logprobs with assistant messages.<br>- `reasoning.encrypted_content`: Includes an encrypted version of reasoning tokens in reasoning item outputs. This enables reasoning items to be used in multi-turn conversations when using the Responses API statelessly (like when the `store` parameter is set to `false`, or when an organization is enrolled in the zero data retention program).|

|include|computer_call_output.output.image_url|

<h1 id="openai-api-completions">Completions</h1>

Given a prompt, the model will return one or more predicted completions, and can also return the probabilities of alternative tokens at each position.

## Create completion

<a id="opIdcreateCompletion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "string",
    "prompt": "<|endoftext|>",
    "best_of": 1,
    "echo": false,
    "frequency_penalty": 0,
    "logit_bias": null,
    "logprobs": null,
    "max_tokens": 16,
    "n": 1,
    "presence_penalty": 0,
    "seed": 0,
    "stop": null,
    "stream": false,
    "stream_options": {
      "include_usage": true,
      "include_obfuscation": true
    },
    "suffix": "test.",
    "temperature": 1,
    "top_p": 1,
    "user": "user-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /completions`

Creates a completion for the provided prompt and parameters.

Returns a completion object, or a sequence of completion objects if the request is streamed.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "prompt": "<|endoftext|>",
  "best_of": 1,
  "echo": false,
  "frequency_penalty": 0,
  "logit_bias": null,
  "logprobs": null,
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "n": 1,
  "presence_penalty": 0,
  "seed": 0,
  "stop": null,
  "stream": false,
  "stream_options": {
    "include_usage": true,
    "include_obfuscation": true
  },
  "suffix": "test.",
  "temperature": 1,
  "top_p": 1,
  "user": "user-1234"
}
```

<h3 id="create-completion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateCompletionRequest](#schemacreatecompletionrequest)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to use. You can use the [List models](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/models/methods/list) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) for descriptions of them.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» prompt|body|string \| [string] \| [integer] \| [[integer]] \| null|true|The prompt(s) to generate completions for, encoded as a string, array of strings, array of tokens, or array of token arrays.<br><br>Note that <\|endoftext\|> is the document separator that the model sees during training, so if a prompt is not specified the model will generate as if from the beginning of a new document.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[integer]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[integer]]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» best_of|body|integer \| null|false|Generates `best_of` completions server-side and returns the "best" (the one with the highest log probability per token). Results cannot be streamed.<br><br>When used with `n`, `best_of` controls the number of candidate completions and `n` specifies how many to return – `best_of` must be greater than `n`.<br><br>**Note:** Because this parameter generates many completions, it can quickly consume your token quota. Use carefully and ensure that you have reasonable settings for `max_tokens` and `stop`.<br>|
|» echo|body|boolean \| null|false|Echo back the prompt in addition to the completion<br>|
|» frequency_penalty|body|number \| null|false|Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.<br><br>[See more information about frequency and presence penalties.](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text)<br>|
|» logit_bias|body|object \| null|false|Modify the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.<br><br>Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You can use this [tokenizer tool](https://platform.openai.com/tokenizer?view=bpe) to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically, the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling. The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100 should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.<br><br>As an example, you can pass `{"50256": -100}` to prevent the <\|endoftext\|> token from being generated.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|integer|false|none|
|» logprobs|body|integer \| null|false|Include the log probabilities on the `logprobs` most likely output tokens, as well the chosen tokens. For example, if `logprobs` is 5, the API will return a list of the 5 most likely tokens. The API will always return the `logprob` of the sampled token, so there may be up to `logprobs+1` elements in the response.<br><br>The maximum value for `logprobs` is 5.<br>|
|» max_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of [tokens](https://platform.openai.com/tokenizer) that can be generated in the completion.<br><br>The token count of your prompt plus `max_tokens` cannot exceed the model's context length. [Example Python code](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/how_to_count_tokens_with_tiktoken) for counting tokens.<br>|
|» n|body|integer \| null|false|How many completions to generate for each prompt.<br><br>**Note:** Because this parameter generates many completions, it can quickly consume your token quota. Use carefully and ensure that you have reasonable settings for `max_tokens` and `stop`.<br>|
|» presence_penalty|body|number \| null|false|Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.<br><br>[See more information about frequency and presence penalties.](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text)<br>|
|» seed|body|integer \| null(int64)|false|If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same `seed` and parameters should return the same result.<br><br>Determinism is not guaranteed, and you should refer to the `system_fingerprint` response parameter to monitor changes in the backend.<br>|
|» stop|body|[StopConfiguration](#schemastopconfiguration)|false|Not supported with latest reasoning models `o3` and `o4-mini`.<br><br>Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The<br>returned text will not contain the stop sequence.<br>|
|» stream|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to stream back partial progress. If set, tokens will be sent as data-only [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events#Event_stream_format) as they become available, with the stream terminated by a `data: [DONE]` message. [Example Python code](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/how_to_stream_completions).<br>|
|» stream_options|body|[ChatCompletionStreamOptions](#schemachatcompletionstreamoptions)|false|none|
|» suffix|body|string \| null|false|The suffix that comes after a completion of inserted text.<br><br>This parameter is only supported for `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`.<br>|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.<br><br>We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.<br>|
|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.<br><br>We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.<br>|
|» user|body|string|false|A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct|
|» » *anyOf*|davinci-002|
|» » *anyOf*|babbage-002|

<h1 id="openai-api-embeddings">Embeddings</h1>

Get a vector representation of a given input that can be easily consumed by machine learning models and algorithms.

## Create embeddings

<a id="opIdcreateEmbedding"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "input": "The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog",
    "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
    "encoding_format": "float",
    "dimensions": 1,
    "user": "user-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /embeddings`

Creates an embedding vector representing the input text.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "input": "The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog",
  "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "encoding_format": "float",
  "dimensions": 1,
  "user": "user-1234"
}
```

<h3 id="create-embeddings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateEmbeddingRequest](#schemacreateembeddingrequest)|true|none|
|» input|body|string \| [string] \| [integer] \| [[integer]]|true|Input text to embed, encoded as a string or array of tokens. To embed multiple inputs in a single request, pass an array of strings or array of token arrays. The input must not exceed the max input tokens for the model (8192 tokens for all embedding models), cannot be an empty string, and any array must be 2048 dimensions or less. [Example Python code](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/how_to_count_tokens_with_tiktoken) for counting tokens. In addition to the per-input token limit, all embedding models enforce a maximum of 300,000 tokens summed across all inputs in a single request.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|The string that will be turned into an embedding.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|The array of strings that will be turned into an embedding.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[integer]|false|The array of integers that will be turned into an embedding.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[integer]]|false|The array of arrays containing integers that will be turned into an embedding.|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to use. You can use the [List models](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/models/methods/list) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) for descriptions of them.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» encoding_format|body|string|false|The format to return the embeddings in. Can be either `float` or [`base64`](https://pypi.org/project/pybase64/).|
|» dimensions|body|integer|false|The number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have. Only supported in `text-embedding-3` and later models.<br>|
|» user|body|string|false|A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).<br>|

## Create eval

<a id="opIdcreateEval"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/evals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "data_source_config": {
      "type": "custom",
      "item_schema": "{\n  \"type\": \"object\",\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n    \"age\": {\"type\": \"integer\"}\n  },\n  \"required\": [\"name\", \"age\"]\n}\n",
      "include_sample_schema": false
    },
    "testing_criteria": [
      {
        "type": "label_model",
        "name": "string",
        "model": "string",
        "input": [
          {
            "role": "string",
            "content": "string"
          }
        ],
        "labels": [
          "string"
        ],
        "passing_labels": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /evals`

Create the structure of an evaluation that can be used to test a model's performance.
An evaluation is a set of testing criteria and the config for a data source, which dictates the schema of the data used in the evaluation. After creating an evaluation, you can run it on different models and model parameters. We support several types of graders and datasources.
For more information, see the [Evals guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evals).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "data_source_config": {
    "type": "custom",
    "item_schema": "{\n  \"type\": \"object\",\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n    \"age\": {\"type\": \"integer\"}\n  },\n  \"required\": [\"name\", \"age\"]\n}\n",
    "include_sample_schema": false
  },
  "testing_criteria": [
    {
      "type": "label_model",
      "name": "string",
      "model": "string",
      "input": [
        {
          "role": "string",
          "content": "string"
        }
      ],
      "labels": [
        "string"
      ],
      "passing_labels": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-eval-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateEvalRequest](#schemacreateevalrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the evaluation.|
|» metadata|body|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|
|» data_source_config|body|object|true|The configuration for the data source used for the evaluation runs. Dictates the schema of the data used in the evaluation.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CreateEvalCustomDataSourceConfig](#schemacreateevalcustomdatasourceconfig)|false|A CustomDataSourceConfig object that defines the schema for the data source used for the evaluation runs.<br>This schema is used to define the shape of the data that will be:<br>- Used to define your testing criteria and<br>- What data is required when creating a run<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CreateEvalLogsDataSourceConfig](#schemacreateevallogsdatasourceconfig)|false|A data source config which specifies the metadata property of your logs query.<br>This is usually metadata like `usecase=chatbot` or `prompt-version=v2`, etc.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CreateEvalStoredCompletionsDataSourceConfig](#schemacreateevalstoredcompletionsdatasourceconfig)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated in favor of LogsDataSourceConfig.<br>|
|» testing_criteria|body|[[CreateEvalLabelModelGrader](#schemacreateevallabelmodelgrader) \| [EvalGraderStringCheck](#schemaevalgraderstringcheck) \| [EvalGraderTextSimilarity](#schemaevalgradertextsimilarity) \| [EvalGraderPython](#schemaevalgraderpython) \| [EvalGraderScoreModel](#schemaevalgraderscoremodel)]|true|A list of graders for all eval runs in this group. Graders can reference variables in the data source using double curly braces notation, like `{{item.variable_name}}`. To reference the model's output, use the `sample` namespace (ie, `{{sample.output_text}}`).|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CreateEvalLabelModelGrader](#schemacreateevallabelmodelgrader)|false|A LabelModelGrader object which uses a model to assign labels to each item<br>in the evaluation.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[EvalGraderStringCheck](#schemaevalgraderstringcheck)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[EvalGraderTextSimilarity](#schemaevalgradertextsimilarity)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[EvalGraderPython](#schemaevalgraderpython)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[EvalGraderScoreModel](#schemaevalgraderscoremodel)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

<a id="opIdcreateEvalRun"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/evals/string/runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "metadata": {

      "property2": "string"
    },
    "data_source": {
      "type": "jsonl",
      "source": {

        "content": [
          {
            "item": {},
            "sample": {}
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /evals/{eval_id}/runs`

Kicks off a new run for a given evaluation, specifying the data source, and what model configuration to use to test. The datasource will be validated against the schema specified in the config of the evaluation.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "data_source": {
    "type": "jsonl",
    "source": {
      "type": "file_content",
      "content": [
        {
          "item": {},
          "sample": {}
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-eval-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|eval_id|path|string|true|The ID of the evaluation to create a run for.|
|body|body|[CreateEvalRunRequest](#schemacreateevalrunrequest)|true|none|

<h1 id="openai-api-fine-tuning">Fine-tuning</h1>

Manage fine-tuning jobs to tailor a model to your specific training data.

## Run grader

<a id="opIdrunGrader"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/fine_tuning/alpha/graders/run \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "grader": {
      "type": "string_check",
      "name": "string",
      "input": "string",
      "reference": "string",
      "operation": "eq"
    },
    "item": {},
    "model_sample": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /fine_tuning/alpha/graders/run`

Run a grader.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "grader": {
    "type": "string_check",
    "name": "string",
    "input": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "operation": "eq"
  },
  "item": {},
  "model_sample": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="run-grader-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RunGraderRequest](#schemarungraderrequest)|true|none|
|» grader|body|object|true|The grader used for the fine-tuning job.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[GraderStringCheck](#schemagraderstringcheck)|false|A StringCheckGrader object that performs a string comparison between input and reference using a specified operation.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[GraderTextSimilarity](#schemagradertextsimilarity)|false|A TextSimilarityGrader object which grades text based on similarity metrics.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[GraderPython](#schemagraderpython)|false|A PythonGrader object that runs a python script on the input.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[GraderScoreModel](#schemagraderscoremodel)|false|A ScoreModelGrader object that uses a model to assign a score to the input.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[GraderMulti](#schemagradermulti)|false|A MultiGrader object combines the output of multiple graders to produce a single score.|
|» item|body|object|false|The dataset item provided to the grader. This will be used to populate<br>the `item` namespace. See [the guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/graders) for more details.<br>|
|» model_sample|body|string|true|The model sample to be evaluated. This value will be used to populate<br>the `sample` namespace. See [the guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/graders) for more details.<br>The `output_json` variable will be populated if the model sample is a<br>valid JSON string.<br>|

Additionally, you must upload your file with the purpose `fine-tune`.<br><br>The contents of the file should differ depending on if the model uses the [chat](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/supervised-fine-tuning#formatting-your-data), [completions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/supervised-fine-tuning#formatting-your-data) format, or if the fine-tuning method uses the [preference](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/direct-preference-optimization) format.<br><br>See the [fine-tuning guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-optimization) for more details.<br>|

|» » batch_size|body|string \| integer|false|Number of examples in each batch. A larger batch size means that model parameters<br>are updated less frequently, but with lower variance.<br>|

|» » learning_rate_multiplier|body|string \| number|false|Scaling factor for the learning rate. A smaller learning rate may be useful to avoid<br>overfitting.<br>|

|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » n_epochs|body|string \| integer|false|The number of epochs to train the model for. An epoch refers to one full cycle<br>through the training dataset.<br>|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» suffix|body|string \| null|false|A string of up to 64 characters that will be added to your fine-tuned model name.<br><br>For example, a `suffix` of "custom-model-name" would produce a model name like `ft:gpt-4o-mini:openai:custom-model-name:7p4lURel`.<br>|
|» validation_file|body|string \| null|false|The ID of an uploaded file that contains validation data.<br><br>If you provide this file, the data is used to generate validation<br>metrics periodically during fine-tuning. These metrics can be viewed in<br>the fine-tuning results file.<br>The same data should not be present in both train and validation files.<br><br>Your dataset must be formatted as a JSONL file. You must upload your file with the purpose `fine-tune`.<br><br>See the [fine-tuning guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-optimization) for more details.<br>|

|» » type|body|string|true|The type of integration to enable. Currently, only "wandb" (Weights and Biases) is supported.<br>|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » wandb|body|object|true|The settings for your integration with Weights and Biases. This payload specifies the project that<br>metrics will be sent to. Optionally, you can set an explicit display name for your run, add tags<br>to your run, and set a default entity (team, username, etc) to be associated with your run.<br>|
|» » » project|body|string|true|The name of the project that the new run will be created under.<br>|
|» » » name|body|string \| null|false|A display name to set for the run. If not set, we will use the Job ID as the name.<br>|
|» » » entity|body|string \| null|false|The entity to use for the run. This allows you to set the team or username of the WandB user that you would<br>like associated with the run. If not set, the default entity for the registered WandB API key is used.<br>|
|» » » tags|body|[string]|false|A list of tags to be attached to the newly created run. These tags are passed through directly to WandB. Some<br>default tags are generated by OpenAI: "openai/finetune", "openai/{base-model}", "openai/{ftjob-abcdef}".<br>|

## Create batch

<a id="opIdcreateBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/batches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "input_file_id": "string",
    "endpoint": "/v1/responses",
    "completion_window": "24h",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "output_expires_after": {
      "anchor": "created_at",
      "seconds": 3600
    }
  }'
```

`POST /batches`

Creates and executes a batch from an uploaded file of requests

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "input_file_id": "string",
  "endpoint": "/v1/responses",
  "completion_window": "24h",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "output_expires_after": {
    "anchor": "created_at",
    "seconds": 3600
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-batch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateBatchRequest](#schemacreatebatchrequest)|true|none|
|» input_file_id|body|string|true|The ID of an uploaded file that contains requests for the new batch.<br><br>See [upload file](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/create) for how to upload a file.<br><br>Your input file must be formatted as a [JSONL file](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch#1-prepare-your-batch-file), and must be uploaded with the purpose `batch`. The file can contain up to 50,000 requests, and can be up to 200 MB in size.<br>|
|» endpoint|body|string|true|The endpoint to be used for all requests in the batch. Currently `/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/moderations`, `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`, and `/v1/videos` are supported. Note that `/v1/embeddings` batches are also restricted to a maximum of 50,000 embedding inputs across all requests in the batch.|
|» completion_window|body|string|true|The time frame within which the batch should be processed. Currently only `24h` is supported.|
|» metadata|body|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|
|» output_expires_after|body|[BatchFileExpirationAfter](#schemabatchfileexpirationafter)|false|The expiration policy for the output and/or error file that are generated for a batch.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» endpoint|/v1/responses|
|» endpoint|/v1/chat/completions|
|» endpoint|/v1/embeddings|
|» endpoint|/v1/completions|
|» endpoint|/v1/moderations|
|» endpoint|/v1/images/generations|
|» endpoint|/v1/images/edits|
|» endpoint|/v1/videos|
|» completion_window|24h|

> Example responses

## Cancel batch

<a id="opIdcancelBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/batches/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /batches/{batch_id}/cancel`

Cancels an in-progress batch. The batch will be in status `cancelling` for up to 10 minutes, before changing to `cancelled`, where it will have partial results (if any) available in the output file.

<h3 id="cancel-batch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batch_id|path|string|true|The ID of the batch to cancel.|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": "string",
  "object": "batch",
  "endpoint": "string",

  "errors": {
    "object": "string",
    "data": [
      {
        "code": "string",

        "param": "string",
```

<h1 id="openai-api-files">Files</h1>

Files are used to upload documents that can be used with features like Assistants and Fine-tuning.

## List files

<a id="opIdlistFiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/files \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files`

Returns a list of files.

<h3 id="list-files-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|purpose|query|string|false|Only return files with the given purpose.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 10,000, and the default is 10,000.<br>|
|order|query|string|false|Sort order by the `created_at` timestamp of the objects. `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include after=obj_foo in order to fetch the next page of the list.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

## Upload file

<a id="opIdcreateFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'purpose=assistants' \
  -F 'expires_after={"anchor":"created_at","seconds":3600}'
```

`POST /files`

Upload a file that can be used across various endpoints. Individual files
can be up to 512 MB, and each project can store up to 2.5 TB of files in
total. There is no organization-wide storage limit. Uploads to this
endpoint are rate-limited to 1,000 requests per minute per authenticated
user.

- The Assistants API supports files up to 2 million tokens and of specific
  file types. See the [Assistants Tools guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools) for
  details.
- The Fine-tuning API only supports `.jsonl` files. The input also has
  certain required formats for fine-tuning
  [chat](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/supervised-fine-tuning#formatting-your-data) or
  [completions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/supervised-fine-tuning#formatting-your-data) models.
- The Batch API only supports `.jsonl` files up to 200 MB in size. The input
  also has a specific required
  [format](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch#1-prepare-your-batch-file).
- For Retrieval or `file_search` ingestion, upload files here first. If
  you need to attach multiple uploaded files to the same vector store, use
  [`/vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/file_batches`](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/vector_stores/subresources/file_batches/methods/create)
  instead of attaching them one by one. Vector store attachment has separate
  limits from file upload, including 2,000 attached files per minute per
  organization.

Please [contact us](https://help.openai.com/) if you need to increase these
storage limits.


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
purpose: assistants
expires_after:
  anchor: created_at
  seconds: 3600
```

<h3 id="upload-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateFileRequest](#schemacreatefilerequest)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The File object (not file name) to be uploaded.<br>|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The intended purpose of the uploaded file. One of:<br>- `assistants`: Used in the Assistants API<br>- `batch`: Used in the Batch API<br>- `fine-tune`: Used for fine-tuning<br>- `vision`: Images used for vision fine-tuning<br>- `user_data`: Flexible file type for any purpose<br>- `evals`: Used for eval data sets<br>|
|» expires_after|body|[FileExpirationAfter](#schemafileexpirationafter)|false|The expiration policy for a file. By default, files with `purpose=batch` expire after 30 days and all other files are persisted until they are manually deleted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» purpose|assistants|
|» purpose|batch|
|» purpose|fine-tune|
|» purpose|vision|
|» purpose|user_data|
|» purpose|evals|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "id": "string",
  "bytes": 0,
  "created_at": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "filename": "string",
  "object": "file",
  "purpose": "assistants",
  "status": "uploaded",
  "status_details": "string"
}
```

```json
      }

```

<h1 id="openai-api-uploads">Uploads</h1>

Use Uploads to upload large files in multiple parts.

## Create upload

<a id="opIdcreateUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/uploads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "filename": "string",
    "purpose": "assistants",
    "bytes": 0,
    "mime_type": "string",
    "expires_after": {
      "anchor": "created_at",
      "seconds": 3600
    }
  }'
```

`POST /uploads`

Creates an intermediate [Upload](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads) object
that you can add [Parts](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads/subresources/parts) to.
Currently, an Upload can accept at most 8 GB in total and expires after an
hour after you create it.

Once you complete the Upload, we will create a
[File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files) object that contains all the parts
you uploaded. This File is usable in the rest of our platform as a regular
File object.

For certain `purpose` values, the correct `mime_type` must be specified.
Please refer to documentation for the
[supported MIME types for your use case](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search#supported-files).

For guidance on the proper filename extensions for each purpose, please
follow the documentation on [creating a
File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/create).

Returns the Upload object with status `pending`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filename": "string",
  "purpose": "assistants",
  "bytes": 0,
  "mime_type": "string",
  "expires_after": {
    "anchor": "created_at",
    "seconds": 3600
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateUploadRequest](#schemacreateuploadrequest)|true|none|
|» filename|body|string|true|The name of the file to upload.<br>|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The intended purpose of the uploaded file.<br><br>See the [documentation on File<br>purposes](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/create#%28resource%29%20files%20%3E%20%28method%29%20create%20%3E%20%28params%29%200%20%3E%20%28param%29%20purpose%20%3E%20%28schema%29).<br>|
|» bytes|body|integer|true|The number of bytes in the file you are uploading.<br>|
|» mime_type|body|string|true|The MIME type of the file.<br><br><br>This must fall within the supported MIME types for your file purpose. See<br>the supported MIME types for assistants and vision.<br>|
|» expires_after|body|[FileExpirationAfter](#schemafileexpirationafter)|false|The expiration policy for a file. By default, files with `purpose=batch` expire after 30 days and all other files are persisted until they are manually deleted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» purpose|assistants|
|» purpose|batch|
|» purpose|fine-tune|
|» purpose|vision|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "created_at": 0,
  "filename": "string",
  "bytes": 0,
  "purpose": "string",
  "status": "pending",
  "expires_at": 0,
  "object": "upload",
  "file": {
    "id": "string",
    "bytes": 0,
    "created_at": 0,
    "expires_at": 0,
    "filename": "string",
    "object": "file",
    "purpose": "assistants",
    "status": "uploaded",
    "status_details": "string"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "misalignment": {
      "review_target": "string",
      "error_type": "string",
      "detailed_explanation": "string",
      "steer": {
        "message": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "misalignment": {

      }
```

## Complete upload

<a id="opIdcompleteUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/uploads/upload_abc123/complete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "part_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "md5": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /uploads/{upload_id}/complete`

Completes the [Upload](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads).

Within the returned Upload object, there is a nested [File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files) object that is ready to use in the rest of the platform.

You can specify the order of the Parts by passing in an ordered list of the Part IDs.

The number of bytes uploaded upon completion must match the number of bytes initially specified when creating the Upload object. No Parts may be added after an Upload is completed.
Returns the Upload object with status `completed`, including an additional `file` property containing the created usable File object.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "part_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "md5": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="complete-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Upload.<br>|
|body|body|[CompleteUploadRequest](#schemacompleteuploadrequest)|true|none|
|» part_ids|body|[string]|true|The ordered list of Part IDs.<br>|
|» md5|body|string|false|The optional md5 checksum for the file contents to verify if the bytes uploaded matches what you expect.<br>|

> Example responses

## Add upload part

<a id="opIdaddUploadPart"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/uploads/upload_abc123/parts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'data=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /uploads/{upload_id}/parts`

Adds a [Part](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads/subresources/parts) to an [Upload](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads) object. A Part represents a chunk of bytes from the file you are trying to upload.

Each Part can be at most 64 MB, and you can add Parts until you hit the Upload maximum of 8 GB.

It is possible to add multiple Parts in parallel. You can decide the intended order of the Parts when you [complete the Upload](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads/methods/complete).


> Body parameter

```yaml
data: string
```

<h3 id="add-upload-part-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Upload.<br>|
|body|body|[AddUploadPartRequest](#schemaadduploadpartrequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|string(binary)|true|The chunk of bytes for this Part.<br>|

<h1 id="openai-api-images">Images</h1>

Given a prompt and/or an input image, the model will generate a new image.

## Create image edit

<a id="opIdcreateImageEdit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-1.5",
    "prompt": "Add a watercolor effect to this image",
    "images": [
      {
        "image_url": "https://example.com/source-image.png"
      }
    ],
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "quality": "high"
  }'
```

`POST /images/edits`

Creates an edited or extended image given one or more source images and a prompt. This endpoint supports GPT Image models.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-image-1.5",
  "prompt": "Add a watercolor effect to this image",
  "images": [
    {
      "image_url": "https://example.com/source-image.png"
    }
  ],
  "size": "1024x1024",
  "quality": "high"
}
```

## Create image

<a id="opIdcreateImage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "A cute baby sea otter",
    "model": "gpt-image-2.5-flare",
    "n": 1,
    "quality": "medium",
    "response_format": "url",
    "output_format": "png",
    "output_compression": 100,
    "stream": false,
    "partial_images": 1,
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "moderation": "low",
    "background": "transparent",
    "style": "vivid",
    "safety_identifier": "user-1234",
    "user": "user-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /images/generations`

Creates an image given a prompt using a GPT Image model. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "prompt": "A cute baby sea otter",
  "model": "gpt-image-2.5-flare",
  "n": 1,
  "quality": "medium",
  "response_format": "url",
  "output_format": "png",
  "output_compression": 100,
  "stream": false,
  "partial_images": 1,
  "size": "1024x1024",
  "moderation": "low",
  "background": "transparent",
  "style": "vivid",
  "safety_identifier": "user-1234",
  "user": "user-1234"
}
```

Specify a model explicitly.<br>Supported models include `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-2`,<br>`gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,<br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`,<br>`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, and `chatgpt-image-latest`.<br><br>`gpt-image-1` was shut down on October 23, 2026. |» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

## Create image variation

<a id="opIdcreateImageVariation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/variations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'image=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'model=dall-e-2' \
  -F 'n=1' \
  -F 'response_format=url' \
  -F 'size=1024x1024' \
  -F 'user=user-1234'
```

`POST /images/variations`

<aside class="warning">

<h1 id="openai-api-moderations">Moderations</h1>

Given text and/or image inputs, classifies if those inputs are potentially harmful.

## Create moderation

<a id="opIdcreateModeration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/moderations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "input": "...text to classify goes here...",
    "model": "omni-moderation-2024-09-26"
  }'
```

`POST /moderations`

Classifies if text and/or image inputs are potentially harmful. Learn
more in the [moderation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/moderation).


> Body parameter

```json
  "input": "...text to classify goes here...",
  "model": "omni-moderation-2024-09-26"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreateModerationResponse](#schemacreatemoderationresponse)|

|403|Forbidden|Access to the requested moderation model was denied.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

|503|Service Unavailable|The service is temporarily unavailable. A server_is_overloaded error means the requested model is temporarily overloaded; retry after a brief delay.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

|503|Retry-After|integer||The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted.|
