<h1 id="openai-api-responses">Responses</h1>

Create and manage model responses.

## Create a model response

<a id="opIdcreateResponse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "top_logprobs": 0,
    "temperature": 1,
    "top_p": 1,
    "user": "user-1234",
    "safety_identifier": "safety-identifier-1234",
    "prompt_cache_key": "prompt-cache-key-1234",
    "prompt_cache_retention": "in_memory",
    "prompt_cache_options": {
      "ttl": "30m",
      "mode": "implicit",
      "prewarm": true,
      "comparison_response_id": "resp_123"
    },
    "previous_response_id": "string",
    "model": "gpt-6-astra",
    "background": false,
    "max_tool_calls": 0,
    "text": {
      "format": {
        "type": "text"
      },
      "verbosity": "medium"
    },
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "async": true,
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {
          "property1": null,
          "property2": null
        },
        "output_schema": {
          "property1": null,
          "property2": null
        },
        "strict": true,
        "defer_loading": true,
        "allowed_callers": [
          "direct"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "none",
    "prompt": {
      "id": "string",
      "version": "string",
      "variables": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    },
    "access_programs": {
      "cyber": "standard"
    },
    "service_tier": "auto",
    "truncation": "disabled",
    "reasoning": {
      "mode": "string",
      "effort": "medium",
      "summary": "auto",
      "context": "auto",
      "generate_summary": "auto"
    },
    "input": "string",
    "include": [
      "file_search_call.results"
    ],
    "parallel_tool_calls": true,
    "store": true,
    "instructions": "string",
    "moderation": {
      "model": "string",
      "policy": {
        "input": {
          "mode": "score"
        },
        "output": {
          "mode": "score"
        }
      }
    },
    "stream": false,
    "stream_options": {
      "include_obfuscation": true
    },
    "conversation": null,
    "context_management": [
      {
        "type": "compaction",
        "compact_threshold": 1000
      }
    ],
    "max_output_tokens": 16
  }'
```

`POST /responses`

Creates a model response. Provide [text](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text) or
[image](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision) inputs to generate [text](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text)
or [JSON](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs) outputs. Have the model call
your own [custom code](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) or use built-in
[tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools) like [web search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search)
or [file search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search) to use your own data
as input for the model's response.

|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling,<br>where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability<br>mass. `GET /responses/{response_id}`

|include_obfuscation|query|boolean|false|When true, stream obfuscation will be enabled. Stream obfuscation adds<br>random characters to an `obfuscation` field on streaming delta events<br>to normalize payload sizes as a mitigation to certain side-channel<br>attacks. These obfuscation fields are included by default, but add a<br>small amount of overhead to the data stream. You can set<br>`include_obfuscation` to false to optimize for bandwidth if you trust<br>the network links between your application and the OpenAI API.<br>|

`GET /responses/{response_id}/input_items`

|include|query|[[IncludeEnum](#schemaincludeenum)]|false|Additional fields to include in the response. See the `include`<br>parameter for Response creation above for more information.<br>|

`POST /responses/compact`

Compact a conversation. Returns a compacted response object.

Learn when and how to compact long-running conversations in the [conversation state guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state#managing-the-context-window). For ZDR-compatible compaction details, see [Compaction (advanced)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state#compaction-advanced).

> Body parameter

```json

  "model": "gpt-6-astra",
  "input": "string",
  "previous_response_id": "resp_123",
  "instructions": "string",
  "prompt_cache_key": "string",
  "prompt_cache_retention": "in_memory",
  "prompt_cache_options": {
    "ttl": "30m",
    "mode": "implicit"
  },
  "service_tier": "auto"
}

## Compact conversation

<a id="opIdbeta_Compactconversation"></a>

curl 'https://api.openai.com/v1/responses/compact?beta=true' \

`POST /responses/compact?beta=true`

Compact a conversation. Returns a compacted response object.

Learn when and how to compact long-running conversations in the [conversation state guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state#managing-the-context-window). For ZDR-compatible compaction details, see [Compaction (advanced)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state#compaction-advanced).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-6-astra",
  "input": "string",
  "previous_response_id": "resp_123",
  "instructions": "string",
  "prompt_cache_key": "string",
  "prompt_cache_retention": "in_memory",
  "prompt_cache_options": {
    "ttl": "30m",
    "mode": "implicit"
  },
  "service_tier": "auto"
}
```

`GET /responses/{response_id}/input_items?beta=true`

<h1 id="openai-api-audit-logs">Audit Logs</h1>

List user actions and configuration changes within this organization.

## List audit logs

<a id="opIdlist-audit-logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/audit_logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/audit_logs`

List user actions and configuration changes within this organization.

<h3 id="list-audit-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|effective_at|query|object|false|Return only events whose `effective_at` (Unix seconds) is in this range.|
|project_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Return only events for these projects.|
|event_types[]|query|[[AuditLogEventType](#schemaauditlogeventtype)]|false|Return only events with a `type` in one of these values. For example, `project.created`. For all options, see the documentation for the [audit log object](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/admin/subresources/organization/subresources/audit_logs).|
|actor_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Return only events performed by these actors. Can be a user ID, a service account ID, or an api key tracking ID.|
|actor_emails[]|query|[string]|false|Return only events performed by users with these emails.|
|resource_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Return only events performed on these targets. For example, a project ID updated. For ChatGPT connector role events, use the workspace connector resource ID shown in `details.id`, such as `<workspace_id>__<connector_id>`.|
|tenant_only|query|boolean|false|Return only tenant-scoped events associated with this organization. Required for tenant-scoped events such as `role.bound_to_resource` and `role.unbound_from_resource`. When `true`, all supplied event types must be tenant-scoped.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 20.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include after=obj_foo in order to fetch the next page of the list.<br>|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include before=obj_foo in order to fetch the previous page of the list.<br>|

|» » *oneOf*|body|[InlineSkillParam](#schemainlineskillparam)|false|none|
|» memory_limit|body|string|false|Optional memory limit for the container. Defaults to "1g".|
|» network_policy|body|[ContainerNetworkPolicyDisabledParam](#schemacontainernetworkpolicydisabledparam) \| [ContainerNetworkPolicyAllowlistParam](#schemacontainernetworkpolicyallowlistparam)|false|Network access policy for the container.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ContainerNetworkPolicyDisabledParam](#schemacontainernetworkpolicydisabledparam)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ContainerNetworkPolicyAllowlistParam](#schemacontainernetworkpolicyallowlistparam)|false|none|

## Decisions

<a id="opIdOrganizationDecisionsusage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/usage/decisions?start_time=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/usage/decisions`

Get Decisions API usage details for the organization.

<h3 id="decisions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|true|Start time (Unix seconds) of the query time range, inclusive.|
|end_time|query|integer \| null|false|End time (Unix seconds) of the query time range, exclusive.|
|bucket_width|query|[DecisionsUsageBucketWidth](#schemadecisionsusagebucketwidth) \| null|false|Width of each time bucket in response. Currently `1m`, `1h` and `1d` are supported, default to `1d`.|
|limit|query|integer \| null|false|Specifies the number of buckets to return.<br>- `bucket_width=1d`: default: 7, max: 31<br>- `bucket_width=1h`: default: 24, max: 168<br>- `bucket_width=1m`: default: 60, max: 1440|
|page|query|string \| null|false|A cursor for use in pagination. Corresponding to the `next_page` field from the previous response.|
|project_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Return only usage for these projects.|
|group_by|query|[[DecisionsUsageGroupBy](#schemadecisionsusagegroupby)] \| null|false|Group the usage data by the specified fields. Support fields include `project_id`, `user_id`, `api_key_id`, `model`, `batch`, `service_tier`, `api_source` or any combination of them. When grouped by `api_source`, results use `agents_api` for attributed Agents API activity and `unlabeled` for all other activity. Without source grouping, `api_source` is null.|
|user_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Return only usage for these users.|
|api_key_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Return only usage for these API keys.|
|models|query|[string] \| null|false|Return only usage for these models.|
|batch|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, return batch jobs only. If `false`, return non-batch jobs only. By default, return both.|

        {

## Create content provenance check

<a id="opIdCreatecontentprovenancecheck"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/content_provenance_checks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /content_provenance_checks`

Check whether an image or audio file contains known OpenAI provenance signals. [Learn more about content provenance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/content-provenance).

If `not_detected`, it means the tool did not find supported signals in the uploaded file. The content could still have been generated by OpenAI if the metadata was stripped or has evidence of tampering, the watermark was degraded, it comes from a legacy generation model, or it was created before provenance signals were available. Content could also still be AI-generated by another company's model, which the tool currently does not detect.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="create-content-provenance-check-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateContentProvenanceBody](#schemacreatecontentprovenancebody)|false|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The image or audio file to check for supported OpenAI provenance signals.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "content_provenance_check",
  "created_at": 0,
  "results": [
    {
      "type": "c2pa",
      "outcome": "detected",
      "validation_state": "trusted",
      "issuer": "string",
      "model": "string",
      "generated_at": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

      "detailed_explanation": "string",
      "steer": {
        "message": "string"
      }

}

{
  "error": {

## Create a ChatKit session

<h1 id="openai-api-live">Live</h1>

## Create session

<a id="opIdcreate-live"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/live/sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "session": {
      "model": "gpt-live-1",
      "instructions": "string",
      "audio": {
        "output": {
          "voice": "string"
        }
      },
      "delegation": {
        "acknowledgement_delay_ms": 0,
        "type": "client"
      },
      "triggers": [
        {
          "type": "decisions",
          "event_type": "session.input_transcript.delta",
          "decisions": {
            "questions": [
              {
                "type": "choice",
                "name": "string",
                "instructions": "string",
                "choices": [
                  {
                    "value": "string",
                    "description": "string"
                  },
                  {
                    "value": "string",
                    "description": "string"
                  }
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      ],
      "store": true,
      "input": [
        {
          "id": "string",
          "type": "message",
          "status": "incomplete",
          "role": "developer",
          "content": [
            {
              "type": "input_text",
              "text": "string"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "client": {
        "data_channel": {
          "allowed_client_events": "all",
          "allowed_server_events": "all"
        }
      }
    },
    "transport": {
      "type": "webrtc",
      "sdp": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /live/sessions`

Create a Live WebRTC session or place an outbound SIP call. Start with the
[Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) for session configuration
and [Telephony and SIP](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-sip?api=live#place-an-outbound-call)
for trunk setup and call monitoring.

Set transport.type to `webrtc` and supply an SDP offer, or set it to `sip`
and supply an E.164 destination and trunk credentials. Outbound SIP calling
must be enabled for your organization.
Ringing is limited to 3 minutes and connected calls to 2 hours; these limits
are not configurable in the request.

Returns `201 Created` after session initialization. WebRTC responses include an
SDP answer. SIP responses do not wait for the callee to answer. Attach a
sideband connection using session.id to monitor SIP call progress.

Each SIP request creates a new call. If a request times out or the connection
fails, retry with caution: the original request may have succeeded, and a
retry can place another call.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "session": {
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "instructions": "string",
    "audio": {
      "output": {

## Costs

<a id="opIdusage-costs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/costs?start_time=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/costs`

Get costs details for the organization.

<h3 id="costs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|true|Start time (Unix seconds) of the query time range, inclusive.|
|end_time|query|integer|false|End time (Unix seconds) of the query time range, exclusive.|
|bucket_width|query|string|false|Width of each time bucket in response. Currently only `1d` is supported, default to `1d`.|
|project_ids|query|[string]|false|Return only costs for these projects.|
|api_key_ids|query|[string]|false|Return only costs for these API keys.|
|line_items|query|[string]|false|Return only costs for these exact line item names. Each value must match the complete `line_item` value, for example `gpt-6-astra, input_tokens`.|
|group_by|query|[string]|false|Group the costs by the specified fields. Supported fields include `project_id`, `user_id`, `line_item`, `api_key_id`, and `api_source`. Support for combining `user_id` with `project_id` grouping or the `project_ids` filter depends on the organization and requested time range. Unsupported combinations return HTTP 400. When grouped by `api_source`, results use `agents_api` for attributed Agents API activity and `unlabeled` for all other activity. Without source grouping, `api_source` is null.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of buckets to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 180, and the default is 7.<br>|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. Corresponding to the `next_page` field from the previous response.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|bucket_width|1d|
|group_by|project_id|
|group_by|user_id|
|group_by|line_item|
|group_by|api_key_id|
|group_by|api_source|

<h3 id="audio-speeches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

#### Enumerated Values

## Create invite

<a id="opIdinviteUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/invites \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "string",
    "role": "reader",
    "projects": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "role": "member"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organization/invites`

Create an invite for a user to the organization. The invite must be accepted by the user before they have access to the organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "string",
  "role": "reader",
  "projects": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "role": "member"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-invite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InviteRequest](#schemainviterequest)|true|The invite request payload.|
|» email|body|string|true|Send an email to this address|
|» role|body|string|true|`owner` or `reader`|
|» projects|body|[object]|false|An array of projects to which membership is granted at the same time the org invite is accepted. If omitted, the user will be invited to the default project for compatibility with legacy behavior. If empty list is passed, the user will not be invited to any projects, including the default one.|
|» » id|body|string|true|Project's public ID|
|» » role|body|string|true|Project membership role|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|reader|
|» role|owner|
|» » role|member|
|» » role|owner|

  "id": "string",

  "role": "owner",
  "status": "accepted",
  "created_at": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,

<a id="opIdcreate-project"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

`POST /organization/projects`

Create a new project in the organization. Projects can be created and archived, but cannot be deleted.

  "geography": "string",
  "residency": "GLOBAL",
  "external_key_id": "string"

|» name|body|string|true|The friendly name of the project, this name appears in reports.|
|» geography|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Create the project with the specified data residency region. Your organization must have access to Data residency functionality in order to use. See [data residency controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data#data-residency-controls) to review the functionality and limitations of setting this field.<br>Deprecated: use `residency` instead. Do not provide both `geography` and `residency`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» residency|body|[PublicProjectResidency](#schemapublicprojectresidency) \| null|false|Create the project with the specified residency configuration. Your organization must have access to the requested residency configuration in order to use it. See [data residency controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data#data-residency-controls) to review the functionality and limitations of setting this field.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[PublicProjectResidency](#schemapublicprojectresidency)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Update project API key

<a id="opIdupdate-project-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/projects/string/api_keys/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "scopes": [
      "api.all.read"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organization/projects/{project_id}/api_keys/{api_key_id}`

Updates the scopes and/or expiration of an existing API key in the project, including a
service-account-owned key. Requires permission to write project API keys.

Provide at least one of `scopes` or `expires_in_seconds`. Omitted fields stay
unchanged; neither field accepts `null`. Both changes are saved together.

`scopes` replaces the key's scope restrictions using the same scope identifiers
as the dashboard. An empty array means All permissions, subject to the owner's
effective access; it does not mean no access. Use `["api.all.read"]` for read-only
access or specific scopes such as `["api.files.read"]` for restricted access.
This does not change user or service-account roles or grant admin permissions.
Scope changes follow the same authentication-cache propagation as dashboard edits.

Provide `expires_in_seconds` to set the expiration relative to this request.
The value must satisfy the organization's and project's expiry policies.
Expired keys cannot be updated. Retrying resets the expiration relative to
the new request. The response contains only the redacted key, not its secret.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scopes": [
    "api.all.read"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-project-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string|true|The ID of the project.|
|api_key_id|path|string|true|The ID of the API key.|
|body|body|[UpdateProjectApiKeyBody](#schemaupdateprojectapikeybody)|true|none|
|» expires_in_seconds|body|integer|false|Number of seconds from this request until the API key expires. Must comply with the organization and project expiry policies. Expired keys cannot be updated. Retrying resets the expiry relative to the new request. Omit to keep the current expiration.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Replace the API key scope restrictions. Omit to leave scopes unchanged. An empty array removes key restrictions (All permissions), subject to the owner's effective permissions. Use ["api.all.read"] for read-only access. Scopes do not change the owner's roles or grant administrative permissions.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "organization.project.api_key",
  "redacted_value": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "created_at": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "last_used_at": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "owner_project_access": "active",
  "owner": {
    "type": "user",
    "user": {
      "id": "string",
      "email": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "created_at": 0,
      "role": "string"
    },
    "service_account": {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "created_at": 0,
      "role": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

`POST /organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts`

Creates a new service account in the project. By default, this also returns an unredacted API key for the service account.

  "expires_in_seconds": 1
}

|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|Create the service account without default roles or an API key.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» expires_in_seconds|body|integer \| null|false|Number of seconds until the initial API key expires. If omitted or null, the key does not expire unless the effective organization or project policy requires an expiration. <h1 id="openai-api-realtime">Realtime</h1>

## Create call

<a id="opIdcreate-realtime-call"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'sdp=string' \
  -F 'session={"type":"realtime","output_modalities":["audio"],"model":"string","instructions":"string","audio":{"input":{"format":{"type":"audio/pcm","rate":24000},"transcription":{"model":"string","language":"string","languages":["string"],"keywords":["string"],"prompt":"string","delay":"minimal"},"noise_reduction":null,"turn_detection":{"type":"server_vad","threshold":0,"prefix_padding_ms":0,"silence_duration_ms":0,"create_response":true,"interrupt_response":true,"idle_timeout_ms":5000}},"output":{"format":{"type":"audio/pcm","rate":24000},"voice":"ash","speed":1}},"include":["item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs"],"tracing":null,"tools":[{"type":"function","name":"string","description":"string","parameters":{}}],"tool_choice":"auto","parallel_tool_calls":true,"reasoning":{"effort":"low"},"max_output_tokens":0,"truncation":"auto","prompt":{"id":"string","version":"string","variables":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"}}}'
```

`POST /realtime/calls`

Create a new Realtime API call over WebRTC and receive the SDP answer needed
to complete the peer connection.

> Body parameter

```yaml
sdp: string
session:
  type: realtime
  output_modalities:
    - audio
  model: string
  instructions: string
  audio:
    input:
      format:
        type: audio/pcm
        rate: 24000
      transcription:
        model: string
        language: string
        languages:
          - string
        keywords:
          - string
        prompt: string
        delay: minimal
      noise_reduction: null
      turn_detection:
        type: server_vad
        threshold: 0
        prefix_padding_ms: 0
        silence_duration_ms: 0
        create_response: true
        interrupt_response: true
        idle_timeout_ms: 5000
    output:
      format:
        type: audio/pcm
        rate: 24000
      voice: ash
      speed: 1
  include:
    - item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs
  tracing: null
  tools:
    -
      type: function
      name: string
      description: string
      parameters: {}
  tool_choice: auto
  parallel_tool_calls: true
  reasoning:
    effort: low
  max_output_tokens: 0
  truncation: auto
  prompt:
    id: string
    version: string
    variables:
      property1: string
      property2: string
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

It defaults to `["audio"]`, indicating<br>that the model will respond with audio plus a transcript. `["text"]` can be used to make<br>the model respond with text only. |» » model|body|string|false|The Realtime model used for this session.<br>|

The model can be instructed on response content and format, (e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the desired behavior.<br><br>Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the start of the session.<br>|

However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.<br><br>Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.<br>|

|» tools|body|[[RealtimeFunctionTool](#schemarealtimefunctiontool) \| [MCPTool](#schemamcptool)]|false|Tools available to the model.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[RealtimeFunctionTool](#schemarealtimefunctiontool)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[MCPTool](#schemamcptool)|false|Give the model access to additional tools via remote Model Context Protocol<br>(MCP) servers. [Learn more about MCP](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).<br>|
|» tool_choice|body|[ToolChoiceOptions](#schematoolchoiceoptions) \| [ToolChoiceFunction](#schematoolchoicefunction) \| [ToolChoiceMCP](#schematoolchoicemcp)|false|How the model chooses tools. Provide one of the string modes or force a specific<br>function/MCP tool.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ToolChoiceOptions](#schematoolchoiceoptions)|false|Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.<br><br>`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.<br><br>`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or<br>more tools.<br><br>`required` means the model must call one or more tools.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ToolChoiceFunction](#schematoolchoicefunction)|false|Use this option to force the model to call a specific function.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ToolChoiceMCP](#schematoolchoicemcp)|false|Use this option to force the model to call a specific tool on a remote MCP server.<br>|
|» parallel_tool_calls|body|boolean|false|Whether the model may call multiple tools in parallel. Only supported by<br>reasoning Realtime models such as `gpt-realtime-2`.<br>|
|» reasoning|body|[RealtimeReasoning](#schemarealtimereasoning)|false|Configuration for reasoning-capable Realtime models such as `gpt-realtime-2`.<br>|
|» max_output_tokens|body|integer \| string|false|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to<br>limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a<br>given model. Defaults to `inf`.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» truncation|body|[RealtimeTruncation](#schemarealtimetruncation)|false|When the number of tokens in a conversation exceeds the model's input token limit, the conversation be truncated, meaning messages (starting from the oldest) will not be included in the model's context. A 32k context model with 4,096 max output tokens can only include 28,224 tokens in the context before truncation occurs.<br><br>Clients can configure truncation behavior to truncate with a lower max token limit, which is an effective way to control token usage and cost.<br><br>Truncation will reduce the number of cached tokens on the next turn (busting the cache), since messages are dropped from the beginning of the context. However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.<br><br>Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.<br>|
|» prompt|body|[Prompt](#schemaprompt)|false|none|

`POST /realtime/client_secrets`

Create a Realtime client secret with an associated session configuration.

Client secrets are short-lived tokens that can be passed to a client app,
such as a web frontend or mobile client, which grants access to the Realtime API without
leaking your main API key. You can configure a custom TTL for each client secret.

You can also attach session configuration options to the client secret, which will be
applied to any sessions created using that client secret, but these can also be overridden
by the client connection.

[Learn more about authentication with client secrets over WebRTC](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-webrtc).

Returns the created client secret and the effective session object. The client secret is a string that looks like `ek_1234`.


> Body parameter

    "seconds": 600
  },

    ],
    "model": "string",
    "instructions": "string",
    "audio": {

          "rate": 24000
        },
        "transcription": {

          "language": "string",
          "languages": [
            "string"
          ],
          "keywords": [
            "string"
          ],
          "prompt": "string",
          "delay": "minimal"
        },
        "noise_reduction": null,
        "turn_detection": {
          "type": "server_vad",
          "threshold": 0,
          "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
          "silence_duration_ms": 0,
          "create_response": true,
          "interrupt_response": true,
          "idle_timeout_ms": 5000
        }
      },
      "output": {
        "format": {
          "type": "audio/pcm",
          "rate": 24000
        },
        "voice": "ash",
        "speed": 1
      }
    },
    "include": [
      "item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs"
    ],
    "tracing": null,
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "parallel_tool_calls": true,
    "reasoning": {
      "effort": "low"
    },
    "max_output_tokens": 0,
    "truncation": "auto",
    "prompt": {
      "id": "string",
      "version": "string",
      "variables": {

        "property2": "string"
      }
    }

}

<h3 id="create-client-secret-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[RealtimeCreateClientSecretRequest](#schemarealtimecreateclientsecretrequest)|true|Create a client secret with the given session configuration.|
|» expires_after|body|object|false|Configuration for the client secret expiration. Expiration refers to the time after which<br>a client secret will no longer be valid for creating sessions. The session itself may<br>continue after that time once started. A secret can be used to create multiple sessions<br>until it expires.<br>|
|» » anchor|body|string|false|The anchor point for the client secret expiration, meaning that `seconds` will be added to the `created_at` time of the client secret to produce an expiration timestamp. Only `created_at` is currently supported.<br>|
|» » seconds|body|integer(int64)|false|The number of seconds from the anchor point to the expiration. Select a value between `10` and `7200` (2 hours). This default to 600 seconds (10 minutes) if not specified.<br>|
|» session|body|[RealtimeSessionCreateRequestGA](#schemarealtimesessioncreaterequestga) \| [RealtimeTranscriptionSessionCreateRequestGA](#schemarealtimetranscriptionsessioncreaterequestga)|false|Session configuration to use for the client secret. Choose either a realtime<br>session or a transcription session.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[RealtimeSessionCreateRequestGA](#schemarealtimesessioncreaterequestga)|false|Realtime session object configuration.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[RealtimeTranscriptionSessionCreateRequestGA](#schemarealtimetranscriptionsessioncreaterequestga)|false|Realtime transcription session object configuration.|

`POST /realtime/sessions`

Create an ephemeral API token for use in client-side applications with the
Realtime API. Can be configured with the same session parameters as the
`session.update` client event.

It responds with a session object, plus a `client_secret` key which contains
a usable ephemeral API token that can be used to authenticate browser clients
for the Realtime API.

Returns the created Realtime session object, plus an ephemeral key.

  "temperature": 0,
  "max_response_output_tokens": 0,
  "truncation": "auto",
  "prompt": {
    "id": "string",
    "version": "string",
    "variables": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-session-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RealtimeSessionCreateRequest](#schemarealtimesessioncreaterequest)|true|Create an ephemeral API key with the given session configuration.|
|» client_secret|body|object|true|Ephemeral key returned by the API.|
|» » value|body|string|true|Ephemeral key usable in client environments to authenticate connections<br>to the Realtime API. Use this in client-side environments rather than<br>a standard API token, which should only be used server-side.<br>|
|» » expires_at|body|integer(unixtime)|true|Timestamp for when the token expires. Currently, all tokens expire<br>after one minute.<br>|
|» modalities|body|[string]|false|The set of modalities the model can respond with. To disable audio,<br>set this to ["text"].<br>|
|» instructions|body|string|false|The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format, (e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the desired behavior.<br>Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the start of the session.<br>|
|» voice|body|[VoiceIdsOrCustomVoice](#schemavoiceidsorcustomvoice)|false|The voice the model uses to respond. Supported built-in voices are<br>`alloy`, `ash`, `ballad`, `coral`, `echo`, `sage`, `shimmer`, `verse`,<br>`marin`, and `cedar`. You may also provide a custom voice object with an<br>`id`, for example `{ "id": "voice_1234" }`. Voice cannot be changed during<br>the session once the model has responded with audio at least once.<br>Custom voices must be created from audio samples. Voices created from text prompts are supported only in Live.<br>|
|» input_audio_format|body|string|false|The format of input audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>|
|» output_audio_format|body|string|false|The format of output audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>|
|» input_audio_transcription|body|object|false|Configuration for input audio transcription, defaults to off and can be<br>set to `null` to turn off once on. Input audio transcription is not native<br>to the model, since the model consumes audio directly. Transcription runs<br>asynchronously and should be treated as rough guidance<br>rather than the representation understood by the model.<br>|
|» » model|body|string|false|The model to use for transcription.<br>|
|» speed|body|number|false|The speed of the model's spoken response. 1.0 is the default speed. 0.25 is<br>the minimum speed. 1.5 is the maximum speed. This value can only be changed<br>in between model turns, not while a response is in progress.<br>|
|» tracing|body|string \| object|false|Configuration options for tracing. Set to null to disable tracing. Once<br>tracing is enabled for a session, the configuration cannot be modified.<br><br>`auto` will create a trace for the session with default values for the<br>workflow name, group id, and metadata.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|Default tracing mode for the session.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Granular configuration for tracing.<br>|
|» » workflow_name|body|string|false|The name of the workflow to attach to this trace. This is used to<br>name the trace in the traces dashboard.<br>|
|» » group_id|body|string|false|The group id to attach to this trace to enable filtering and<br>grouping in the traces dashboard.<br>|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|The arbitrary metadata to attach to this trace to enable<br>filtering in the traces dashboard.<br>|
|» turn_detection|body|object|false|Configuration for turn detection. Can be set to `null` to turn off. Server<br>VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on<br>audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.<br>|
|» » type|body|string|false|Type of turn detection, only `server_vad` is currently supported.<br>|
|» » threshold|body|number|false|Activation threshold for VAD (0.0 to 1.0), this defaults to 0.5. A<br>higher threshold will require louder audio to activate the model, and<br>thus might perform better in noisy environments.<br>|
|» » prefix_padding_ms|body|integer|false|Amount of audio to include before the VAD detected speech (in<br>milliseconds). Defaults to 300ms.<br>|
|» » silence_duration_ms|body|integer|false|Duration of silence to detect speech stop (in milliseconds). Defaults<br>to 500ms. With shorter values the model will respond more quickly,<br>but may jump in on short pauses from the user.<br>|
|» tools|body|[object]|false|Tools (functions) available to the model.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The type of the tool, i.e. `function`.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the function.|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the function, including guidance on when and how<br>to call it, and guidance about what to tell the user when calling<br>(if anything).<br>|
|» » parameters|body|object|false|Parameters of the function in JSON Schema.|
|» tool_choice|body|string|false|How the model chooses tools. Options are `auto`, `none`, `required`, or<br>specify a function.<br>|
|» temperature|body|number|false|Sampling temperature for the model, limited to [0.6, 1.2]. Defaults to 0.8.<br>|
|» max_response_output_tokens|body|integer \| string|false|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to<br>limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a<br>given model. Defaults to `inf`.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» truncation|body|[RealtimeTruncation](#schemarealtimetruncation)|false|When the number of tokens in a conversation exceeds the model's input token limit, the conversation be truncated, meaning messages (starting from the oldest) will not be included in the model's context. A 32k context model with 4,096 max output tokens can only include 28,224 tokens in the context before truncation occurs.<br><br>Clients can configure truncation behavior to truncate with a lower max token limit, which is an effective way to control token usage and cost.<br><br>Truncation will reduce the number of cached tokens on the next turn (busting the cache), since messages are dropped from the beginning of the context. However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.<br><br>Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.<br>|
|» prompt|body|[Prompt](#schemaprompt)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» modalities|text|
|» modalities|audio|
|» » *oneOf*|auto|
|» » type|function|
|» » *oneOf*|inf|

## Create transcription session

<a id="opIdcreate-realtime-transcription-session"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/transcription_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "turn_detection": {
      "type": "server_vad",
      "threshold": 0,
      "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
      "silence_duration_ms": 0
    },
    "input_audio_noise_reduction": null,
    "input_audio_format": "pcm16",
    "input_audio_transcription": {
      "model": "string",
      "language": "string",
      "languages": [
        "string"
      ],
      "keywords": [
        "string"
      ],
      "prompt": "string",
      "delay": "minimal"
    },
    "include": [
      "item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /realtime/transcription_sessions`

Create an ephemeral API token for use in client-side applications with the
Realtime API specifically for realtime transcriptions. 
Can be configured with the same session parameters as the `transcription_session.update` client event.

It responds with a session object, plus a `client_secret` key which contains
a usable ephemeral API token that can be used to authenticate browser clients
for the Realtime API.

Returns the created Realtime transcription session object, plus an ephemeral key.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "turn_detection": {
    "type": "server_vad",
    "threshold": 0,
    "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
    "silence_duration_ms": 0
  },
  "input_audio_noise_reduction": null,
  "input_audio_format": "pcm16",
  "input_audio_transcription": {
    "model": "string",
    "language": "string",
    "languages": [
      "string"
    ],
    "keywords": [
      "string"
    ],
    "prompt": "string",
    "delay": "minimal"
  },
  "include": [
    "item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-transcription-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RealtimeTranscriptionSessionCreateRequest](#schemarealtimetranscriptionsessioncreaterequest)|true|Create an ephemeral API key with the given session configuration.|
|» turn_detection|body|object|false|Configuration for turn detection. Can be set to `null` to turn off. Server VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.<br>|
|» » type|body|string|false|Type of turn detection. Only `server_vad` is currently supported for transcription sessions.<br>|
|» » threshold|body|number|false|Activation threshold for VAD (0.0 to 1.0), this defaults to 0.5. A<br>higher threshold will require louder audio to activate the model, and<br>thus might perform better in noisy environments.<br>|
|» » prefix_padding_ms|body|integer|false|Amount of audio to include before the VAD detected speech (in<br>milliseconds). Defaults to 300ms.<br>|
|» » silence_duration_ms|body|integer|false|Duration of silence to detect speech stop (in milliseconds). Defaults<br>to 500ms. With shorter values the model will respond more quickly,<br>but may jump in on short pauses from the user.<br>|
|» input_audio_noise_reduction|body|object|false|Configuration for input audio noise reduction. This can be set to `null` to turn off.<br>Noise reduction filters audio added to the input audio buffer before it is sent to VAD and the model.<br>Filtering the audio can improve VAD and turn detection accuracy (reducing false positives) and model performance by improving perception of the input audio.<br>|
|» » type|body|[NoiseReductionType](#schemanoisereductiontype)|false|Type of noise reduction. `near_field` is for close-talking microphones such as headphones, `far_field` is for far-field microphones such as laptop or conference room microphones.<br>|
|» input_audio_format|body|string|false|The format of input audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>For `pcm16`, input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 24kHz sample rate,<br>single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order.<br>|
|» input_audio_transcription|body|[AudioTranscription](#schemaaudiotranscription)|false|Configuration for input audio transcription. The client can optionally set the language and prompt for transcription, these offer additional guidance to the transcription service.<br>|
|» include|body|[string]|false|The set of items to include in the transcription. Current available items are:<br>`item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs`<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|server_vad|
|» » type|near_field|
|» » type|far_field|
|» input_audio_format|pcm16|
|» input_audio_format|g711_ulaw|
|» input_audio_format|g711_alaw|
|» include|item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "client_secret": {
    "value": "string",
    "expires_at": 0
  },
  "modalities": [
    "text"
  ],
  "input_audio_format": "string",
  "input_audio_transcription": {
    "model": "string",
    "language": "string",
    "languages": [
      "string"
    ],
    "prompt": "string"
  },
  "turn_detection": {
    "type": "string",
    "threshold": 0,
    "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
    "silence_duration_ms": 0
  }
}
```

## Create translation client secret

<a id="opIdcreate-realtime-translation-client-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/translations/client_secrets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expires_after": {
      "anchor": "created_at",
      "seconds": 600
    },
    "session": {
      "model": "string",
      "audio": {
        "input": {
          "transcription": {
            "model": "string"
          },
          "noise_reduction": {
            "type": "near_field"
          }
        },
        "output": {
          "language": "string"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /realtime/translations/client_secrets`

Create a Realtime translation client secret with an associated translation session configuration.

Client secrets are short-lived tokens that can be passed to a client app,
such as a web frontend or mobile client, which grants access to the Realtime
Translation API without leaking your main API key. You can configure a custom
TTL for each client secret.

Returns the created client secret and the effective translation session object.
The client secret is a string that looks like `ek_1234`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expires_after": {
    "anchor": "created_at",
    "seconds": 600
  },
  "session": {
    "model": "string",
    "audio": {
      "input": {
        "transcription": {
          "model": "string"
        },
        "noise_reduction": {
          "type": "near_field"
        }
      },
      "output": {
        "language": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-translation-client-secret-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RealtimeTranslationClientSecretCreateRequest](#schemarealtimetranslationclientsecretcreaterequest)|true|Create a client secret with the given translation session configuration.|
|» expires_after|body|object|false|Configuration for the client secret expiration. Expiration refers to the time after which<br>a client secret will no longer be valid for creating sessions. The session itself may<br>continue after that time once started. A secret can be used to create multiple sessions<br>until it expires.<br>|
|» » anchor|body|string|false|The anchor point for the client secret expiration, meaning that `seconds` will be added to the `created_at` time of the client secret to produce an expiration timestamp. Only `created_at` is currently supported.<br>|
|» » seconds|body|integer(int64)|false|The number of seconds from the anchor point to the expiration. Select a value between `10` and `7200` (2 hours). This default to 600 seconds (10 minutes) if not specified.<br>|
|» session|body|[RealtimeTranslationSessionCreateRequest](#schemarealtimetranslationsessioncreaterequest)|true|Realtime translation session configuration. Translation sessions stream source<br>audio in and translated audio plus transcript deltas out continuously.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » anchor|created_at|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

  "value": "string",
  "expires_at": 0,
  "session": {
    "id": "string",
    "type": "translation",
    "expires_at": 0,
    "model": "string",
    "audio": {
      "input": {
        "transcription": {
          "model": "string"
        },

        }
      },

      }

}

`GET /vector_stores`

Returns a list of vector stores.

<h3 id="list-vector-stores-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 20.<br>|
|order|query|string|false|Sort order by the `created_at` timestamp of the objects. `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include after=obj_foo in order to fetch the next page of the list.<br>|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with obj_foo, your subsequent call can include before=obj_foo in order to fetch the previous page of the list.<br>|

|order|desc|

`POST /vector_stores`

Create a vector store.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "file_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "expires_after": {
    "anchor": "last_active_at",
    "days": 1
  },

<h3 id="create-vector-store-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateVectorStoreRequest](#schemacreatevectorstorerequest)|true|none|
|» file_ids|body|[string]|false|A list of [File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files) IDs that the vector store should use. Useful for tools like `file_search` that can access files.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the vector store.|

<a id="opIdcreateVectorStoreFileBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/vector_stores/vs_abc123/file_batches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "file_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "files": [
      {
        "file_id": "string",
        "chunking_strategy": {
          "type": "auto"
        },
        "attributes": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "chunking_strategy": {
      "type": "auto"
    },
    "attributes": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/file_batches`

Create a vector store file batch.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "file_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "files": [
    {
      "file_id": "string",
      "chunking_strategy": {
        "type": "auto"
      },
      "attributes": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "chunking_strategy": {
    "type": "auto"
  },
  "attributes": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-vector-store-file-batch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vector_store_id|path|string|true|The ID of the vector store for which to create a File Batch.<br>|
|body|body|[CreateVectorStoreFileBatchRequest](#schemacreatevectorstorefilebatchrequest)|true|none|
|» file_ids|body|[string]|false|A list of [File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files) IDs that the vector store should use. Useful for tools like `file_search` that can access files. If `attributes` or `chunking_strategy` are provided, they will be applied to all files in the batch. The maximum batch size is 2000 files. This endpoint is recommended for multi-file ingestion and helps reduce per-vector-store write request pressure. Mutually exclusive with `files`.|
|» files|body|[[CreateVectorStoreFileRequest](#schemacreatevectorstorefilerequest)]|false|A list of objects that each include a `file_id` plus optional `attributes` or `chunking_strategy`. Use this when you need to override metadata for specific files. The global `attributes` or `chunking_strategy` will be ignored and must be specified for each file. The maximum batch size is 2000 files. This endpoint is recommended for multi-file ingestion and helps reduce per-vector-store write request pressure. Mutually exclusive with `file_ids`.|
|» chunking_strategy|body|[ChunkingStrategyRequestParam](#schemachunkingstrategyrequestparam)|false|The chunking strategy used to chunk the file(s). If not set, will use the `auto` strategy.|
|» attributes|body|[VectorStoreFileAttributes](#schemavectorstorefileattributes)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

<a id="opIdcreateVectorStoreFile"></a>

> Code samples

curl https://api.openai.com/v1/vector_stores/vs_abc123/files \
  -X POST \

      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/files`

    "property2": "string"

For multi-file ingestion, we recommend [`file_batches`](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/vector_stores/subresources/file_batches/methods/create) to minimize per-vector-store write requests.|

|404|Not Found|The vector store or file was not found.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|The vector store is temporarily unavailable for this change or was modified concurrently.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The request was rejected because a rate limit was exceeded.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|The vector store file attributes could not be updated.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|409|Retry-After|integer||When this change is blocked by a vector store migration, the number of seconds to wait before retrying. Other conflicts may omit this header.|
|429|Retry-After|integer||The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted for 429 responses that require user action.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## Search vector store

<a id="opIdsearchVectorStore"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/vector_stores/vs_abc123/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "query": "string",
    "rewrite_query": false,
    "max_num_results": 10,
    "filters": {
      "type": "eq",
      "key": "string",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "ranking_options": {
      "ranker": "auto",
      "score_threshold": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/search`

Search a vector store for relevant chunks based on a query and file attributes filter.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": "string",
  "rewrite_query": false,
  "max_num_results": 10,
  "filters": {
    "type": "eq",
    "key": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "ranking_options": {
    "ranker": "auto",
    "score_threshold": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="search-vector-store-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vector_store_id|path|string|true|The ID of the vector store to search.|
|body|body|[VectorStoreSearchRequest](#schemavectorstoresearchrequest)|true|none|
|» query|body|string \| [string]|true|A query string for a search|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» rewrite_query|body|boolean|false|Whether to rewrite the natural language query for vector search.|
|» max_num_results|body|integer|false|The maximum number of results to return. This number should be between 1 and 50 inclusive.|
|» filters|body|[ComparisonFilter](#schemacomparisonfilter) \| [CompoundFilter](#schemacompoundfilter)|false|A filter to apply based on file attributes.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ComparisonFilter](#schemacomparisonfilter)|false|A filter used to compare a specified attribute key to a given value using a defined comparison operation.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CompoundFilter](#schemacompoundfilter)|false|Combine multiple filters using `and` or `or`.|
|» ranking_options|body|object|false|Ranking options for search.|
|» » ranker|body|string|false|Enable re-ranking; set to `none` to disable, which can help reduce latency.|
|» » score_threshold|body|number|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » ranker|none|
|» » ranker|auto|
|» » ranker|default-2024-11-15|

  ],

      },

        {

        }
      ]
    }
  ],

}
```

<h1 id="openai-api-decisions">Decisions</h1>

## Create a decision

<a id="opIdcreateDecision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "string",
    "input": "string",
    "questions": [
      {
        "type": "predicate",
        "name": "string",
        "instructions": "string"
      }
    ],
    "safety_identifier": "string",
    "prompt_cache_key": "string",
    "prompt_cache_options": {
      "ttl": "30m",
      "mode": "implicit"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /decisions`

Use this endpoint to quickly answer classification or scoring questions about some input. You can ask multiple questions in one request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "questions": [
    {
      "type": "predicate",
      "name": "string",
      "instructions": "string"
    }
  ],
  "safety_identifier": "string",
  "prompt_cache_key": "string",
  "prompt_cache_options": {
    "ttl": "30m",
    "mode": "implicit"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-decision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DecisionRequest](#schemadecisionrequest)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|The model to use. Only `gpt-6-luna` is supported.|
|» input|body|[DecisionInput](#schemadecisioninput)|true|The input to evaluate for every question. Provide a text string or an ordered array of messages, function calls and outputs, or custom tool calls and outputs. Each tool output must identify a matching call by call ID.|
|» questions|body|[[QuestionParam](#schemaquestionparam)]|true|Ask 1–400 questions about the input. Each question can be a predicate, choice, or score. Answers come back in the same order.|
|» safety_identifier|body|string \| null|false|Opaque caller-provided end-user identifier, scoped by the verified org. Match Responses' limit; this is never the authenticated user identity.|
|» prompt_cache_key|body|string \| null|false|Partition prompt cache reuse by caller-provided key.|
|» prompt_cache_options|body|object \| null|false|Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.|
|» » ttl|body|string|false|The minimum lifetime applied to every implicit and explicit cache breakpoint written by the request. Defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. The backend may retain cache entries for longer.|
|» » mode|body|string \| null|false|Controls whether OpenAI automatically creates an implicit cache breakpoint. Defaults to `implicit`. With `implicit`, OpenAI creates one implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest three explicit breakpoints in the request. With `explicit`, OpenAI does not create an implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest four explicit breakpoints. If there are no explicit breakpoints, the request does not use prompt caching.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » ttl|30m|
|» » mode|implicit|
|» » mode|explicit|
|» » mode|null|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "answers": [
    {
      "type": "predicate",
      "name": "string",
      "probability": 0
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": -2147483648,
    "input_tokens_details": {
      "cached_tokens": -2147483648,
      "cache_write_tokens": -2147483648
    },
    "output_tokens": -2147483648,
    "output_tokens_details": {
      "reasoning_tokens": -2147483648
    },
    "total_tokens": -2147483648
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The answers and token usage.|[DecisionResponse](#schemadecisionresponse)|

ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## Write an agent environment file

<a id="opIdcreateAgentEnvironmentFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/environments/string/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "file_id",
    "file_id": "string",
    "path": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /agents/environments/{environment_id}/files`

Copies inline bytes or a Files API file into a connected execution environment, replacing an existing regular file at the same path. Upload between turns and wait for success before starting the next turn. See [environment files](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/environments/files).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "file_id",
  "file_id": "string",
  "path": "string"
}

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» *oneOf*|body|[HostedEnvironmentFileParamFileId](#schemahostedenvironmentfileparamfileid)|false|A file previously uploaded through the OpenAI Files API.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[HostedEnvironmentFileParamInline](#schemahostedenvironmentfileparaminline)|false|A file supplied directly as standard-base64 data.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

## Create an agent

<a id="opIdcreateAgent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/agents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "experimental": {
      "time_awareness": false
    },
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "model": "string",
    "reasoning": {
      "effort": "none",
      "summary": "concise"
    },
    "text": {
      "format": {
        "type": "text"
      },
      "verbosity": "low"
    },
    "service_tier": "auto",
    "instructions": "string",
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {
          "property1": null,
          "property2": null
        },
        "defer_loading": false
      }
    ],
    "multi_agent": {
      "enabled": true,
      "max_concurrent_subagents": 1
    },
    "compaction": {
      "async": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /agents`

Creates a reusable agent without storing credentials. See [agent configuration](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/configuration).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "experimental": {
    "time_awareness": false
  },
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "model": "string",
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": "none",
    "summary": "concise"
  },
  "text": {
    "format": {
      "type": "text"
    },
    "verbosity": "low"
  },
  "service_tier": "auto",
  "instructions": "string",
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "parameters": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "defer_loading": false
    }
  ],
  "multi_agent": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_concurrent_subagents": 1
  },
  "compaction": {
    "async": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-agent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateAgentParams](#schemacreateagentparams)|false|none|
|» experimental|body|[ExperimentalConfigParam](#schemaexperimentalconfigparam)|false|Experimental agent settings. All experimental features default to disabled.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Up to 16 string key-value pairs, with keys up to 64 and values up to 512 characters. Omission or null defaults to an empty map.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|A human-readable name for the agent. Omission or null leaves the agent unnamed.|
|» model|body|string|true|The model to use for the agent. The requested model name is preserved.|
|» reasoning|body|[ReasoningParam](#schemareasoningparam) \| null|false|Configuration for model reasoning. Omission uses the model's default effort.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ReasoningParam](#schemareasoningparam)|false|Reasoning configuration for the agent.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» text|body|[TextParam](#schematextparam) \| null|false|Configuration for generated text. Defaults to the `text` format and medium verbosity.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[TextParam](#schematextparam)|false|Configuration for text generated by the agent.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» service_tier|body|[ServiceTierParam](#schemaservicetierparam) \| null|false|The service tier used for model requests. Defaults to `auto`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ServiceTierParam](#schemaservicetierparam)|false|The service tier used for model requests.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» instructions|body|string \| null|false|Additional instructions appended to the agent's default base instructions. Omit or set to null to add no custom instructions.|
|» tools|body|[[PersistedAgentToolConfigParam](#schemapersistedagenttoolconfigparam)]|false|Tools available to the agent. Defaults to an empty list. The tool list must fit within 3 MiB (3,145,728 bytes) of compact UTF-8 JSON.|
|» multi_agent|body|[MultiAgentConfigCurrentParam](#schemamultiagentconfigcurrentparam) \| null|false|Configuration for creating and coordinating subagents. Subagent tools are disabled by default.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[MultiAgentConfigCurrentParam](#schemamultiagentconfigcurrentparam)|false|Explicit configuration for creating and coordinating subagents.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» compaction|body|[CompactionParam](#schemacompactionparam) \| null|false|Context compaction settings. Omission or null enables background compaction.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CompactionParam](#schemacompactionparam)|false|Settings for compacting the agent's context.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|auto|
|» » *anyOf*|default|
|» » *anyOf*|flex|
|» » *anyOf*|priority|
|» » *anyOf*|fast|
|» » *anyOf*|ultrafast|

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» compaction|body|[CompactionParam](#schemacompactionparam) \| null|false|Context compaction settings. Omit to keep the current settings. A supplied object replaces the settings; null or an empty object enables background compaction.|

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## List agent sessions

<a id="opIdlistAgentSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/sessions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /agents/sessions`

Lists managed agent sessions using ID-based pagination and the requested sort order. See [managing sessions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/sessions/manage).

<h3 id="list-agent-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of resources to return, between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20.|
|order|query|[ListOrderParam](#schemalistorderparam)|false|The order in which resources are returned. Defaults to `desc`.|
|after|query|string|false|Return resources after this resource ID in the selected order.|
|agent_id|query|string|false|Only return sessions whose root agent has this ID. Omit to return sessions for all agents.|
|metadata|query|object|false|Exact string matches supplied as `metadata[key]=value`. All supplied pairs must match. Up to 16 pairs, with keys from 1 to 64 characters and values up to 512 characters. New sessions and metadata updates may take time to appear in filtered results.|

|order|asc|
|order|desc|

`POST /agents/sessions`

Creates a managed agent session, optionally submits initial input, and returns the session or streams its events when stream is true. See [running sessions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/sessions).

  ],
  "input": "string",
  "stream": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-agent-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateAgentSessionParams](#schemacreateagentsessionparams)|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Up to 16 string key-value pairs, with keys up to 64 and values up to 512 characters. Omission or null defaults to an empty map.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

|» environment|body|[EnvironmentParam](#schemaenvironmentparam)|true|An inline execution environment or a reference to an environment template.|
|» vault_ids|body|[string]|false|The IDs of vaults made available to the session.|
|» input|body|[CreateSessionInputParam](#schemacreatesessioninputparam) \| null|false|Initial input to submit when the session is created. A string is shorthand for a single user message. Required when `environment.type` is `none`, or when `stream` is `true` for an environment that is not `self_hosted`; optional for self-hosted and non-streaming execution environments.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CreateSessionInputParam](#schemacreatesessioninputparam)|false|Initial input submitted when creating a session.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|Whether to stream session events as server-sent events. Defaults to `false`.|

## Delete an agent session

<a id="opIddeleteAgentSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/sessions/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /agents/sessions/{session_id}`

Removes a managed agent session from the public API and returns a deletion confirmation. If backend execution has ended, deletion can cancel a still-open public turn and abandon unpublished outputs. Running execution must be cancelled first. Physical cleanup may continue asynchronously. See [managing sessions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/sessions/manage).

<h3 id="delete-an-agent-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Create agent session input events

<a id="opIdcreateAgentSessionEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/sessions/string/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "events": [
      {
        "type": "agent.session.input.computer_use_approval_request_result",
        "request_id": "string",
        "response": {
          "type": "browser_authentication",
          "action": "submit",
          "fields": [
            {
              "field_id": "string",
              "value": "string"
            }
          ],
          "selected_option": "string"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /agents/sessions/{session_id}/events`

Submits message, cancellation, tool-result, or computer-use approval-response events to a managed agent session. Cancellation can recover a still-open turn whose backend execution has ended by marking it cancelled and abandoning unpublished outputs. Saved results, published files, and existing terminal outcomes are preserved. HTTP 202 confirms acceptance, not durable completion. See [session events](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/sessions/events).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "type": "agent.session.input.computer_use_approval_request_result",
      "request_id": "string",
      "response": {
        "type": "browser_authentication",
        "action": "submit",
        "fields": [
          {
            "field_id": "string",
            "value": "string"
          }
        ],
        "selected_option": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-agent-session-input-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the session.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional client-generated key that makes retries of submitted messages idempotent.|
|body|body|[CreateSessionEventsParams](#schemacreatesessioneventsparams)|false|none|
|» events|body|[[SessionInputParam](#schemasessioninputparam)]|true|The input events to submit to the session.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

    "type": "string",

    "param": "string"
  }
}

  }
}

## List agent session traces

<a id="opIdlistAgentSessionTraces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/sessions/string/traces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /agents/sessions/{session_id}/traces`

Lists published root-turn traces as OTLP JSON, ordered by turn creation time and ID. Unpublished traces are skipped. Each page returns data available when read; it does not wait for late traces. Trace reads and the JSON response are limited to 16 MiB per request. If the limit is exceeded, request fewer traces.

`GET /vaults/{vault_id}/credentials`

Lists a vault's credentials using ID-based pagination without returning secret values. See [vaults](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools/vaults).

<h3 id="list-vault-credentials-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vault_id|path|string|true|The ID of the vault.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of resources to return, between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20.|
|order|query|[ListOrderParam](#schemalistorderparam)|false|The order in which resources are returned. Defaults to `desc`.|
|after|query|string|false|Return resources after this resource ID in the selected order.|
|metadata|query|object|false|Exact string matches supplied as `metadata[key]=value`. All supplied pairs must match. Up to 16 pairs, with keys from 1 to 64 characters and values up to 512 characters. Filtering is eventually consistent; metadata changes may take time to appear.|
|status|query|[VaultStatusFilterParam](#schemavaultstatusfilterparam)|false|Filter by one status or a list, such as `status=active` or `status[]=active&status[]=archived`. Both statuses are included by default.|
