## Create a vault credential

<a id="opIdcreateVaultCredential"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/vaults/string/credentials \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{

    "auth": {

      "expires_at": "string",
      "refresh": {
        "token_endpoint": "string",
        "client_id": "string",
        "resource": "string",
        "scope": "string",
        "refresh_token": "string",
        "token_endpoint_auth": {
          "type": "none"
        }
      }

      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /vaults/{vault_id}/credentials`

Creates a vault credential. Secret values are write-only and are never returned. See [vaults](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools/vaults).

## Delete a vault credential

<a id="opIddeleteVaultCredential"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/vaults/string/credentials/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /vaults/{vault_id}/credentials/{credential_id}`

<h2 id="tocS_AssistantStreamEvent">AssistantStreamEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistantstreamevent"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantStreamEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSassistantstreamevent"></a>
<a id="tocsassistantstreamevent"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "event": "thread.created",
  "data": {
    "id": "string",
    "object": "thread",
    "created_at": 0,
    "tool_resources": {
      "code_interpreter": {
        "file_ids": []
      },
      "file_search": {
        "vector_store_ids": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    },
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

Represents an event emitted when streaming a Run.

Each event in a server-sent events stream has an `event` and `data` property:

```
event: thread.created
data: {"id": "thread_123", "object": "thread", ...}
```

We emit events whenever a new object is created, transitions to a new state, or is being
streamed in parts (deltas). For example, we emit `thread.run.created` when a new run
is created, `thread.run.completed` when a run completes, and so on. When an Assistant chooses
to create a message during a run, we emit a `thread.message.created event`, a
`thread.message.in_progress` event, many `thread.message.delta` events, and finally a
`thread.message.completed` event.

We may add additional events over time, so we recommend handling unknown events gracefully
in your code. See the [Assistants API quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) to learn how to
integrate the Assistants API with streaming.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[ThreadStreamEvent](#schemathreadstreamevent)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[RunStreamEvent](#schemarunstreamevent)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[RunStepStreamEvent](#schemarunstepstreamevent)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[MessageStreamEvent](#schemamessagestreamevent)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[ErrorEvent](#schemaerrorevent)|false|none|Occurs when an [error](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/error-codes#api-errors) occurs. This can happen due to an internal server error or a timeout.|
|*oneOf*|[DoneEvent](#schemadoneevent)|false|none|Occurs when a stream ends.|

<h2 id="tocS_AssistantsApiResponseFormatOption">AssistantsApiResponseFormatOption</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistantsapiresponseformatoption"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantsApiResponseFormatOption"></a>
<a id="tocSassistantsapiresponseformatoption"></a>
<a id="tocsassistantsapiresponseformatoption"></a>

```json
"auto"
```

Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with [GPT-4o](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o), [GPT-4 Turbo](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4-turbo), and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`.

Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.

**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. Without this, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace until the generation reaches the token limit, resulting in a long-running and seemingly "stuck" request. Also note that the message content may be partially cut off if `finish_reason="length"`, which indicates the generation exceeded `max_tokens` or the conversation exceeded the max context length.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|`auto` is the default value<br>|
|*oneOf*|[ResponseFormatText](#schemaresponseformattext)|false|none|Default response format. Used to generate text responses.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[ResponseFormatJsonObject](#schemaresponseformatjsonobject)|false|none|JSON object response format. An older method of generating JSON responses.<br>Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the<br>model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it<br>to do so.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[ResponseFormatJsonSchema](#schemaresponseformatjsonschema)|false|none|JSON Schema response format. Used to generate structured JSON responses.<br>Learn more about [Structured Outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|auto|

<h2 id="tocS_AssistantsApiToolChoiceOption">AssistantsApiToolChoiceOption</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistantsapitoolchoiceoption"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantsApiToolChoiceOption"></a>
<a id="tocSassistantsapitoolchoiceoption"></a>
<a id="tocsassistantsapitoolchoiceoption"></a>

```json
"none"
```

Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.
`none` means the model will not call any tools and instead generates a message.
`auto` is the default value and means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools.
`required` means the model must call one or more tools before responding to the user.
Specifying a particular tool like `{"type": "file_search"}` or `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "my_function"}}` forces the model to call that tool.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|`none` means the model will not call any tools and instead generates a message. `auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. `required` means the model must call one or more tools before responding to the user.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[AssistantsNamedToolChoice](#schemaassistantsnamedtoolchoice)|false|none|Specifies a tool the model should use. Use to force the model to call a specific tool.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|none|
|*oneOf*|auto|
|*oneOf*|required|

<h2 id="tocS_AudioResponseFormat">AudioResponseFormat</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaudioresponseformat"></a>
<a id="schema_AudioResponseFormat"></a>
<a id="tocSaudioresponseformat"></a>
<a id="tocsaudioresponseformat"></a>

```json
"json"
```

The format of the output, in one of these options: `json`, `text`, `srt`, `verbose_json`, `vtt`, or `diarized_json`. For `gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, the only supported format is `json`. For `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`, the supported formats are `json`, `text`, and `diarized_json`, with `diarized_json` required to receive speaker annotations.

<h2 id="tocS_AudioTranscription">AudioTranscription</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaudiotranscription"></a>
<a id="schema_AudioTranscription"></a>
<a id="tocSaudiotranscription"></a>
<a id="tocsaudiotranscription"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "string",
  "language": "string",
  "languages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "keywords": [
    "string"
  ],
  "prompt": "string",
  "delay": "minimal"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|false|none|The model to use for transcription. Current options are `whisper-1`, `gpt-transcribe`, `gpt-live-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`, and `gpt-realtime-whisper`. Use `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` when you need diarization with speaker labels.<br>|
|language|string|false|none|The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in<br>[ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) (e.g. `en`) format<br>will improve accuracy and latency.<br>|
|languages|[string]|false|none|Possible languages of the input audio, in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) format. Supported by `gpt-transcribe` and `gpt-live-transcribe`.<br>|
|keywords|[string]|false|none|Words or phrases to guide transcription of the input audio. Supported by `gpt-transcribe` and `gpt-live-transcribe`.<br>|
|prompt|string|false|none|An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio<br>segment.<br>For `whisper-1`, the [prompt is a list of keywords](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text#prompting).<br>For `gpt-4o-transcribe` models (excluding `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`), the prompt is a free text string, for example "expect words related to technology".<br>Prompt is not supported with `gpt-realtime-whisper` in GA Realtime sessions.<br>|
|delay|string|false|none|Controls how long the model waits before emitting transcription text.<br>Higher values can improve transcription accuracy at the cost of latency.<br>Only supported with `gpt-realtime-whisper` in GA Realtime sessions.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|delay|minimal|
|delay|low|
|delay|medium|
|delay|high|
|delay|xhigh|

|error_file_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the file containing the outputs of requests with errors.|

|failed_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|false|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch failed.|
|expired_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|false|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch expired.|
|cancelling_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|false|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch started cancelling.|
|cancelled_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|false|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch was cancelled.|

|include_obfuscation|boolean|false|none|When true, stream obfuscation will be enabled. Stream obfuscation adds<br>random characters to an `obfuscation` field on streaming delta events to<br>normalize payload sizes as a mitigation to certain side-channel attacks.<br>These obfuscation fields are included by default, but add a small amount<br>of overhead to the data stream. You can set `include_obfuscation` to<br>false to optimize for bandwidth if you trust the network links between<br>your application and the OpenAI API.<br>|
|*anyOf*|null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ChatCompletionToolChoiceOption">ChatCompletionToolChoiceOption</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemachatcompletiontoolchoiceoption"></a>
<a id="schema_ChatCompletionToolChoiceOption"></a>
<a id="tocSchatcompletiontoolchoiceoption"></a>
<a id="tocschatcompletiontoolchoiceoption"></a>

```json
"none"
```

Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.
`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.
`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools.
`required` means the model must call one or more tools.
Specifying a particular tool via `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "my_function"}}` forces the model to call that tool.

`none` is the default when no tools are present. `auto` is the default if tools are present.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message. `auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. `required` means the model must call one or more tools.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[ChatCompletionAllowedToolsChoice](#schemachatcompletionallowedtoolschoice)|false|none|Constrains the tools available to the model to a pre-defined set.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[ChatCompletionNamedToolChoice](#schemachatcompletionnamedtoolchoice)|false|none|Specifies a tool the model should use. Use to force the model to call a specific function.|
|*oneOf*|[ChatCompletionNamedToolChoiceCustom](#schemachatcompletionnamedtoolchoicecustom)|false|none|Specifies a tool the model should use. Use to force the model to call a specific custom tool.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|none|
|*oneOf*|auto|
|*oneOf*|required|

Represents a streamed chunk of a chat completion response returned
by the model, based on the provided input.
[Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/streaming-responses).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for the chat completion. Each chunk has the same ID.|
|choices|[object]|true|none|A list of chat completion choices. Can contain more than one elements if `n` is greater than 1. Can also be empty for the<br>last chunk if you set `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`.<br>|
|created|integer(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the chat completion was created. Each chunk has the same timestamp.|
|model|string|true|none|The model to generate the completion.|
|obfuscation|string|false|none|An obfuscation string added to normalize the size of streamed chunks as a<br>mitigation to certain side-channel attacks. The field is included by<br>default and omitted when `stream_options.include_obfuscation` is `false`.<br>|
|service_tier|[ServiceTier](#schemaservicetier)|false|none|none|
|system_fingerprint|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with.<br>Can be used in conjunction with the `seed` request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism.<br>|
|object|string|true|none|The object type, which is always `chat.completion.chunk`.|
|usage|[CompletionUsage](#schemacompletionusage) \| null|false|none|An optional field that will only be present when you set<br>`stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` in your request. When present, it<br>contains a null value **except for the last chunk** which contains the<br>token usage statistics for the entire request.<br><br>**NOTE:** If the stream is interrupted or cancelled, you may not<br>receive the final usage chunk which contains the total token usage for<br>the request.<br>|
|moderation|[ChatCompletionModeration](#schemachatcompletionmoderation) \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|chat.completion.chunk|

|temperature|number \| null|false|none|What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.<br><br>We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.<br>|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.<br><br>We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.<br>|
|user|string|false|none|A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).<br>|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|system_fingerprint|string|false|none|This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with.<br><br>Can be used in conjunction with the `seed` request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism.<br>|
|object|string|true|none|The object type, which is always "text_completion"|
|usage|[CompletionUsage](#schemacompletionusage)|false|none|Usage statistics for the completion request.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateEmbeddingRequest">CreateEmbeddingRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreateembeddingrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateEmbeddingRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreateembeddingrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreateembeddingrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "input": "The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog",
  "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "encoding_format": "float",
  "dimensions": 1,
  "user": "user-1234"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input|string \| [string] \| [integer] \| [[integer]]|true|none|Input text to embed, encoded as a string or array of tokens. To embed multiple inputs in a single request, pass an array of strings or array of token arrays. The input must not exceed the max input tokens for the model (8192 tokens for all embedding models), cannot be an empty string, and any array must be 2048 dimensions or less. [Example Python code](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/how_to_count_tokens_with_tiktoken) for counting tokens. In addition to the per-input token limit, all embedding models enforce a maximum of 300,000 tokens summed across all inputs in a single request.<br>|
|model|string|true|none|ID of the model to use. You can use the [List models](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/models/methods/list) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) for descriptions of them.<br>|
|encoding_format|string|false|none|The format to return the embeddings in. Can be either `float` or [`base64`](https://pypi.org/project/pybase64/).|
|dimensions|integer|false|none|The number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have. Only supported in `text-embedding-3` and later models.<br>|
|user|string|false|none|A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|encoding_format|float|
|encoding_format|base64|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|image|string(binary) \| [string(binary)]|true|none|The image(s) to edit. Must be a supported image file or an array of images.<br><br>For the GPT image models (`gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`,<br>`gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,<br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and<br>`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`), each image should be a `png`, `webp`, or `jpg`<br>file less than 50MB. You can provide up to 16 images. `chatgpt-image-latest`<br>follows the same input constraints as GPT image models.<br>|
|prompt|string|true|none|A text description of the desired image(s). The maximum length is 32000 characters for the GPT image models.|
|mask|string(binary)|false|none|An additional image whose fully transparent areas (e.g. where alpha is zero) indicate where `image` should be edited. If there are multiple images provided, the mask will be applied on the first image. Must be a valid PNG file, less than 4MB, and have the same dimensions as `image`.|
|markup|[markup](#schemamarkup)|false|none|A transparent PNG overlaid on the first image to guide the edit. Must match that image's dimensions after orientation and contain transparent pixels. Supports GPT Image 2.5 and 2.6. Cannot be combined with mask.|
|background|string \| null|false|none|Set the background of the generated image(s). This parameter is only supported for<br>the GPT image models. Must be one of `transparent`, `opaque`, or `auto` (default<br>value). When `auto` is used, the model will automatically determine the best<br>background for the image.<br><br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their `2026-09-08`<br>snapshots, support `opaque` and `transparent` backgrounds. Transparent backgrounds<br>are available for supported GPT Image models. For `gpt-image-2` and<br>`gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, this support is in preview. When using `transparent`,<br>set the output format to `png` or `webp`.<br>|
|model|string|true|none|The GPT image model to use for image editing<br>(`gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-2`,<br>`gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,<br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`,<br>`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, or `chatgpt-image-latest`).<br><br>`gpt-image-1` was shut down on October 23, 2026. Use<br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare` instead.<br>|
|n|integer \| null|false|none|The number of images to generate. Must be between 1 and 10.|
|size|string \| null|false|none|The size of the generated images. Defaults to `auto`. For `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, arbitrary resolutions are supported as `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings, for example `1536x864`. Width and height must both be divisible by 16 and the requested aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Resolutions above `2560x1440` are experimental, and the maximum supported resolution is `3840x2160`. The requested size must also satisfy the model's current pixel and edge limits. The standard sizes `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, and `1024x1536` are supported by the GPT image models; `auto` is supported for models that allow automatic sizing.|
|response_format|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** Legacy response format parameter for retired image models. Unsupported for GPT image models, which always return base64-encoded images.|
|output_format|string \| null|false|none|The format in which the generated images are returned. This parameter is<br>only supported for the GPT image models. Must be one of `png`, `jpeg`, or `webp`.<br>The default value is `png`.<br>|
|output_compression|integer \| null|false|none|The compression level (0-100%) for the generated images. This parameter<br>is only supported for the GPT image models with the `webp` or `jpeg` output<br>formats, and defaults to 100.<br>|
|safety_identifier|string \| null|false|none|A stable identifier for an end user in your organization, used for safety monitoring and abuse detection. Hash a username or email address to avoid sending identifying information. A non-empty value takes precedence over the deprecated `user` parameter. If omitted, null, or empty, the API uses `user` when available. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).|
|user|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `safety_identifier` instead. This parameter remains accepted for backward compatibility and is used when `safety_identifier` is omitted, null, or empty. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).|
|input_fidelity|[InputFidelity](#schemainputfidelity) \| null|false|none|none|
|stream|boolean \| null|false|none|Edit the image in streaming mode. Defaults to `false`. See the<br>[Image generation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation) for more information.<br>|
|partial_images|[PartialImages](#schemapartialimages)|false|none|none|
|quality|string \| null|false|none|The quality of the image that will be generated for GPT image models. The GPT image models support `low`, `medium`, and `high`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their `2026-09-08` snapshots, also support `xhigh` and `max`. Defaults to `auto`.<br>|

Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).<br><br>Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.<br><br>**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. Without this, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace until the generation reaches the token limit, resulting in a long-running and seemingly "stuck" request. Also note that the message content may be partially cut off if `finish_reason="length"`, which indicates the generation exceeded `max_tokens` or the conversation exceeded the max context length.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateTranscriptionRequest">CreateTranscriptionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatetranscriptionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateTranscriptionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreatetranscriptionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreatetranscriptionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "file": "string",
  "model": "gpt-4o-transcribe",
  "language": "string",
  "languages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "keywords": [
    "string"
  ],
  "prompt": "string",
  "response_format": "json",
  "temperature": 0,
  "include": [
    "logprobs"
  ],
  "timestamp_granularities": [
    "segment"
  ],
  "stream": false,
  "chunking_strategy": "auto",
  "known_speaker_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "known_speaker_references": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file|string(binary)|true|none|The audio file object (not file name) to transcribe, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm.<br>The request must include enough format metadata for the file to be identified. We recommend an extension-bearing filename and an appropriate content type.<br>|
|model|string|true|none|ID of the model to use. The options are `gpt-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`, `whisper-1` (which is powered by our open source Whisper V2 model), and `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|language|string|false|none|The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) (e.g. `en`) format will improve accuracy and latency.<br>|
|languages|[string]|false|none|Possible languages of the input audio, in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) format. Supported by `gpt-transcribe`.<br>|
|keywords|[string]|false|none|Words or phrases to guide transcription of the input audio. Supported by `gpt-transcribe`.<br>|
|prompt|string|false|none|An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The [prompt](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text#prompting) should match the audio language. This field is not supported when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|response_format|[AudioResponseFormat](#schemaaudioresponseformat)|false|none|The format of the output, in one of these options: `json`, `text`, `srt`, `verbose_json`, `vtt`, or `diarized_json`. For `gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, the only supported format is `json`. For `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`, the supported formats are `json`, `text`, and `diarized_json`, with `diarized_json` required to receive speaker annotations.<br>|
|temperature|number|false|none|The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use [log probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability) to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.<br>|
|include|[[TranscriptionInclude](#schematranscriptioninclude)]|false|none|Additional information to include in the transcription response.<br>`logprobs` will return the log probabilities of the tokens in the<br>response to understand the model's confidence in the transcription.<br>`logprobs` only works with response_format set to `json` and only with<br>the models `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`. This field is not supported when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|timestamp_granularities|[string]|false|none|The timestamp granularities to populate for this transcription. `response_format` must be set `verbose_json` to use timestamp granularities. Either or both of these options are supported: `word`, or `segment`. Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.<br>This option is not available for `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|
|stream|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|chunking_strategy|string \| [VadConfig](#schemavadconfig) \| null|false|none|none|
|known_speaker_names|[string]|false|none|Optional list of speaker names that correspond to the audio samples provided in `known_speaker_references[]`. Each entry should be a short identifier (for example `customer` or `agent`). Up to 4 speakers are supported.<br>|
|known_speaker_references|[string]|false|none|Optional list of audio samples (as [data URLs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/Data_URLs)) that contain known speaker references matching `known_speaker_names[]`. Each sample must be between 2 and 10 seconds, and can use any of the same input audio formats supported by `file`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|response_format|json|
|response_format|text|
|response_format|srt|
|response_format|verbose_json|
|response_format|vtt|
|response_format|diarized_json|
|include|logprobs|
|timestamp_granularities|word|
|timestamp_granularities|segment|

<a id="schemacreatevoicefromconsentrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateVoiceFromConsentRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreatevoicefromconsentrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreatevoicefromconsentrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "audio_sample",
  "name": "string",
  "audio_sample": "string",
  "consent": "string"
}
```

Creates a voice from a consent recording and an audio sample. Requires multipart/form-data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The voice creation method. Defaults to `audio_sample` when omitted.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the new voice.|
|audio_sample|string(binary)|true|none|The sample audio recording file. Maximum size is 10 MiB.<br><br>Supported MIME types:<br>`audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/aac`, `audio/flac`, `audio/webm`, `audio/mp4`.<br>|
|consent|string|true|none|The consent recording ID (for example, `cons_1234`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|audio_sample|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateVoicePromptRequest">CreateVoicePromptRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatevoicepromptrequest"></a>

<a id="tocScreatevoicepromptrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreatevoicepromptrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "prompt",
  "name": "string",
  "prompt": "string",
  "script_hint": "string",
  "model": "auto"
}
```

Creates a synthetic voice from a text description. Supports application/json or multipart/form-data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Set to `prompt` to create a voice from a text description.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the new voice.|
|prompt|string|true|none|A description of the desired voice. Must not contain only whitespace.|
|script_hint|string|false|none|Optional text for the voice to speak during creation. If omitted, a script is generated from the prompt. Must not be blank after trimming whitespace; scripts that are too short are rejected.|
|model|string|false|none|The voice creation model to use. Defaults to `auto`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|prompt|

<h2 id="tocS_EasyInputMessage">EasyInputMessage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaeasyinputmessage"></a>
<a id="schema_EasyInputMessage"></a>
<a id="tocSeasyinputmessage"></a>
<a id="tocseasyinputmessage"></a>

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "string",
  "phase": "commentary",
  "type": "message"
}
```

A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take
precedence over instructions given with the `user` role. Messages with the
`assistant` role are presumed to have been generated by the model in previous
interactions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|string|true|none|The role of the message input. One of `user`, `assistant`, `system`, or<br>`developer`.<br>|
|content|string \| [InputMessageContentList](#schemainputmessagecontentlist)|true|none|Text, image, or audio input to the model, used to generate a response.<br>Can also contain previous assistant responses.<br>|
|phase|[MessagePhase](#schemamessagephase) \| null|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the message input. Always `message`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|user|
|role|assistant|
|role|system|
|role|developer|
|type|message|

<h2 id="tocS_EditImageBodyJsonParam">EditImageBodyJsonParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaeditimagebodyjsonparam"></a>
<a id="schema_EditImageBodyJsonParam"></a>
<a id="tocSeditimagebodyjsonparam"></a>
<a id="tocseditimagebodyjsonparam"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-image-2.5-sunburst",
  "images": [
    {
      "image_url": "https://example.com/source-image.png",
      "file_id": "file-abc123"
    }
  ],
  "mask": {
    "image_url": "https://example.com/source-image.png",
    "file_id": "file-abc123"
  },
  "markup": {
    "image_url": "https://example.com/source-image.png",
    "file_id": "file-abc123"
  },
  "prompt": "Add a watercolor effect and keep the subject centered",
  "n": 1,
  "quality": "high",
  "input_fidelity": "high",
  "size": "1024x1024",
  "safety_identifier": "user-1234",
  "user": "user-1234",
  "output_format": "png",
  "output_compression": 100,
  "moderation": "auto",
  "background": "transparent",
  "stream": false,
  "partial_images": 1
}
```

JSON request body for image edits.

Use `images` (array of `ImageRefParam`) instead of multipart `image` uploads.
You can reference images via external URLs, data URLs, or uploaded file IDs.
JSON edits support GPT image models.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string \| null|false|none|The GPT image model to use for image editing, including `gpt-image-2`, its dated<br>snapshot `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,<br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and<br>`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`. Defaults to `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`.<br><br>`gpt-image-1` was shut down on October 23, 2026. Use<br>`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare` instead.<br>|
|images|[[ImageRefParam](#schemaimagerefparam)]|true|none|Input image references to edit.<br>For GPT image models, you can provide up to 16 images.<br>|
|mask|[ImageRefParam](#schemaimagerefparam)|false|none|Reference an input image by either URL or uploaded file ID.<br>Provide exactly one of `image_url` or `file_id`.<br>|
|markup|[ImageRefParam](#schemaimagerefparam)|false|none|A transparent PNG overlaid on the first image, referenced by file ID, HTTPS URL, or base64 data URL. Must match that image's dimensions after orientation and contain transparent pixels. Supports GPT Image 2.5 and 2.6. Cannot be combined with mask.|
|prompt|string|true|none|A text description of the desired image edit.|
|n|integer \| null|false|none|The number of edited images to generate.|
|quality|string \| null|false|none|Output quality for GPT image models. The GPT image models support `low`, `medium`,<br>and `high`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their<br>`2026-09-08` snapshots, also support `xhigh` and `max`. Defaults to `auto`.<br>|
|input_fidelity|string \| null|false|none|Control how much effort the model will exert to match the style and features, especially facial features, of input images. Supports `high` and `low` on `gpt-image-1.5`; `gpt-image-1-mini` supports only `low`. For `gpt-image-2`, omit this parameter. Defaults to `low` on supported models.|
|size|string \| null|false|none|The size of the generated images. For `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, arbitrary resolutions are supported as `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings, for example `1536x864`. Width and height must both be divisible by 16 and the requested aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Resolutions above `2560x1440` are experimental, and the maximum supported resolution is `3840x2160`. The requested size must also satisfy the model's current pixel and edge limits. The standard sizes `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, and `1024x1536` are supported by the GPT image models; `auto` is supported for models that allow automatic sizing.|
|safety_identifier|string \| null|false|none|A stable identifier for an end user in your organization, used for safety monitoring and abuse detection. Hash a username or email address to avoid sending identifying information. A non-empty value takes precedence over the deprecated `user` parameter. If omitted, null, or empty, the API uses `user` when available. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).|
|user|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `safety_identifier` instead. This parameter remains accepted for backward compatibility and is used when `safety_identifier` is omitted, null, or empty. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).|
|output_format|string \| null|false|none|Output image format. Supported for GPT image models.|
|output_compression|integer \| null|false|none|Compression level for `jpeg` or `webp` output.|
|moderation|string \| null|false|none|Moderation level for GPT image models.|
|background|string \| null|false|none|Set the background of the generated image output. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their `2026-09-08` snapshots, support `opaque` and `transparent` backgrounds. Transparent backgrounds are available for supported GPT Image models. For `gpt-image-2` and `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, this support is in preview. When using `transparent`, set the output format to `png` or `webp`.|
|stream|boolean \| null|false|none|Stream partial image results as events.|
|partial_images|[PartialImages](#schemapartialimages)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_Eval">Eval</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaeval"></a>
<a id="schema_Eval"></a>
<a id="tocSeval"></a>
<a id="tocseval"></a>

```json
{
  "object": "eval",
  "id": "string",
  "name": "Chatbot effectiveness Evaluation",
  "data_source_config": {
    "type": "custom",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "item": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "label": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "label"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "item"
      ]
    }
  },
  "testing_criteria": [
    {
      "type": "label_model",
      "name": "string",
      "model": "string",
      "input": [
        {
          "role": "user",
          "content": "string",
          "type": "message"
        }
      ],
      "labels": [
        "string"
      ],
      "passing_labels": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "created_at": 0,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

An Eval object with a data source config and testing criteria.
An Eval represents a task to be done for your LLM integration.
Like:
 - Improve the quality of my chatbot
 - See how well my chatbot handles customer support
 - Check if o4-mini is better at my usecase than gpt-6-astra

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|true|none|The object type.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the evaluation.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the evaluation.|
|data_source_config|object|true|none|Configuration of data sources used in runs of the evaluation.|
|testing_criteria|[[EvalGraderLabelModel](#schemaevalgraderlabelmodel) \| [EvalGraderStringCheck](#schemaevalgraderstringcheck) \| [EvalGraderTextSimilarity](#schemaevalgradertextsimilarity) \| [EvalGraderPython](#schemaevalgraderpython) \| [EvalGraderScoreModel](#schemaevalgraderscoremodel)]|true|none|A list of testing criteria.|
|created_at|integer(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the eval was created.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|eval|

```json
  "content": "string",
  "type": "message"
}
```

A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take
precedence over instructions given with the `user` role. Messages with the
`assistant` role are presumed to have been generated by the model in previous
interactions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|string|true|none|The role of the message input. One of `user`, `assistant`, `system`, or<br>`developer`.<br>|
|content|[EvalItemContent](#schemaevalitemcontent)|true|none|Inputs to the model - can contain template strings. Supports text, output text, input images, and input audio, either as a single item or an array of items.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the message input. Always `message`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|user|
|role|assistant|
|role|system|
|role|developer|
|type|message|

A LogsDataSourceConfig which specifies the metadata property of your logs query.
This is usually metadata like `usecase=chatbot` or `prompt-version=v2`, etc.
The schema returned by this data source config is used to defined what variables are available in your evals.
`item` and `sample` are both defined when using this data source config.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of data source. Always `logs`.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|none|
|schema|object|true|none|The json schema for the run data source items.<br>Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|logs|

```json
  "beta": "auto",
  "batch_size": "auto",
  "learning_rate_multiplier": "auto",
  "n_epochs": "auto"
}
```

The hyperparameters used for the DPO fine-tuning job.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|beta|string \| number|false|none|The beta value for the DPO method. A higher beta value will increase the weight of the penalty between the policy and reference model.<br>|
|batch_size|string \| integer|false|none|Number of examples in each batch. A larger batch size means that model parameters are updated less frequently, but with lower variance.<br>|
|learning_rate_multiplier|string \| number|false|none|Scaling factor for the learning rate. A smaller learning rate may be useful to avoid overfitting.<br>|
|n_epochs|string \| integer|false|none|The number of epochs to train the model for. An epoch refers to one full cycle through the training dataset.<br>|

|compute_multiplier|string \| number|false|none|Multiplier on amount of compute used for exploring search space during training.<br>|

|eval_samples|string \| integer|false|none|Number of evaluation samples to generate per training step.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ImageGenTool">ImageGenTool</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "type": "image_generation",
  "model": "string",
  "quality": "auto",
  "size": "auto",
  "output_format": "png",
  "output_compression": 100,
  "moderation": "auto",
  "background": "auto",
  "input_fidelity": "high",
  "input_image_mask": {
    "image_url": "string",
    "file_id": "string"
  },
  "partial_images": 0,
  "action": "generate"
}
```

A tool that generates images using the GPT image models.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the image generation tool. Always `image_generation`.<br>|
|model|string|false|none|none|
|quality|string|false|none|The quality of the generated image. The GPT image models support `low`,<br>`medium`, and `high`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`,<br>including their `2026-09-08` snapshots, also support `xhigh` and `max`.<br>Default: `auto`.<br>|
|size|string|false|none|The size of the generated images. For `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, arbitrary resolutions are supported as `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings, for example `1536x864`. Width and height must both be divisible by 16 and the requested aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Resolutions above `2560x1440` are experimental, and the maximum supported resolution is `3840x2160`. The requested size must also satisfy the model's current pixel and edge limits. The standard sizes `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, and `1024x1536` are supported by the GPT image models; `auto` is supported for models that allow automatic sizing.|
|output_format|string|false|none|The output format of the generated image. One of `png`, `webp`, or<br>`jpeg`. Default: `png`.<br>|
|output_compression|integer|false|none|Compression level for the output image. Default: 100.<br>|
|moderation|string|false|none|Moderation level for the generated image. Default: `auto`.<br>|
|background|string|false|none|Set the background of the generated image. One of `transparent`, `opaque`,<br>or `auto`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including<br>their `2026-09-08` snapshots, support `opaque` and `transparent`<br>backgrounds. Transparent backgrounds are available for supported GPT Image<br>models. For `gpt-image-2` and `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, this support is in<br>preview. When using `transparent`, set the output format to `png` or `webp`.<br>Default: `auto`.<br>|
|input_fidelity|[InputFidelity](#schemainputfidelity) \| null|false|none|none|
|input_image_mask|object|false|none|Optional mask for inpainting. Contains `image_url`<br>(string, optional) and `file_id` (string, optional).<br>|
|partial_images|integer|false|none|Number of partial images to generate in streaming mode, from 0 (default value) to 3.<br>|
|action|[ImageGenActionEnum](#schemaimagegenactionenum)|false|none|Whether to generate a new image or edit an existing image. Default: `auto`.<br>|

|quality|xhigh|
|quality|max|

|moderation|low|

|action|auto|

Startup configuration for accepting an incoming Live SIP call. Follow the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) when writing frontend and backend instructions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|[ModelIdsLive](#schemamodelidslive)|true|none|The Live model to use for the accepted call.|
|instructions|[instructions](#schemainstructions)|false|none|none|
|audio|[LiveMediaSessionAudioParam](#schemalivemediasessionaudioparam)|false|none|Startup audio output configuration. SIP negotiates the media format; audio.format is only accepted for primary WebSockets. Voice cannot change after startup.|
|delegation|[delegation](#schemadelegation)|false|none|none|
|triggers|[triggers](#schematriggers)|false|none|At most one Decisions trigger per transcript event type. Triggers run independently of delegation. On update, omit triggers to keep the current configuration, send a list to replace it, or send an empty list to disable triggers.|
|store|[store](#schemastore)|false|none|Whether to store the session for later forking and recording download. Defaults to false for new sessions.|
|input|[input](#schemainput)|false|none|Ordered text-only history supplied before startup. Supports developer, user, and assistant messages with one text part each; at most 128 messages and a configured rendered-token limit (8,192 by default).|
|type|string|true|none|The session type. Always `live`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|live|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveClientEvent">LiveClientEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaliveclientevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "session.start",
  "event_id": "evt_start_001",
  "session": {
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "instructions": "Help the caller plan a restaurant reservation. Confirm details before booking.",
    "audio": {
      "format": {
        "type": "audio/pcm",
        "rate": 24000
      },
      "output": {
        "voice": "marin"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "type": "client"
    }
  }
}
```

Client events for Live. Initialize a primary WebSocket with session.start and wait for session.started. WebRTC creation already starts the session. Audio append is primary WebSocket-only. See the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) before writing frontend instructions and delegation policies.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionStartEvent](#schemalivesessionstartevent)|false|none|Start a Live session on a primary WebSocket. Send this event before other commands and wait for `session.started`.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUpdateParam](#schemalivesessionupdateparam)|false|none|Update the delegation settings or transcript triggers of an active Live session. The server acknowledges accepted changes with `session.updated`.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioAppendEvent](#schemaliveinputaudioappendevent)|false|none|Send audio to a Live session over its primary WebSocket. WebRTC and SIP sessions send audio over their media transport.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioMuteParam](#schemaliveinputaudiomuteparam)|false|none|Mute audio input to the Live model without closing the session. The server acknowledges with `session.input_audio.muted`.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioUnmuteParam](#schemaliveinputaudiounmuteparam)|false|none|Resume audio input to a Live model after muting it. The server acknowledges with `session.input_audio.unmuted`. An active audio fixture still pauses inference until playback finishes.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayParam](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplayparam)|false|none|Play one complete audio fixture through the session output. Send this event over the primary WebSocket or a server sideband. Audio must be raw mono PCM16 little-endian at 24 kHz, regardless of the session audio format, and at most 30 seconds. The entire payload is validated before model speech is interrupted and input is muted. Only one fixture can be active. fixture.playing acknowledges acceptance and fixture.played reports server mixer drain. These notifications are not exact transport-media boundaries. Input arriving during playback is dropped and not replayed.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInstructionsAppendParam](#schemaliveinstructionsappendparam)|false|none|Append developer instructions to the Live conversation while it is running, optionally associating them with an existing client delegation. Rejected while an audio fixture is active. These instructions remain in conversation history through compaction and are included in future backend delegations. For external audio, describe content already delivered so the assistant does not repeat it.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveThinkingAppendParam](#schemalivethinkingappendparam)|false|none|Provide silent reasoning or progress context to the Live model, optionally for an existing client delegation. Rejected while an audio fixture is active.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveCommentaryAppendParam](#schemalivecommentaryappendparam)|false|none|Provide context the Live model can communicate to the user, optionally for an existing client delegation. Rejected while an audio fixture is active.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionCreateParam](#schemalivedecisioncreateparam)|false|none|Evaluate the configured questions using the current conversation and Decision inputs. Reusing an event_id is rejected for the lifetime of the session.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemCreateParam](#schemalivedecisionitemcreateparam)|false|none|Append an input item for future decisions without starting an evaluation or changing Live voice context.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemDeleteParam](#schemalivedecisionitemdeleteparam)|false|none|Delete an input item from future decisions without starting an evaluation or changing Live voice context.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseItemCreateParam](#schemaliveresponseitemcreateparam)|false|none|Add an input item to the Live session’s Responses backend. Requires Responses delegation; use `response.create` to request a response.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseCreateParam](#schemaliveresponsecreateparam)|false|none|Request a response from the Live session’s Responses backend, or continue a delegated response waiting for tool results. Requires Responses delegation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionCloseParam](#schemalivesessioncloseparam)|false|none|Request that the Live session close. The terminal `session.closed` event contains the close reason and final usage.|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveCreateRequest">LiveCreateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalivecreaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveCreateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSlivecreaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocslivecreaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "session": {
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "instructions": "string",
    "audio": {
      "output": {
        "voice": "string"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "acknowledgement_delay_ms": 0,
      "type": "client"
    },
    "triggers": [
      {
        "type": "decisions",
        "event_type": "session.input_transcript.delta",
        "decisions": {
          "questions": [
            {
              "type": "choice",
              "name": "string",
              "instructions": "string",
              "choices": [
                {
                  "value": "string",
                  "description": "string"
                },
                {
                  "value": "string",
                  "description": "string"
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "store": true,
    "input": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "type": "message",
        "status": "incomplete",
        "role": "developer",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "input_text",
            "text": "string"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "client": {
      "data_channel": {
        "allowed_client_events": "all",
        "allowed_server_events": "all"
      }
    }
  },
  "transport": {
    "type": "webrtc",
    "sdp": "string"
  }
}
```

Create a Live WebRTC session with JSON session configuration and an SDP offer. Follow the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) before choosing frontend and backend instructions. The request starts the session; do not send session.start on the data channel.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|[LiveMediaSessionCreateParams](#schemalivemediasessioncreateparams)|true|none|Startup configuration for the Live session.|
|transport|[LiveWebRTCTransport](#schemalivewebrtctransport)|true|none|WebRTC transport with the browser's SDP offer.|

Send this event over the primary WebSocket or a server sideband. Audio must be raw mono PCM16 little-endian at 24 kHz, regardless of the session audio format, and at most 30 seconds. <h2 id="tocS_LiveForkServerEvent">LiveForkServerEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaliveforkserverevent"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveForkServerEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSliveforkserverevent"></a>
<a id="tocsliveforkserverevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "session.started",
  "event_id": "evt_started_001",
  "client_event_id": "evt_start_001",
  "session": {
    "id": "live_abc123",
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "status": "active",
    "expires_at": 1788555600,
    "instructions": "Help the caller plan a restaurant reservation. Confirm details before booking.",
    "input": [],
    "audio": {
      "format": {
        "type": "audio/pcm",
        "rate": 24000
      },
      "output": {
        "voice": "marin"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "type": "client"
    }
  }
}
```

Server events for Live. Response lifecycle events are wrapped inside response.event; dispatch the nested event by its full type and tolerate new response event types. Follow the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) when designing the conversation and delegation policy.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionStarted](#schemalivesessionstarted)|false|none|Returned when a Live session has started. Contains the resolved session configuration, including server defaults.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUpdated](#schemalivesessionupdated)|false|none|Returned when a Live session update is accepted. Contains the resolved session configuration after the update.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioMuted](#schemaliveinputaudiomuted)|false|none|Acknowledges a session.input_audio.mute command. An independent input mute sends silence to the model and preserves sideband audio reflection. Fixture playback does not emit this event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioUnmuted](#schemaliveinputaudiounmuted)|false|none|Acknowledges a session.input_audio.unmute command, removing the independent input mute. An active audio fixture still pauses inference until playback finishes. Fixture playback does not emit this event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlaying](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplaying)|false|none|The existing playback path has accepted the validated audio fixture. This acknowledgment does not identify when the listener receives the first sample. The optional client_event_id echoes the play command.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayed](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplayed)|false|none|The complete audio fixture has drained from the server mixer and normal inference has resumed. Transport buffers may still contain audio; this event does not prove listener-side completion. The optional client_event_id echoes the play command. This event is not emitted for canceled or failed playback.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInstructionsAppended](#schemaliveinstructionsappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.instructions.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the appended instructions without guaranteeing that the model has acted on them.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveThinkingAppended](#schemalivethinkingappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.thinking.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the added reasoning context without guaranteeing any spoken output.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveCommentaryAppended](#schemalivecommentaryappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.commentary.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the added commentary without guaranteeing exact wording or completed audio playback.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioAppend](#schemaliveinputaudioappend)|false|none|Input audio received from the primary transport and reflected to a Live sideband connection before model-input muting.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioDelta](#schemaliveoutputaudiodelta)|false|none|An audio chunk generated by the Live model. Decode and play primary WebSocket chunks in delivery order using the configured session audio format. Sideband connections receive reflected output audio with timestamps.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputTranscriptDelta](#schemaliveinputtranscriptdelta)|false|none|A transcript fragment for user input audio in the Live session. Accumulate fragments in delivery order; these events do not define complete turns or include a transcript-done event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputTranscriptDelta](#schemaliveoutputtranscriptdelta)|false|none|A transcript fragment for assistant output audio in the Live session. Accumulate fragments in delivery order; these events do not define complete turns or include a transcript-done event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDelegationCreated](#schemalivedelegationcreated)|false|none|Returned when the Live model delegates work to your application, Responses, or Decisions. Contains delegation metadata and the position on the session timeline where the work was delegated.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionEvent](#schemalivedecisionevent)|false|none|A Decision API event for a Live delegation or transcript trigger. For a trigger, source_event_id identifies the transcript delta that caused this evaluation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemCreated](#schemalivedecisionitemcreated)|false|none|An input item was appended for future decisions.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemDeleted](#schemalivedecisionitemdeleted)|false|none|An input item was removed from future decisions.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseEvent](#schemaliveresponseevent)|false|none|A streaming Responses API event from a backend delegated to by the Live session. Use the outer delegation_id to associate the nested stream with its Live delegation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUsageUpdated](#schemalivesessionusageupdated)|false|none|Reports cumulative Live audio usage and, when available, the most recent context-window usage. Delegated Responses token usage is reported separately in response.event events.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionClosed](#schemalivesessionclosed)|false|none|Returned after the Live session finishes finalizing, with the close reason, final session snapshot, and cumulative audio usage. A connection closing without this event does not confirm successful finalization.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveErrorEvent](#schemaliveerrorevent)|false|none|Reports an error in the Live session, such as an invalid client command. Use error.client_event_id, when present, to identify the command that caused the error.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInfoEvent](#schemaliveinfoevent)|false|none|An informational notice about the Live session, such as the event permissions applied to a frontend data channel.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFReceived](#schemalivetransportdtmfreceived)|false|none|A SIP DTMF keypress received from the caller. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFSent](#schemalivetransportdtmfsent)|false|none|A SIP DTMF keypress successfully sent to the SIP trunk. Delivered only to sideband observers; this is not a client command.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportRinging](#schemalivetransportringing)|false|none|The outbound SIP provider leg is ringing or providing early media. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportAnswered](#schemalivetransportanswered)|false|none|The outbound SIP provider leg answered and media is established. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportFailed](#schemalivetransportfailed)|false|none|An asynchronous outbound SIP setup failure. Delivered only to sideband observers.|

Startup configuration for a Live media session. Follow the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) when writing frontend instructions and the backend prompt under delegation.responses.instructions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|[ModelIdsLive](#schemamodelidslive)|true|none|The Live model. Required in the session configuration for every transport; do not pass it as a URL query parameter.|
|instructions|[instructions](#schemainstructions)|false|none|none|
|audio|[LiveMediaSessionAudioParam](#schemalivemediasessionaudioparam)|false|none|Startup audio configuration. WebRTC and SIP negotiate their audio format on the media transport.|
|delegation|[delegation](#schemadelegation)|false|none|none|
|triggers|[triggers](#schematriggers)|false|none|At most one Decisions trigger per transcript event type. Triggers run independently of delegation. On update, omit triggers to keep the current configuration, send a list to replace it, or send an empty list to disable triggers.|
|store|[store](#schemastore)|false|none|Whether to store the session for later forking and recording download. Defaults to false for new sessions.|
|input|[input](#schemainput)|false|none|Ordered text-only history supplied before startup. Supports developer, user, and assistant messages with one text part each; at most 128 messages and a configured rendered-token limit (8,192 by default).|
|client|[LiveClientConfigParam](#schemaliveclientconfigparam)|false|none|Startup-only capabilities for an untrusted frontend attached to a unified WebRTC session. Trusted sideband connections are unaffected.|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveSIPTransport">LiveSIPTransport</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalivesiptransport"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveSIPTransport"></a>
<a id="tocSlivesiptransport"></a>
<a id="tocslivesiptransport"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "sip",
  "destination": "+14155550123",
  "trunk": {
    "provider_url": "sips:sip.example.com:5061",
    "auth": {
      "type": "digest",
      "username": "string",
      "password": "string"
    },
    "caller_number": "+14155550100"
  }
}
```

Place an outbound SIP call using your provider's trunk. Outbound SIP calling must be enabled for your organization. The trunk must support TLS signaling, Opus audio, and SDES-SRTP media. See [Telephony and SIP](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-sip?api=live#place-an-outbound-call).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The transport used for the Live session. Always `sip`.|

```json
{

    "type": "digest",
```

SIP trunk configuration supplied for this call. Keep trunk credentials on your server. The creation response does not return this configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider_url|string|true|none|Provider endpoint in the form `sips:host[:port][;transport=tcp]`. The default port is 5061. IPv6 addresses must be bracketed. TLS signaling is required; plaintext SIP is not supported. Do not include userinfo, a path, URI headers, or other URI parameters. Local hostnames and literal private, loopback, link-local, unspecified, multicast, and broadcast IP addresses are rejected.|
|auth|[LiveSIPTrunkAuth](#schemalivesiptrunkauth)|true|none|Credentials for SIP Digest authentication with your trunk provider.|
|caller_number|string|true|none|Caller phone number in E.164 format to use in the SIP From header.|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveServerEvent">LiveServerEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaliveserverevent"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveServerEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSliveserverevent"></a>
<a id="tocsliveserverevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "session.started",
  "event_id": "evt_started_001",
  "client_event_id": "evt_start_001",
  "session": {
    "id": "live_abc123",
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "status": "active",
    "expires_at": 1788555600,
    "instructions": "Help the caller plan a restaurant reservation. Confirm details before booking.",
    "input": [],
    "audio": {
      "format": {
        "type": "audio/pcm",
        "rate": 24000
      },
      "output": {
        "voice": "marin"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "type": "client"
    }
  }
}
```

Server events for Live. Response lifecycle events are wrapped inside response.event; dispatch the nested event by its full type and tolerate new response event types. Follow the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) when designing the conversation and delegation policy.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionStarted](#schemalivesessionstarted)|false|none|Returned when a Live session has started. Contains the resolved session configuration, including server defaults.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUpdated](#schemalivesessionupdated)|false|none|Returned when a Live session update is accepted. Contains the resolved session configuration after the update.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioMuted](#schemaliveinputaudiomuted)|false|none|Acknowledges a session.input_audio.mute command. An independent input mute sends silence to the model and preserves sideband audio reflection. Fixture playback does not emit this event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioUnmuted](#schemaliveinputaudiounmuted)|false|none|Acknowledges a session.input_audio.unmute command, removing the independent input mute. An active audio fixture still pauses inference until playback finishes. Fixture playback does not emit this event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlaying](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplaying)|false|none|The existing playback path has accepted the validated audio fixture. This acknowledgment does not identify when the listener receives the first sample. The optional client_event_id echoes the play command.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayed](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplayed)|false|none|The complete audio fixture has drained from the server mixer and normal inference has resumed. Transport buffers may still contain audio; this event does not prove listener-side completion. The optional client_event_id echoes the play command. This event is not emitted for canceled or failed playback.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInstructionsAppended](#schemaliveinstructionsappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.instructions.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the appended instructions without guaranteeing that the model has acted on them.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveThinkingAppended](#schemalivethinkingappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.thinking.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the added reasoning context without guaranteeing any spoken output.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveCommentaryAppended](#schemalivecommentaryappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.commentary.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the added commentary without guaranteeing exact wording or completed audio playback.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioAppend](#schemaliveinputaudioappend)|false|none|Input audio received from the primary transport and reflected to a Live sideband connection before model-input muting.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioDelta](#schemaliveoutputaudiodelta)|false|none|An audio chunk generated by the Live model. Decode and play primary WebSocket chunks in delivery order using the configured session audio format. Sideband connections receive reflected output audio with timestamps.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputTranscriptDelta](#schemaliveinputtranscriptdelta)|false|none|A transcript fragment for user input audio in the Live session. Accumulate fragments in delivery order; these events do not define complete turns or include a transcript-done event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputTranscriptDelta](#schemaliveoutputtranscriptdelta)|false|none|A transcript fragment for assistant output audio in the Live session. Accumulate fragments in delivery order; these events do not define complete turns or include a transcript-done event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDelegationCreated](#schemalivedelegationcreated)|false|none|Returned when the Live model delegates work to your application, Responses, or Decisions. Contains delegation metadata and the position on the session timeline where the work was delegated.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionEvent](#schemalivedecisionevent)|false|none|A Decision API event for a Live delegation or transcript trigger. For a trigger, source_event_id identifies the transcript delta that caused this evaluation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemCreated](#schemalivedecisionitemcreated)|false|none|An input item was appended for future decisions.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemDeleted](#schemalivedecisionitemdeleted)|false|none|An input item was removed from future decisions.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseEvent](#schemaliveresponseevent)|false|none|A streaming Responses API event from a backend delegated to by the Live session. Use the outer delegation_id to associate the nested stream with its Live delegation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUsageUpdated](#schemalivesessionusageupdated)|false|none|Reports cumulative Live audio usage and, when available, the most recent context-window usage. Delegated Responses token usage is reported separately in response.event events.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionClosed](#schemalivesessionclosed)|false|none|Returned after the Live session finishes finalizing, with the close reason, final session snapshot, and cumulative audio usage. A connection closing without this event does not confirm successful finalization.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveErrorEvent](#schemaliveerrorevent)|false|none|Reports an error in the Live session, such as an invalid client command. Use error.client_event_id, when present, to identify the command that caused the error.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInfoEvent](#schemaliveinfoevent)|false|none|An informational notice about the Live session, such as the event permissions applied to a frontend data channel.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFReceived](#schemalivetransportdtmfreceived)|false|none|A SIP DTMF keypress received from the caller. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFSent](#schemalivetransportdtmfsent)|false|none|A SIP DTMF keypress successfully sent to the SIP trunk. Delivered only to sideband observers; this is not a client command.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportRinging](#schemalivetransportringing)|false|none|The outbound SIP provider leg is ringing or providing early media. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportAnswered](#schemalivetransportanswered)|false|none|The outbound SIP provider leg answered and media is established. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportFailed](#schemalivetransportfailed)|false|none|An asynchronous outbound SIP setup failure. Delivered only to sideband observers.|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveSessionCreateRequest">LiveSessionCreateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalivesessioncreaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveSessionCreateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSlivesessioncreaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocslivesessioncreaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "session": {
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "instructions": "string",
    "audio": {
      "output": {
        "voice": "string"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "acknowledgement_delay_ms": 0,
      "type": "client"
    },
    "triggers": [
      {
        "type": "decisions",
        "event_type": "session.input_transcript.delta",
        "decisions": {
          "questions": [
            {
              "type": "choice",
              "name": "string",
              "instructions": "string",
              "choices": [
                {
                  "value": "string",
                  "description": "string"
                },
                {
                  "value": "string",
                  "description": "string"
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "store": true,
    "input": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "type": "message",
        "status": "incomplete",
        "role": "developer",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "input_text",
            "text": "string"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "client": {
      "data_channel": {
        "allowed_client_events": "all",
        "allowed_server_events": "all"
      }
    }
  },
  "transport": {
    "type": "webrtc",
    "sdp": "string"
  }
}
```

Create a Live session with a WebRTC SDP offer or place an outbound SIP call. Follow the [Live prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-prompting) before choosing frontend and backend instructions. The request starts the session; do not send session.start again on the data channel or sideband.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|[LiveMediaSessionCreateParams](#schemalivemediasessioncreateparams)|true|none|Startup configuration for the Live session.|
|transport|[LiveWebRTCTransport](#schemalivewebrtctransport) \| [LiveSIPTransport](#schemalivesiptransport)|true|none|WebRTC transport with an SDP offer, or SIP transport with a destination and per-call trunk credentials.|

The created Live session and its transport. WebRTC creation returns 201 Created with an SDP answer. Outbound SIP creation returns 201 Created after initialization, before the callee necessarily answers, without SDP or trunk credentials.

For SIP, attach a sideband using session.id to receive transport.ringing, transport.answered, and transport.failed notifications.|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveSidebandClientEvent">LiveSidebandClientEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalivesidebandclientevent"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveSidebandClientEvent"></a>

<a id="tocslivesidebandclientevent"></a>

