```json
  "type": "session.update",
  "event_id": "evt_update_001",
  "session": {
    "delegation": {
      "type": "responses",
      "responses": {
        "instructions": "Check restaurant availability. Ask before confirming a booking.",
        "max_output_tokens": 1024
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Client events accepted by an attached Live sideband WebSocket. The session has already started. Send input audio over the primary connection.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUpdateParam](#schemalivesessionupdateparam)|false|none|Update the delegation settings or transcript triggers of an active Live session. The server acknowledges accepted changes with `session.updated`.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioMuteParam](#schemaliveinputaudiomuteparam)|false|none|Mute audio input to the Live model without closing the session. The server acknowledges with `session.input_audio.muted`.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioUnmuteParam](#schemaliveinputaudiounmuteparam)|false|none|Resume audio input to a Live model after muting it. The server acknowledges with `session.input_audio.unmuted`. An active audio fixture still pauses inference until playback finishes.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayParam](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplayparam)|false|none|Play one complete audio fixture through the session output. Send this event over the primary WebSocket or a server sideband. Audio must be raw mono PCM16 little-endian at 24 kHz, regardless of the session audio format, and at most 30 seconds. The entire payload is validated before model speech is interrupted and input is muted. Only one fixture can be active. fixture.playing acknowledges acceptance and fixture.played reports server mixer drain. These notifications are not exact transport-media boundaries. Input arriving during playback is dropped and not replayed.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFSendParam](#schemalivetransportdtmfsendparam)|false|none|Send one DTMF keypress to the SIP trunk through a Live sideband connection. This command is supported only for SIP calls. A successful send emits `transport.dtmf.sent` on sideband. If you provide `event_id`, the success notification includes it as `client_event_id`; a failure includes it as `error.client_event_id`. Send separate events for multiple keypresses.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInstructionsAppendParam](#schemaliveinstructionsappendparam)|false|none|Append developer instructions to the Live conversation while it is running, optionally associating them with an existing client delegation. Rejected while an audio fixture is active. These instructions remain in conversation history through compaction and are included in future backend delegations. For external audio, describe content already delivered so the assistant does not repeat it.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveThinkingAppendParam](#schemalivethinkingappendparam)|false|none|Provide silent reasoning or progress context to the Live model, optionally for an existing client delegation. Rejected while an audio fixture is active.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveCommentaryAppendParam](#schemalivecommentaryappendparam)|false|none|Provide context the Live model can communicate to the user, optionally for an existing client delegation. Rejected while an audio fixture is active.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionCreateParam](#schemalivedecisioncreateparam)|false|none|Evaluate the configured questions using the current conversation and Decision inputs. Reusing an event_id is rejected for the lifetime of the session.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemCreateParam](#schemalivedecisionitemcreateparam)|false|none|Append an input item for future decisions without starting an evaluation or changing Live voice context.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemDeleteParam](#schemalivedecisionitemdeleteparam)|false|none|Delete an input item from future decisions without starting an evaluation or changing Live voice context.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseItemCreateParam](#schemaliveresponseitemcreateparam)|false|none|Add an input item to the Live session’s Responses backend. Requires Responses delegation; use `response.create` to request a response.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseCreateParam](#schemaliveresponsecreateparam)|false|none|Request a response from the Live session’s Responses backend, or continue a delegated response waiting for tool results. Requires Responses delegation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionCloseParam](#schemalivesessioncloseparam)|false|none|Request that the Live session close. The terminal `session.closed` event contains the close reason and final usage.|

<h2 id="tocS_MCPTool">MCPTool</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamcptool"></a>
<a id="schema_MCPTool"></a>
<a id="tocSmcptool"></a>
<a id="tocsmcptool"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "mcp",
  "server_label": "string",
  "server_url": "http://example.com",
  "connector_id": "connector_dropbox",
  "tunnel_id": "string",
  "authorization": "string",
  "server_description": "string",
  "headers": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "allowed_tools": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_callers": [
    "direct"
  ],
  "require_approval": "always",
  "defer_loading": true
}
```

Give the model access to additional tools via remote Model Context Protocol
(MCP) servers. [Learn more about MCP](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the MCP tool. Always `mcp`.|
|server_label|string|true|none|A label for this MCP server, used to identify it in tool calls.<br>|
|server_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL for the MCP server. One of `server_url`, `connector_id`, or<br>`tunnel_id` must be provided.<br>|
|connector_id|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Identifier for service connectors, like those available in ChatGPT. One of<br>`server_url`, `connector_id`, or `tunnel_id` must be provided. Learn more<br>about service connectors [here](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp#connectors).<br><br>This field is deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026.<br>Use `server_url` to connect to a remote MCP server, or `tunnel_id` to<br>connect through a Secure MCP Tunnel.<br><br>Currently supported `connector_id` values are:<br><br>- Dropbox: `connector_dropbox`<br>- Gmail: `connector_gmail`<br>- Google Calendar: `connector_googlecalendar`<br>- Google Drive: `connector_googledrive`<br>- Microsoft Teams: `connector_microsoftteams`<br>- Outlook Calendar: `connector_outlookcalendar`<br>- Outlook Email: `connector_outlookemail`<br>- SharePoint: `connector_sharepoint`<br>|
|tunnel_id|string|false|none|The Secure MCP Tunnel ID to use instead of a direct server URL. One of<br>`server_url`, `connector_id`, or `tunnel_id` must be provided.<br>|
|authorization|string|false|none|An OAuth access token that can be used with a remote MCP server, either<br>with a custom MCP server URL or a service connector. Your application<br>must handle the OAuth authorization flow and provide the token here.<br>|
|server_description|string|false|none|Optional description of the MCP server, used to provide more context.<br>|
|headers|object \| null|false|none|none|
|allowed_tools|[string] \| [MCPToolFilter](#schemamcptoolfilter) \| null|false|none|none|
|allowed_callers|[[CallableToolAllowedCaller](#schemacallabletoolallowedcaller)] \| null|false|none|none|
|require_approval|object \| string \| null|false|none|none|
|defer_loading|boolean|false|none|Whether this MCP tool is deferred and discovered via tool search.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|mcp|
|connector_id|connector_dropbox|
|connector_id|connector_gmail|
|connector_id|connector_googlecalendar|
|connector_id|connector_googledrive|
|connector_id|connector_microsoftteams|
|connector_id|connector_outlookcalendar|
|connector_id|connector_outlookemail|
|connector_id|connector_sharepoint|


Labels an `assistant` message as intermediate commentary (`commentary`) or the final answer (`final_answer`).
For models like `gpt-5.3-codex` and beyond, when sending follow-up requests, preserve and resend
phase on all assistant messages — dropping it can degrade performance. Not used for user messages.

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "bytes": 0,
  "created_at": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "filename": "string",
  "object": "file",
  "purpose": "assistants",
  "status": "uploaded",
  "status_details": "string"
}
```

The `File` object represents a document that has been uploaded to OpenAI.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The file identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.|
|bytes|integer \| null|true|none|The size of the file, in bytes. In a completed file upload response, this can<br>be null when the file size is not yet available.<br>|
|created_at|integer(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the file was created.|
|expires_at|integer(unixtime)|false|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the file will expire. In a<br>completed file upload response, this can be null when no expiry is set.<br>|
|filename|string|true|none|The name of the file.|
|object|string|true|none|The object type, which is always `file`.|
|purpose|string|true|none|The intended purpose of the file. Supported values are `assistants`, `assistants_output`, `batch`, `batch_output`, `fine-tune`, `fine-tune-results`, `vision`, and `user_data`.|
|status|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. The current status of the file, which can be either `uploaded`, `processed`, or `error`.|
|status_details|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. For details on why a fine-tuning training file failed validation, see the `error` field on `fine_tuning.job`. Completed file upload responses can return null when these details are unset.|

|purpose|vision|
|purpose|user_data|
|status|uploaded|
|status|processed|
|status|error|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemCreate">RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemCreate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemcreate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemCreate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemcreate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemcreate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.create",
  "previous_item_id": "string",
  "item": {
    "id": "string",
    "object": "realtime.item",
    "type": "message",
    "status": "completed",
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Add a new Item to the Conversation's context, including messages, function 
calls, and function call responses. This event can be used both to populate a 
"history" of the conversation and to add new items mid-stream, but has the 
current limitation that it cannot populate assistant audio messages.

If successful, the server will respond with a `conversation.item.created` 
event, otherwise an `error` event will be sent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.create`.|
|previous_item_id|string|false|none|The ID of the preceding item after which the new item will be inserted. <br>If not set, the new item will be appended to the end of the conversation.<br>If set to `root`, the new item will be added to the beginning of the conversation.<br>If set to an existing ID, it allows an item to be inserted mid-conversation. If the<br>ID cannot be found, an error will be returned and the item will not be added.<br>|
|item|[RealtimeConversationItem](#schemarealtimeconversationitem)|true|none|A single item within a Realtime conversation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.create|

|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the item to delete.|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemRetrieve">RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemRetrieve</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemretrieve"></a>

```json

  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.retrieve",
  "item_id": "string"
}
```

Send this event when you want to retrieve the server's representation of a specific item in the conversation history. This is useful, for example, to inspect user audio after noise cancellation and VAD.
The server will respond with a `conversation.item.retrieved` event, 
unless the item does not exist in the conversation history, in which case the 
server will respond with an error.

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemTruncate">RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemTruncate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemtruncate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemTruncate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemtruncate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaclienteventconversationitemtruncate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.truncate",
  "item_id": "string",
  "content_index": 0,
  "audio_end_ms": 0
}
```

Send this event to truncate a previous assistant message’s audio. The server 
will produce audio faster than realtime, so this event is useful when the user 
interrupts to truncate audio that has already been sent to the client but not 
yet played. This will synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with 
the client's playback.

Truncating audio will delete the server-side text transcript to ensure there 
is not text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.

If successful, the server will respond with a `conversation.item.truncated` 
event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.truncate`.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the assistant message item to truncate. Only assistant message <br>items can be truncated.<br>|
|content_index|integer|true|none|The index of the content part to truncate. Set this to 0.|
|audio_end_ms|integer|true|none|Inclusive duration up to which audio is truncated, in milliseconds. If <br>the audio_end_ms is greater than the actual audio duration, the server <br>will respond with an error.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.truncate|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend">RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.append",
  "audio": "string"
}
```

Send this event to append audio bytes to the input audio buffer. The audio 
buffer is temporary storage you can write to and later commit. In Server VAD 
mode, the audio buffer is used to detect speech and the server will decide 
when to commit. When Server VAD is disabled, you must commit the audio buffer
manually.

The client may choose how much audio to place in each event up to a maximum 
of 15 MiB, for example streaming smaller chunks from the client may allow the 
VAD to be more responsive. Unlike made other client events, the server will 
not send a confirmation response to this event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.append`.|
|audio|string|true|none|Base64-encoded audio bytes. This must be in the format specified by the <br>`input_audio_format` field in the session configuration.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.append|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferCommit">RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferCommit</h2>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.commit"
}
```

Send this event to commit the user input audio buffer, which will create a 
new user message item in the conversation. This event will produce an error 
if the input audio buffer is empty. When in Server VAD mode, the client does 
not need to send this event, the server will commit the audio buffer 
automatically.

Committing the input audio buffer will trigger input audio transcription 
(if enabled in session configuration), but it will not create a response 
from the model. The server will respond with an `input_audio_buffer.committed` 
event.

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCreate">RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCreate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaclienteventresponsecreate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCreate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaclienteventresponsecreate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaclienteventresponsecreate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "response.create",
  "response": {
    "modalities": [
      "text"
    ],
    "instructions": "string",
    "voice": "ash",
    "output_audio_format": "pcm16",
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_output_tokens": 0,
    "conversation": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "prompt": {
      "id": "string",
      "version": "string",
      "variables": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    },
    "input": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "object": "realtime.item",
        "type": "message",
        "status": "completed",
        "role": "system",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "input_text",
            "text": "string"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

This event instructs the server to create a Response, which means triggering 
model inference. When in Server VAD mode, the server will create Responses 
automatically.

A Response will include at least one Item, and may have two, in which case 
the second will be a function call. These Items will be appended to the 
conversation history.

The server will respond with a `response.created` event, events for Items 
and content created, and finally a `response.done` event to indicate the 
Response is complete.

The `response.create` event can optionally include inference configuration like 
`instructions`, and `temperature`. These fields will override the Session's 
configuration for this Response only.

Responses can be created out-of-band of the default Conversation, meaning that they can
have arbitrary input, and it's possible to disable writing the output to the Conversation.
Only one Response can write to the default Conversation at a time, but otherwise multiple
Responses can be created in parallel.

Clients can set `conversation` to `none` to create a Response that does not write to the default
Conversation. Arbitrary input can be provided with the `input` field, which is an array accepting
raw Items and references to existing Items.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `response.create`.|
|response|[RealtimeBetaResponseCreateParams](#schemarealtimebetaresponsecreateparams)|false|none|Create a new Realtime response with these parameters|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.create|

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "session.update",
  "session": {
    "client_secret": {
      "value": "string",
      "expires_at": 0
    },
    "modalities": [
      "text"

    "instructions": "string",

    "output_audio_format": "string",

      "model": "string"
    },
    "speed": 1,
    "tracing": "auto",
    "turn_detection": {
      "type": "string",
      "threshold": 0,
      "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
      "silence_duration_ms": 0
    },

        "type": "function",

    "truncation": "auto",

        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Send this event to update the session’s default configuration.
The client may send this event at any time to update any field,
except for `voice`. However, note that once a session has been
initialized with a particular `model`, it can’t be changed to
another model using `session.update`.

When the server receives a `session.update`, it will respond
with a `session.updated` event showing the full, effective configuration.
Only the fields that are present are updated. To clear a field like
`instructions`, pass an empty string.

|session|[RealtimeSessionCreateRequest](#schemarealtimesessioncreaterequest)|true|none|A new Realtime session configuration, with an ephemeral key. Default TTL<br>for keys is one minute.<br>|

Voice cannot be changed during<br>the session once the model has responded with audio at least once.<br>Custom voices must be created from audio samples. |max_output_tokens|integer \| string|false|none|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to<br>limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a<br>given model. Defaults to `inf`.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemCreated">RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemCreated</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaservereventconversationitemcreated"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemCreated"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaservereventconversationitemcreated"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaservereventconversationitemcreated"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.created",
  "previous_item_id": "string",
  "item": {
    "id": "string",
    "object": "realtime.item",
    "type": "message",
    "status": "completed",
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Returned when a conversation item is created. There are several scenarios that produce this event:
  - The server is generating a Response, which if successful will produce
    either one or two Items, which will be of type `message`
    (role `assistant`) or type `function_call`.
  - The input audio buffer has been committed, either by the client or the
    server (in `server_vad` mode). The server will take the content of the
    input audio buffer and add it to a new user message Item.
  - The client has sent a `conversation.item.create` event to add a new Item
    to the Conversation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.created`.|
|previous_item_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|item|[RealtimeConversationItem](#schemarealtimeconversationitem)|true|none|A single item within a Realtime conversation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.created|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted">RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed",
  "item_id": "string",
  "content_index": 0,
  "transcript": "string",
  "languages": [
    {
      "code": "string"
    }
  ],
  "logprobs": [
    {
      "token": "string",
      "logprob": 0,
      "bytes": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "type": "tokens",
    "input_tokens": 0,
    "input_token_details": {
      "text_tokens": 0,
      "audio_tokens": 0
    },
    "output_tokens": 0,
    "total_tokens": 0
  }
}
```

This event is the output of audio transcription for user audio written to the
user audio buffer. Transcription begins when the input audio buffer is
committed by the client or server (in `server_vad` mode). Transcription runs
asynchronously with Response creation, so this event may come before or after
the Response events.

Realtime API models accept audio natively, and thus input transcription is a
separate process run on a separate ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) model.
The transcript may diverge somewhat from the model's interpretation, and
should be treated as a rough guide.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be<br>`conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed`.<br>|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user message item containing the audio.|
|content_index|integer|true|none|The index of the content part containing the audio.|
|transcript|string|true|none|The transcribed text.|
|languages|[[TranscriptionLanguage](#schematranscriptionlanguage)]|false|none|The languages detected in the audio. Returned by `gpt-transcribe`. An empty array indicates that no language could be reliably detected.<br>|
|logprobs|[[LogProbProperties](#schemalogprobproperties)] \| null|false|none|none|
|usage|object|true|none|Usage statistics for the transcription.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemTruncated">RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemTruncated</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaservereventconversationitemtruncated"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemTruncated"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaservereventconversationitemtruncated"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaservereventconversationitemtruncated"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.truncated",
  "item_id": "string",
  "content_index": 0,
  "audio_end_ms": 0
}
```

Returned when an earlier assistant audio message item is truncated by the 
client with a `conversation.item.truncate` event. This event is used to 
synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with the client's playback.

This action will truncate the audio and remove the server-side text transcript 
to ensure there is no text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.truncated`.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the assistant message item that was truncated.|
|content_index|integer|true|none|The index of the content part that was truncated.|
|audio_end_ms|integer|true|none|The duration up to which the audio was truncated, in milliseconds.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.truncated|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted">RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.speech_started",
  "audio_start_ms": 0,
  "item_id": "string"
}
```

Sent by the server when in `server_vad` mode to indicate that speech has been 
detected in the audio buffer. This can happen any time audio is added to the 
buffer (unless speech is already detected). The client may want to use this 
event to interrupt audio playback or provide visual feedback to the user. 

The client should expect to receive a `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event 
when speech stops. The `item_id` property is the ID of the user message item 
that will be created when speech stops and will also be included in the 
`input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event (unless the client manually commits 
the audio buffer during VAD activation).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.speech_started`.|
|audio_start_ms|integer|true|none|Milliseconds from the start of all audio written to the buffer during the <br>session when speech was first detected. This will correspond to the <br>beginning of audio sent to the model, and thus includes the <br>`prefix_padding_ms` configured in the Session.<br>|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user message item that will be created when speech stops.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.speech_started|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStopped">RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStopped</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimebetaservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstopped"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStopped"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimebetaservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstopped"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimebetaservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstopped"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped",
  "audio_end_ms": 0,
  "item_id": "string"
}
```

Returned in `server_vad` mode when the server detects the end of speech in 
the audio buffer. The server will also send an `conversation.item.created` 
event with the user message item that is created from the audio buffer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped`.|
|audio_end_ms|integer|true|none|Milliseconds since the session started when speech stopped. This will <br>correspond to the end of audio sent to the model, and thus includes the <br>`min_silence_duration_ms` configured in the Session.<br>|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user message item that will be created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped|

```json
      }
```
```json
    ]
  }
```

A realtime client event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventConversationItemCreate](#schemarealtimeclienteventconversationitemcreate)|false|none|Add a new Item to the Conversation's context, including messages, function <br>calls, and function call responses. This event can be used both to populate a <br>"history" of the conversation and to add new items mid-stream, but has the <br>current limitation that it cannot populate assistant audio messages.<br><br>If successful, the server will emit a `conversation.item.added` event and,<br>when the item is finalized, a `conversation.item.done` event. Otherwise, an<br>`error` event will be sent.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventConversationItemDelete](#schemarealtimeclienteventconversationitemdelete)|false|none|Send this event when you want to remove any item from the conversation <br>history. The server will respond with a `conversation.item.deleted` event, <br>unless the item does not exist in the conversation history, in which case the <br>server will respond with an error.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventConversationItemRetrieve](#schemarealtimeclienteventconversationitemretrieve)|false|none|Send this event when you want to retrieve the server's representation of a specific item in the conversation history. This is useful, for example, to inspect user audio after noise cancellation and VAD.<br>The server will respond with a `conversation.item.retrieved` event, <br>unless the item does not exist in the conversation history, in which case the <br>server will respond with an error.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventConversationItemTruncate](#schemarealtimeclienteventconversationitemtruncate)|false|none|Send this event to truncate a previous assistant message’s audio. The server <br>will produce audio faster than realtime, so this event is useful when the user <br>interrupts to truncate audio that has already been sent to the client but not <br>yet played. This will synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with <br>the client's playback.<br><br>Truncating audio will delete the server-side text transcript to ensure there <br>is not text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.<br><br>If successful, the server will respond with a `conversation.item.truncated` <br>event. <br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend](#schemarealtimeclienteventinputaudiobufferappend)|false|none|Send this event to append audio bytes to the input audio buffer. The audio <br>buffer is temporary storage you can write to and later commit. A "commit" will create a new<br>user message item in the conversation history from the buffer content and clear the buffer.<br>Input audio transcription (if enabled) will be generated when the buffer is committed.<br><br>If VAD is enabled the audio buffer is used to detect speech and the server will decide <br>when to commit. When Server VAD is disabled, you must commit the audio buffer<br>manually. Input audio noise reduction operates on writes to the audio buffer.<br><br>The client may choose how much audio to place in each event up to a maximum <br>of 15 MiB, for example streaming smaller chunks from the client may allow the <br>VAD to be more responsive. Unlike most other client events, the server will <br>not send a confirmation response to this event.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventInputAudioBufferClear](#schemarealtimeclienteventinputaudiobufferclear)|false|none|Send this event to clear the audio bytes in the buffer. The server will <br>respond with an `input_audio_buffer.cleared` event.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventOutputAudioBufferClear](#schemarealtimeclienteventoutputaudiobufferclear)|false|none|**WebRTC/SIP Only:** Emit to cut off the current audio response. This will trigger the server to<br>stop generating audio and emit a `output_audio_buffer.cleared` event. This<br>event should be preceded by a `response.cancel` client event to stop the<br>generation of the current response.<br>[Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-conversations#client-and-server-events-for-audio-in-webrtc).<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventInputAudioBufferCommit](#schemarealtimeclienteventinputaudiobuffercommit)|false|none|Send this event to commit the user input audio buffer, which will create a  new user message item in the conversation. This event will produce an error  if the input audio buffer is empty. When in Server VAD mode, the client does  not need to send this event, the server will commit the audio buffer  automatically.<br><br>Committing the input audio buffer will trigger input audio transcription  (if enabled in session configuration), but it will not create a response  from the model. The server will respond with an `input_audio_buffer.committed` event.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventResponseCancel](#schemarealtimeclienteventresponsecancel)|false|none|Send this event to cancel an in-progress response. The server will respond <br>with a `response.done` event with a status of `response.status=cancelled`. If <br>there is no response to cancel, the server will respond with an error. It's safe<br>to call `response.cancel` even if no response is in progress, an error will be<br>returned the session will remain unaffected.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventResponseCreate](#schemarealtimeclienteventresponsecreate)|false|none|This event instructs the server to create a Response, which means triggering <br>model inference. When in Server VAD mode, the server will create Responses <br>automatically.<br><br>A Response will include at least one Item, and may have two, in which case <br>the second will be a function call. These Items will be appended to the <br>conversation history by default.<br><br>The server will respond with a `response.created` event, events for Items <br>and content created, and finally a `response.done` event to indicate the <br>Response is complete.<br><br>The `response.create` event includes inference configuration like <br>`instructions` and `tools`. If these are set, they will override the Session's <br>configuration for this Response only.<br><br>Responses can be created out-of-band of the default Conversation, meaning that they can<br>have arbitrary input, and it's possible to disable writing the output to the Conversation.<br>Only one Response can write to the default Conversation at a time, but otherwise multiple<br>Responses can be created in parallel. The `metadata` field is a good way to disambiguate<br>multiple simultaneous Responses.<br><br>Clients can set `conversation` to `none` to create a Response that does not write to the default<br>Conversation. Arbitrary input can be provided with the `input` field, which is an array accepting<br>raw Items and references to existing Items.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeClientEventSessionUpdate](#schemarealtimeclienteventsessionupdate)|false|none|Send this event to update the session’s configuration.<br>The client may send this event at any time to update any field<br>except for `voice` and `model`. `voice` can be updated only if there have been no other audio outputs yet.<br><br>When the server receives a `session.update`, it will respond<br>with a `session.updated` event showing the full, effective configuration.<br>Only the fields that are present in the `session.update` are updated. To clear a field like<br>`instructions`, pass an empty string. To clear a field like `tools`, pass an empty array.<br>To clear a field like `turn_detection`, pass `null`.<br><br>To turn off input audio noise reduction, send this Realtime event:<br><br>```json<br>{"type":"session.update","session":{"type":"realtime","audio":{"input":{"noise_reduction":null}}}}<br>```<br><br>For a transcription session, use `"type":"transcription"` inside `session`.<br>Omitting `audio.input.noise_reduction` from an update leaves its current setting unchanged.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeClientEventConversationItemCreate">RealtimeClientEventConversationItemCreate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeclienteventconversationitemcreate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeClientEventConversationItemCreate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeclienteventconversationitemcreate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeclienteventconversationitemcreate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.create",
  "previous_item_id": "string",
  "item": {
    "id": "string",
    "object": "realtime.item",
    "type": "message",
    "status": "completed",
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Add a new Item to the Conversation's context, including messages, function 
calls, and function call responses. This event can be used both to populate a 
"history" of the conversation and to add new items mid-stream, but has the 
current limitation that it cannot populate assistant audio messages.

If successful, the server will emit a `conversation.item.added` event and,
when the item is finalized, a `conversation.item.done` event. Otherwise, an
`error` event will be sent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.create`.|
|previous_item_id|string|false|none|The ID of the preceding item after which the new item will be inserted. If not set, the new item will be appended to the end of the conversation.<br><br>If set to `root`, the new item will be added to the beginning of the conversation.<br><br>If set to an existing ID, it allows an item to be inserted mid-conversation. If the ID cannot be found, an error will be returned and the item will not be added.<br>|
|item|[RealtimeConversationItem](#schemarealtimeconversationitem)|true|none|A single item within a Realtime conversation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.create|

Send this event when you want to retrieve the server's representation of a specific item in the conversation history. This is useful, for example, to inspect user audio after noise cancellation and VAD.
The server will respond with a `conversation.item.retrieved` event, 
unless the item does not exist in the conversation history, in which case the 
server will respond with an error.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.retrieve`.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the item to retrieve.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.retrieve|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeClientEventConversationItemTruncate">RealtimeClientEventConversationItemTruncate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeclienteventconversationitemtruncate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeClientEventConversationItemTruncate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeclienteventconversationitemtruncate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeclienteventconversationitemtruncate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.truncate",
  "item_id": "string",
  "content_index": 0,
  "audio_end_ms": 0
}
```

Send this event to truncate a previous assistant message’s audio. The server 
will produce audio faster than realtime, so this event is useful when the user 
interrupts to truncate audio that has already been sent to the client but not 
yet played. This will synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with 
the client's playback.

Truncating audio will delete the server-side text transcript to ensure there 
is not text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.

If successful, the server will respond with a `conversation.item.truncated` 
event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.truncate`.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the assistant message item to truncate. Only assistant message <br>items can be truncated.<br>|
|content_index|integer|true|none|The index of the content part to truncate. Set this to `0`.|
|audio_end_ms|integer|true|none|Inclusive duration up to which audio is truncated, in milliseconds. If <br>the audio_end_ms is greater than the actual audio duration, the server <br>will respond with an error.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.truncate|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend">RealtimeClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.append",
  "audio": "string"
}
```

Send this event to append audio bytes to the input audio buffer. The audio 
buffer is temporary storage you can write to and later commit. A "commit" will create a new
user message item in the conversation history from the buffer content and clear the buffer.
Input audio transcription (if enabled) will be generated when the buffer is committed.

If VAD is enabled the audio buffer is used to detect speech and the server will decide 
when to commit. When Server VAD is disabled, you must commit the audio buffer
manually. Input audio noise reduction operates on writes to the audio buffer.

The client may choose how much audio to place in each event up to a maximum 
of 15 MiB, for example streaming smaller chunks from the client may allow the 
VAD to be more responsive. Unlike most other client events, the server will 
not send a confirmation response to this event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.append`.|
|audio|string|true|none|Base64-encoded audio bytes. This must be in the format specified by the <br>`input_audio_format` field in the session configuration.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.append|

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.commit"
}
```

Send this event to commit the user input audio buffer, which will create a  new user message item in the conversation. This event will produce an error  if the input audio buffer is empty. When in Server VAD mode, the client does  not need to send this event, the server will commit the audio buffer  automatically.

Committing the input audio buffer will trigger input audio transcription  (if enabled in session configuration), but it will not create a response  from the model. The server will respond with an `input_audio_buffer.committed` event.

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeClientEventResponseCancel">RealtimeClientEventResponseCancel</h2>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "response.cancel",
  "response_id": "string"
}
```

Send this event to cancel an in-progress response. The server will respond 
with a `response.done` event with a status of `response.status=cancelled`. If 
there is no response to cancel, the server will respond with an error. It's safe
to call `response.cancel` even if no response is in progress, an error will be
returned the session will remain unaffected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `response.cancel`.|
|response_id|string|false|none|A specific response ID to cancel - if not provided, will cancel an <br>in-progress response in the default conversation.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.cancel|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeClientEventResponseCreate">RealtimeClientEventResponseCreate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeclienteventresponsecreate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeClientEventResponseCreate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeclienteventresponsecreate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeclienteventresponsecreate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "response.create",
  "response": {
    "output_modalities": [
      "text"
    ],
    "instructions": "string",
    "audio": {
      "output": {
        "format": {
          "type": "audio/pcm",
          "rate": 24000
        },
        "voice": "ash"
      }
    },
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "parallel_tool_calls": true,
    "reasoning": {
      "effort": "low"
    },
    "max_output_tokens": 0,
    "conversation": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "prompt": {
      "id": "string",
      "version": "string",
      "variables": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    },
    "input": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "type": "message",
        "status": "completed",
        "role": "system",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "input_text",
            "text": "string"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

This event instructs the server to create a Response, which means triggering 
model inference. When in Server VAD mode, the server will create Responses 
automatically.

A Response will include at least one Item, and may have two, in which case 
the second will be a function call. These Items will be appended to the 
conversation history by default.

The server will respond with a `response.created` event, events for Items 
and content created, and finally a `response.done` event to indicate the 
Response is complete.

The `response.create` event includes inference configuration like 
`instructions` and `tools`. If these are set, they will override the Session's 
configuration for this Response only.

Responses can be created out-of-band of the default Conversation, meaning that they can
have arbitrary input, and it's possible to disable writing the output to the Conversation.
Only one Response can write to the default Conversation at a time, but otherwise multiple
Responses can be created in parallel. The `metadata` field is a good way to disambiguate
multiple simultaneous Responses.

Clients can set `conversation` to `none` to create a Response that does not write to the default
Conversation. Arbitrary input can be provided with the `input` field, which is an array accepting
raw Items and references to existing Items.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `response.create`.|
|response|[RealtimeResponseCreateParams](#schemarealtimeresponsecreateparams)|false|none|Create a new Realtime response with these parameters|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.create|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeClientEventSessionUpdate">RealtimeClientEventSessionUpdate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeclienteventsessionupdate"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeClientEventSessionUpdate"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeclienteventsessionupdate"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeclienteventsessionupdate"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "session.update",
  "session": {
    "type": "realtime",
    "output_modalities": [
      "audio"
    ],
    "model": "string",
    "instructions": "string",
    "audio": {
      "input": {
        "format": {
          "type": "audio/pcm",
          "rate": 24000
        },
        "transcription": {
          "model": "string",
          "language": "string",
          "languages": [
            "string"
          ],
          "keywords": [
            "string"
          ],
          "prompt": "string",
          "delay": "minimal"
        },
        "noise_reduction": null,
        "turn_detection": {
          "type": "server_vad",
          "threshold": 0,
          "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
          "silence_duration_ms": 0,
          "create_response": true,
          "interrupt_response": true,
          "idle_timeout_ms": 5000
        }
      },
      "output": {
        "format": {
          "type": "audio/pcm",
          "rate": 24000
        },
        "voice": "ash",
        "speed": 1
      }
    },
    "include": [
      "item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs"
    ],
    "tracing": null,
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "parallel_tool_calls": true,
    "reasoning": {
      "effort": "low"
    },
    "max_output_tokens": 0,
    "truncation": "auto",
    "prompt": {
      "id": "string",
      "version": "string",
      "variables": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Send this event to update the session’s configuration.
The client may send this event at any time to update any field
except for `voice` and `model`. `voice` can be updated only if there have been no other audio outputs yet.

When the server receives a `session.update`, it will respond
with a `session.updated` event showing the full, effective configuration.
Only the fields that are present in the `session.update` are updated. To clear a field like
`instructions`, pass an empty string. To clear a field like `tools`, pass an empty array.
To clear a field like `turn_detection`, pass `null`.

To turn off input audio noise reduction, send this Realtime event:

```json
{"type":"session.update","session":{"type":"realtime","audio":{"input":{"noise_reduction":null}}}}
```

For a transcription session, use `"type":"transcription"` inside `session`.
Omitting `audio.input.noise_reduction` from an update leaves its current setting unchanged.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event. This is an arbitrary string that a client may assign. It will be passed back if there is an error with the event, but the corresponding `session.updated` event will not include it.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `session.update`.|
|session|object|true|none|Update the Realtime session. Choose either a realtime<br>session or a transcription session.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|session.update|

```json
  "role": "system",
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "input_text",
      "text": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

A system message in a Realtime conversation can be used to provide additional context or instructions to the model. This is similar but distinct from the instruction prompt provided at the start of a conversation, as system messages can be added at any point in the conversation. For major changes to the conversation's behavior, use instructions, but for smaller updates (e.g. "the user is now asking about a different topic"), use system messages.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the item. This may be provided by the client or generated by the server.|
|object|string|false|none|Identifier for the API object being returned - always `realtime.item`. Optional when creating a new item.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the item. Always `message`.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the item. Has no effect on the conversation.|
|role|string|true|none|The role of the message sender. Always `system`.|
|content|[object]|true|none|The content of the message.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|realtime.item|
|type|message|
|status|completed|
|status|incomplete|
|status|in_progress|
|role|system|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|id|string|false|none|For an item of type (`message` \| `function_call` \| `function_call_output`)<br>this field allows the client to assign the unique ID of the item. It is<br>not required because the server will generate one if not provided.<br><br>For an item of type `item_reference`, this field is required and is a<br>reference to any item that has previously existed in the conversation.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the item (`message`, `function_call`, `function_call_output`, `item_reference`).<br>|
|object|string|false|none|Identifier for the API object being returned - always `realtime.item`.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the item (`completed`, `incomplete`, `in_progress`). These have no effect <br>on the conversation, but are accepted for consistency with the <br>`conversation.item.created` event.<br>|
|role|string|false|none|The role of the message sender (`user`, `assistant`, `system`), only <br>applicable for `message` items.<br>|
|content|[object]|false|none|The content of the message, applicable for `message` items. <br>- Message items of role `system` support only `input_text` content<br>- Message items of role `user` support `input_text` and `input_audio` <br>  content<br>- Message items of role `assistant` support `text` content.<br>|
|call_id|string|false|none|The ID of the function call (for `function_call` and <br>`function_call_output` items). If passed on a `function_call_output` <br>item, the server will check that a `function_call` item with the same <br>ID exists in the conversation history.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the function being called (for `function_call` items).<br>|
|arguments|string|false|none|The arguments of the function call (for `function_call` items).<br>|
|output|string|false|none|The output of the function call (for `function_call_output` items).<br>|

Create a session and client secret for the Realtime API. The request can specify
either a realtime or a transcription session configuration.
[Learn more about the Realtime API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expires_after|object|false|none|Configuration for the client secret expiration. Expiration refers to the time after which<br>a client secret will no longer be valid for creating sessions. The session itself may<br>continue after that time once started. A secret can be used to create multiple sessions<br>until it expires.<br>|
|session|[RealtimeSessionCreateRequestGA](#schemarealtimesessioncreaterequestga) \| [RealtimeTranscriptionSessionCreateRequestGA](#schemarealtimetranscriptionsessioncreaterequestga)|false|none|Session configuration to use for the client secret. Choose either a realtime<br>session or a transcription session.<br>|

The response resource.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the response, will look like `resp_1234`.|
|object|string|false|none|The object type, must be `realtime.response`.|
|status|string|false|none|The final status of the response (`completed`, `cancelled`, `failed`, or <br>`incomplete`, `in_progress`).<br>|
|status_details|object|false|none|Additional details about the status.|
|output|[[RealtimeConversationItem](#schemarealtimeconversationitem)]|false|none|The list of output items generated by the response.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|none|
|audio|object|false|none|Configuration for audio output.|
|usage|object|false|none|Usage statistics for the Response, this will correspond to billing. A <br>Realtime API session will maintain a conversation context and append new <br>Items to the Conversation, thus output from previous turns (text and <br>audio tokens) will become the input for later turns.<br>|
|conversation_id|string|false|none|Which conversation the response is added to, determined by the `conversation`<br>field in the `response.create` event. If `auto`, the response will be added to<br>the default conversation and the value of `conversation_id` will be an id like<br>`conv_1234`. If `none`, the response will not be added to any conversation and<br>the value of `conversation_id` will be `null`. If responses are being triggered<br>automatically by VAD the response will be added to the default conversation<br>|
|output_modalities|[string]|false|none|The set of modalities the model used to respond, currently the only possible values are<br>`[\"audio\"]`, `[\"text\"]`. Audio output always include a text transcript. Setting the<br>output to mode `text` will disable audio output from the model.<br>|
|max_output_tokens|integer \| string|false|none|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls, that was used in this response.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|realtime.response|
|status|completed|
|status|cancelled|
|status|failed|
|status|incomplete|
|status|in_progress|
|output_modalities|text|
|output_modalities|audio|

```json
      "voice": "ash"
    }
  },
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "parameters": {}
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "parallel_tool_calls": true,
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": "low"
  },
  "max_output_tokens": 0,
  "conversation": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "prompt": {
    "id": "string",
    "version": "string",
    "variables": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "input": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "type": "message",
      "status": "completed",
      "role": "system",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Create a new Realtime response with these parameters

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|output_modalities|[string]|false|none|The set of modalities the model used to respond, currently the only possible values are<br>`[\"audio\"]`, `[\"text\"]`. Audio output always include a text transcript. Setting the<br>output to mode `text` will disable audio output from the model.<br>|
|instructions|string|false|none|The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format, (e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the desired behavior.<br>Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the start of the session.<br>|
|audio|object|false|none|Configuration for audio input and output.|
|tools|[[RealtimeFunctionTool](#schemarealtimefunctiontool) \| [MCPTool](#schemamcptool)]|false|none|Tools available to the model.|
|tool_choice|[ToolChoiceOptions](#schematoolchoiceoptions) \| [ToolChoiceFunction](#schematoolchoicefunction) \| [ToolChoiceMCP](#schematoolchoicemcp)|false|none|How the model chooses tools. Provide one of the string modes or force a specific<br>function/MCP tool.<br>|
|parallel_tool_calls|boolean|false|none|Whether the model may call multiple tools in parallel. Only supported by<br>reasoning Realtime models such as `gpt-realtime-2`.<br>|
|reasoning|[RealtimeReasoning](#schemarealtimereasoning)|false|none|Configuration for reasoning-capable Realtime models such as `gpt-realtime-2`.<br>|
|max_output_tokens|integer \| string|false|none|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to<br>limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a<br>given model. Defaults to `inf`.<br>|
|conversation|string|false|none|Controls which conversation the response is added to. Currently supports<br>`auto` and `none`, with `auto` as the default value. The `auto` value<br>means that the contents of the response will be added to the default<br>conversation. Set this to `none` to create an out-of-band response which<br>will not add items to default conversation.<br>|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|none|
|prompt|[Prompt](#schemaprompt)|false|none|none|
|input|[[RealtimeResponseInputItem](#schemarealtimeresponseinputitem)]|false|none|Input items to include in the prompt for the model. Using this field<br>creates a new context for this Response instead of using the default<br>conversation. An empty array `[]` will clear the context for this Response.<br>Note that this can include references to items that previously appeared in the session<br>using their id.<br>|

|output_modalities|audio|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeServerEvent">RealtimeServerEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeserverevent"></a>

```json
  "event_id": "string",

    "id": "string",
    "object": "string"
  }
}
```

A realtime server event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationCreated](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationcreated)|false|none|Returned when a conversation is created. Emitted right after session creation.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemCreated](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemcreated)|false|none|Returned when a conversation item is created. There are several scenarios that produce this event:<br>  - The server is generating a Response, which if successful will produce<br>    either one or two Items, which will be of type `message`<br>    (role `assistant`) or type `function_call`.<br>  - The input audio buffer has been committed, either by the client or the<br>    server (in `server_vad` mode). The server will take the content of the<br>    input audio buffer and add it to a new user message Item.<br>  - The client has sent a `conversation.item.create` event to add a new Item<br>    to the Conversation.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemDeleted](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemdeleted)|false|none|Returned when an item in the conversation is deleted by the client with a <br>`conversation.item.delete` event. This event is used to synchronize the <br>server's understanding of the conversation history with the client's view.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted)|false|none|This event is the output of audio transcription for user audio written to the<br>user audio buffer. Transcription begins when the input audio buffer is<br>committed by the client or server (when VAD is enabled). Transcription runs<br>asynchronously with Response creation, so this event may come before or after<br>the Response events.<br><br>Realtime API models accept audio natively, and thus input transcription is a<br>separate process run on a separate ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) model.<br>The transcript may diverge somewhat from the model's interpretation, and<br>should be treated as a rough guide.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionDelta](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptiondelta)|false|none|Returned when the text value of an input audio transcription content part is updated with incremental transcription results.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionFailed](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptionfailed)|false|none|Returned when input audio transcription is configured, and a transcription <br>request for a user message failed. These events are separate from other <br>`error` events so that the client can identify the related Item.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemRetrieved](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemretrieved)|false|none|Returned when a conversation item is retrieved with `conversation.item.retrieve`. This is provided as a way to fetch the server's representation of an item, for example to get access to the post-processed audio data after noise cancellation and VAD. It includes the full content of the Item, including audio data.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemTruncated](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemtruncated)|false|none|Returned when an earlier assistant audio message item is truncated by the <br>client with a `conversation.item.truncate` event. This event is used to <br>synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with the client's playback.<br><br>This action will truncate the audio and remove the server-side text transcript <br>to ensure there is no text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventError](#schemarealtimeservereventerror)|false|none|Returned when an error occurs, which could be a client problem or a server<br>problem. Most errors are recoverable and the session will stay open, we<br>recommend to implementers to monitor and log error messages by default.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferCleared](#schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobuffercleared)|false|none|Returned when the input audio buffer is cleared by the client with a <br>`input_audio_buffer.clear` event.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferCommitted](#schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobuffercommitted)|false|none|Returned when an input audio buffer is committed, either by the client or<br>automatically in server VAD mode. The `item_id` property is the ID of the user<br>message item that will be created, thus a `conversation.item.created` event<br>will also be sent to the client.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferDtmfEventReceived](#schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobufferdtmfeventreceived)|false|none|**SIP Only:** Returned when an DTMF event is received. A DTMF event is a message that<br>represents a telephone keypad press (0–9, *, #, A–D). The `event` property<br>is the keypad that the user press. The `received_at` is the UTC Unix Timestamp<br>that the server received the event.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted](#schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted)|false|none|Sent by the server when in `server_vad` mode to indicate that speech has been <br>detected in the audio buffer. This can happen any time audio is added to the <br>buffer (unless speech is already detected). The client may want to use this <br>event to interrupt audio playback or provide visual feedback to the user. <br><br>The client should expect to receive a `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event <br>when speech stops. The `item_id` property is the ID of the user message item <br>that will be created when speech stops and will also be included in the <br>`input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event (unless the client manually commits <br>the audio buffer during VAD activation).<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStopped](#schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstopped)|false|none|Returned in `server_vad` mode when the server detects the end of speech in <br>the audio buffer. The server will also send an `conversation.item.created` <br>event with the user message item that is created from the audio buffer.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventRateLimitsUpdated](#schemarealtimeservereventratelimitsupdated)|false|none|Emitted at the beginning of a Response to indicate the updated rate limits. <br>When a Response is created some tokens will be "reserved" for the output <br>tokens, the rate limits shown here reflect that reservation, which is then <br>adjusted accordingly once the Response is completed.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseAudioDelta](#schemarealtimeservereventresponseaudiodelta)|false|none|Returned when the model-generated audio is updated.|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseAudioDone](#schemarealtimeservereventresponseaudiodone)|false|none|Returned when the model-generated audio is done. Also emitted when a Response<br>is interrupted, incomplete, or cancelled.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseAudioTranscriptDelta](#schemarealtimeservereventresponseaudiotranscriptdelta)|false|none|Returned when the model-generated transcription of audio output is updated.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseAudioTranscriptDone](#schemarealtimeservereventresponseaudiotranscriptdone)|false|none|Returned when the model-generated transcription of audio output is done<br>streaming. Also emitted when a Response is interrupted, incomplete, or<br>cancelled.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseContentPartAdded](#schemarealtimeservereventresponsecontentpartadded)|false|none|Returned when a new content part is added to an assistant message item during<br>response generation.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseContentPartDone](#schemarealtimeservereventresponsecontentpartdone)|false|none|Returned when a content part is done streaming in an assistant message item.<br>Also emitted when a Response is interrupted, incomplete, or cancelled.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseCreated](#schemarealtimeservereventresponsecreated)|false|none|Returned when a new Response is created. The first event of response creation,<br>where the response is in an initial state of `in_progress`.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventResponseDone](#schemarealtimeservereventresponsedone)|false|none|Returned when a Response is done streaming. Always emitted, no matter the <br>final state. The Response object included in the `response.done` event will <br>include all output Items in the Response but will omit the raw audio data.<br><br>Clients should check the `status` field of the Response to determine if it was successful<br>(`completed`) or if there was another outcome: `cancelled`, `failed`, or `incomplete`.<br><br>A response will contain all output items that were generated during the response, excluding<br>any audio content.<br>|

|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventOutputAudioBufferStarted](#schemarealtimeservereventoutputaudiobufferstarted)|false|none|**WebRTC/SIP Only:** Emitted when the server begins streaming audio to the client. This event is<br>emitted after an audio content part has been added (`response.content_part.added`)<br>to the response.<br>[Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-conversations#client-and-server-events-for-audio-in-webrtc).<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventOutputAudioBufferStopped](#schemarealtimeservereventoutputaudiobufferstopped)|false|none|**WebRTC/SIP Only:** Emitted when the output audio buffer has been completely drained on the server,<br>and no more audio is forthcoming. This event is emitted after the full response<br>data has been sent to the client (`response.done`).<br>[Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-conversations#client-and-server-events-for-audio-in-webrtc).<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventOutputAudioBufferCleared](#schemarealtimeservereventoutputaudiobuffercleared)|false|none|**WebRTC/SIP Only:** Emitted when the output audio buffer is cleared. This happens either in VAD<br>mode when the user has interrupted (`input_audio_buffer.speech_started`),<br>or when the client has emitted the `output_audio_buffer.clear` event to manually<br>cut off the current audio response.<br>[Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-conversations#client-and-server-events-for-audio-in-webrtc).<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemAdded](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemadded)|false|none|Sent by the server when an Item is added to the default Conversation. This can happen in several cases:<br>- When the client sends a `conversation.item.create` event.<br>- When the input audio buffer is committed. In this case the item will be a user message containing the audio from the buffer.<br>- When the model is generating a Response. In this case the `conversation.item.added` event will be sent when the model starts generating a specific Item, and thus it will not yet have any content (and `status` will be `in_progress`).<br><br>The event will include the full content of the Item (except when model is generating a Response) except for audio data, which can be retrieved separately with a `conversation.item.retrieve` event if necessary.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventConversationItemDone](#schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemdone)|false|none|Returned when a conversation item is finalized.<br><br>The event will include the full content of the Item except for audio data, which can be retrieved separately with a `conversation.item.retrieve` event if needed.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferTimeoutTriggered](#schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobuffertimeouttriggered)|false|none|Returned when the Server VAD timeout is triggered for the input audio buffer. This is configured<br>with `idle_timeout_ms` in the `turn_detection` settings of the session, and it indicates that<br>there hasn't been any speech detected for the configured duration.<br><br>The `audio_start_ms` and `audio_end_ms` fields indicate the segment of audio after the last<br>model response up to the triggering time, as an offset from the beginning of audio written<br>to the input audio buffer. This means it demarcates the segment of audio that was silent and<br>the difference between the start and end values will roughly match the configured timeout.<br><br>The empty audio will be committed to the conversation as an `input_audio` item (there will be a<br>`input_audio_buffer.committed` event) and a model response will be generated.
