<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeServerEventConversationItemAdded">RealtimeServerEventConversationItemAdded</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemadded"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeServerEventConversationItemAdded"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeservereventconversationitemadded"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeservereventconversationitemadded"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.added",
  "previous_item_id": "string",
  "item": {
    "id": "string",
    "object": "realtime.item",
    "type": "message",
    "status": "completed",
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Sent by the server when an Item is added to the default Conversation. This can happen in several cases:
- When the client sends a `conversation.item.create` event.
- When the input audio buffer is committed. In this case the item will be a user message containing the audio from the buffer.
- When the model is generating a Response. In this case the `conversation.item.added` event will be sent when the model starts generating a specific Item, and thus it will not yet have any content (and `status` will be `in_progress`).

The event will include the full content of the Item (except when model is generating a Response) except for audio data, which can be retrieved separately with a `conversation.item.retrieve` event if necessary.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.added`.|
|previous_item_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|item|[RealtimeConversationItem](#schemarealtimeconversationitem)|true|none|A single item within a Realtime conversation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.added|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeServerEventConversationItemCreated">RealtimeServerEventConversationItemCreated</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeservereventconversationitemcreated"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeServerEventConversationItemCreated"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeservereventconversationitemcreated"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeservereventconversationitemcreated"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.created",
  "previous_item_id": "string",
  "item": {
    "id": "string",
    "object": "realtime.item",
    "type": "message",
    "status": "completed",
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Returned when a conversation item is created. There are several scenarios that produce this event:
  - The server is generating a Response, which if successful will produce
    either one or two Items, which will be of type `message`
    (role `assistant`) or type `function_call`.
  - The input audio buffer has been committed, either by the client or the
    server (in `server_vad` mode). The server will take the content of the
    input audio buffer and add it to a new user message Item.
  - The client has sent a `conversation.item.create` event to add a new Item
    to the Conversation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `conversation.item.created`.|
|previous_item_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|item|[RealtimeConversationItem](#schemarealtimeconversationitem)|true|none|A single item within a Realtime conversation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.created|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted">RealtimeServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeservereventconversationiteminputaudiotranscriptioncompleted"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed",
  "item_id": "string",
  "content_index": 0,
  "transcript": "string",
  "languages": [
    {
      "code": "string"
    }
  ],
  "logprobs": [
    {
      "token": "string",
      "logprob": 0,
      "bytes": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "type": "tokens",
    "input_tokens": 0,
    "input_token_details": {
      "text_tokens": 0,
      "audio_tokens": 0
    },
    "output_tokens": 0,
    "total_tokens": 0
  }
}
```

This event is the output of audio transcription for user audio written to the
user audio buffer. Transcription begins when the input audio buffer is
committed by the client or server (when VAD is enabled). Transcription runs
asynchronously with Response creation, so this event may come before or after
the Response events.

Realtime API models accept audio natively, and thus input transcription is a
separate process run on a separate ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) model.
The transcript may diverge somewhat from the model's interpretation, and
should be treated as a rough guide.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be<br>`conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed`.<br>|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the item containing the audio that is being transcribed.|
|content_index|integer|true|none|The index of the content part containing the audio.|
|transcript|string|true|none|The transcribed text.|
|languages|[[TranscriptionLanguage](#schematranscriptionlanguage)]|false|none|The languages detected in the audio. Returned by `gpt-transcribe`. An empty array indicates that no language could be reliably detected.<br>|
|logprobs|[[LogProbProperties](#schemalogprobproperties)] \| null|false|none|none|
|usage|object|true|none|Usage statistics for the transcription, this is billed according to the ASR model's pricing rather than the realtime model's pricing.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed|

```json
  "item_id": "string",
```

Returned when an earlier assistant audio message item is truncated by the 
client with a `conversation.item.truncate` event. This event is used to 
synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with the client's playback.

This action will truncate the audio and remove the server-side text transcript 
to ensure there is no text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted">RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeservereventinputaudiobufferspeechstarted"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.speech_started",
  "audio_start_ms": 0,
  "item_id": "string"
}
```

Sent by the server when in `server_vad` mode to indicate that speech has been 
detected in the audio buffer. This can happen any time audio is added to the 
buffer (unless speech is already detected). The client may want to use this 
event to interrupt audio playback or provide visual feedback to the user. 

The client should expect to receive a `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event 
when speech stops. The `item_id` property is the ID of the user message item 
that will be created when speech stops and will also be included in the 
`input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event (unless the client manually commits 
the audio buffer during VAD activation).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.speech_started`.|
|audio_start_ms|integer|true|none|Milliseconds from the start of all audio written to the buffer during the <br>session when speech was first detected. This will correspond to the <br>beginning of audio sent to the model, and thus includes the <br>`prefix_padding_ms` configured in the Session.<br>|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user message item that will be created when speech stops.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.speech_started|

```json
{

  "audio_end_ms": 0,
  "item_id": "string"
}
```

Returned in `server_vad` mode when the server detects the end of speech in 
the audio buffer. The server will also send an `conversation.item.created` 
event with the user message item that is created from the audio buffer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped`.|
|audio_end_ms|integer|true|none|Milliseconds since the session started when speech stopped. This will <br>correspond to the end of audio sent to the model, and thus includes the <br>`min_silence_duration_ms` configured in the Session.<br>|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user message item that will be created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferTimeoutTriggered">RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferTimeoutTriggered</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeservereventinputaudiobuffertimeouttriggered"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeServerEventInputAudioBufferTimeoutTriggered"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeservereventinputaudiobuffertimeouttriggered"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeservereventinputaudiobuffertimeouttriggered"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "input_audio_buffer.timeout_triggered",
  "audio_start_ms": 0,
  "audio_end_ms": 0,
  "item_id": "string"
}
```

Returned when the Server VAD timeout is triggered for the input audio buffer. This is configured
with `idle_timeout_ms` in the `turn_detection` settings of the session, and it indicates that
there hasn't been any speech detected for the configured duration.

The `audio_start_ms` and `audio_end_ms` fields indicate the segment of audio after the last
model response up to the triggering time, as an offset from the beginning of audio written
to the input audio buffer. This means it demarcates the segment of audio that was silent and
the difference between the start and end values will roughly match the configured timeout.

The empty audio will be committed to the conversation as an `input_audio` item (there will be a
`input_audio_buffer.committed` event) and a model response will be generated. There may be speech
that didn't trigger VAD but is still detected by the model, so the model may respond with
something relevant to the conversation or a prompt to continue speaking.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the server event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.timeout_triggered`.|
|audio_start_ms|integer|true|none|Millisecond offset of audio written to the input audio buffer that was after the playback time of the last model response.|
|audio_end_ms|integer|true|none|Millisecond offset of audio written to the input audio buffer at the time the timeout was triggered.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The ID of the item associated with this segment.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_audio_buffer.timeout_triggered|

Returned when a Response is done streaming. Always emitted, no matter the 
final state. The Response object included in the `response.done` event will 
include all output Items in the Response but will omit the raw audio data.

Clients should check the `status` field of the Response to determine if it was successful
(`completed`) or if there was another outcome: `cancelled`, `failed`, or `incomplete`.

A response will contain all output items that were generated during the response, excluding
any audio content.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `response.done`.|
|response|[RealtimeResponse](#schemarealtimeresponse)|true|none|The response resource.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.done|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Unique identifier for the session that looks like `sess_1234567890abcdef`.<br>|
|object|string|false|none|The object type. Always `realtime.session`.|

|model|string|false|none|The Realtime model used for this session.<br>|
|instructions|string|false|none|The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model<br>calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired<br>responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format,<br>(e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good<br>responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion<br>into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not<br>guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the<br>model on the desired behavior.<br><br><br>Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this<br>field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the<br>start of the session.<br>|
|voice|[VoiceIdsShared](#schemavoiceidsshared)|false|none|The voice the model uses to respond. Voice cannot be changed during the<br>session once the model has responded with audio at least once. |input_audio_format|string|false|none|The format of input audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>For `pcm16`, input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 24kHz sample rate,<br>single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order.<br>|
|output_audio_format|string|false|none|The format of output audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>For `pcm16`, output audio is sampled at a rate of 24kHz.<br>|
|input_audio_transcription|object \| null|false|none|none|
|turn_detection|[RealtimeTurnDetection](#schemarealtimeturndetection)|false|none|none|
|input_audio_noise_reduction|object|false|none|Configuration for input audio noise reduction. This can be set to `null` to turn off.<br>Noise reduction filters audio added to the input audio buffer before it is sent to VAD and the model.<br>Filtering the audio can improve VAD and turn detection accuracy (reducing false positives) and model performance by improving perception of the input audio.<br>|
|speed|number|false|none|The speed of the model's spoken response. 1.0 is the default speed. 0.25 is<br>the minimum speed. 1.5 is the maximum speed. This value can only be changed<br>in between model turns, not while a response is in progress.<br>|
|tracing|string \| object \| null|false|none|none|
|tools|[[RealtimeFunctionTool](#schemarealtimefunctiontool)]|false|none|Tools (functions) available to the model.|
|tool_choice|string|false|none|How the model chooses tools. Options are `auto`, `none`, `required`, or<br>specify a function.<br>|
|temperature|number|false|none|Sampling temperature for the model, limited to [0.6, 1.2]. For audio models a temperature of 0.8 is highly recommended for best performance.<br>|

|expires_at|integer(unixtime)|false|none|Expiration timestamp for the session, in seconds since epoch.|

A new Realtime session configuration, with an ephemeral key. Default TTL
for keys is one minute.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_secret|object|true|none|Ephemeral key returned by the API.|
|modalities|[string]|false|none|The set of modalities the model can respond with. To disable audio,<br>set this to ["text"].<br>|
|instructions|string|false|none|The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format, (e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the desired behavior.<br>Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the start of the session.<br>|
|voice|[VoiceIdsOrCustomVoice](#schemavoiceidsorcustomvoice)|false|none|The voice the model uses to respond. Supported built-in voices are<br>`alloy`, `ash`, `ballad`, `coral`, `echo`, `sage`, `shimmer`, `verse`,<br>`marin`, and `cedar`. You may also provide a custom voice object with an<br>`id`, for example `{ "id": "voice_1234" }`. Voice cannot be changed during<br>the session once the model has responded with audio at least once.<br>Custom voices must be created from audio samples. Voices created from text prompts are supported only in Live.<br>|
|input_audio_format|string|false|none|The format of input audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>|
|output_audio_format|string|false|none|The format of output audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.<br>|
|input_audio_transcription|object|false|none|Configuration for input audio transcription, defaults to off and can be<br>set to `null` to turn off once on. Input audio transcription is not native<br>to the model, since the model consumes audio directly. Transcription runs<br>asynchronously and should be treated as rough guidance<br>rather than the representation understood by the model.<br>|
|speed|number|false|none|The speed of the model's spoken response. 1.0 is the default speed. 0.25 is<br>the minimum speed. 1.5 is the maximum speed. This value can only be changed<br>in between model turns, not while a response is in progress.<br>|
|tracing|string \| object|false|none|Configuration options for tracing. Set to null to disable tracing. Once<br>tracing is enabled for a session, the configuration cannot be modified.<br><br>`auto` will create a trace for the session with default values for the<br>workflow name, group id, and metadata.<br>|
|turn_detection|object|false|none|Configuration for turn detection. Can be set to `null` to turn off. Server<br>VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on<br>audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.<br>|
|tools|[object]|false|none|Tools (functions) available to the model.|
|tool_choice|string|false|none|How the model chooses tools. Options are `auto`, `none`, `required`, or<br>specify a function.<br>|
|temperature|number|false|none|Sampling temperature for the model, limited to [0.6, 1.2]. Defaults to 0.8.<br>|
|max_response_output_tokens|integer \| string|false|none|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to<br>limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a<br>given model. Defaults to `inf`.<br>|
|truncation|[RealtimeTruncation](#schemarealtimetruncation)|false|none|When the number of tokens in a conversation exceeds the model's input token limit, the conversation be truncated, meaning messages (starting from the oldest) will not be included in the model's context. A 32k context model with 4,096 max output tokens can only include 28,224 tokens in the context before truncation occurs.<br><br>Clients can configure truncation behavior to truncate with a lower max token limit, which is an effective way to control token usage and cost.<br><br>Truncation will reduce the number of cached tokens on the next turn (busting the cache), since messages are dropped from the beginning of the context. However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.<br><br>Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.<br>|
|prompt|[Prompt](#schemaprompt)|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|modalities|text|
|modalities|audio|

```json
    "effort": "low"
  },
  "max_output_tokens": 0,
  "truncation": "auto",
  "prompt": {
    "id": "string",
    "version": "string",
    "variables": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

A Realtime session configuration object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of session to create. Always `realtime` for the Realtime API.<br>|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the session that looks like `sess_1234567890abcdef`.<br>|
|object|string|true|none|The object type. Always `realtime.session`.|
|expires_at|integer(unixtime)|false|none|Expiration timestamp for the session, in seconds since epoch.|
|output_modalities|[string]|false|none|The set of modalities the model can respond with. It defaults to `["audio"]`, indicating<br>that the model will respond with audio plus a transcript. `["text"]` can be used to make<br>the model respond with text only. It is not possible to request both `text` and `audio` at the same time.<br>|
|model|string|false|none|The Realtime model used for this session.<br>|
|instructions|string|false|none|The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format, (e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the desired behavior.<br><br>Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the start of the session.<br>|
|audio|object|false|none|Configuration for input and output audio.<br>|
|include|[string]|false|none|Additional fields to include in server outputs.<br><br>`item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs`: Include logprobs for input audio transcription.<br>|
|tracing|string \| object \| null|false|none|none|
|tools|[[RealtimeFunctionTool](#schemarealtimefunctiontool) \| [MCPTool](#schemamcptool)]|false|none|Tools available to the model.|
|tool_choice|[ToolChoiceOptions](#schematoolchoiceoptions) \| [ToolChoiceFunction](#schematoolchoicefunction) \| [ToolChoiceMCP](#schematoolchoicemcp)|false|none|How the model chooses tools. Provide one of the string modes or force a specific<br>function/MCP tool.<br>|
|reasoning|[RealtimeReasoning](#schemarealtimereasoning)|false|none|Configuration for reasoning-capable Realtime models such as `gpt-realtime-2`.<br>|
|max_output_tokens|integer \| string|false|none|Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,<br>inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to<br>limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a<br>given model. Defaults to `inf`.<br>|
|truncation|[RealtimeTruncation](#schemarealtimetruncation)|false|none|When the number of tokens in a conversation exceeds the model's input token limit, the conversation be truncated, meaning messages (starting from the oldest) will not be included in the model's context. A 32k context model with 4,096 max output tokens can only include 28,224 tokens in the context before truncation occurs.<br><br>Clients can configure truncation behavior to truncate with a lower max token limit, which is an effective way to control token usage and cost.<br><br>Truncation will reduce the number of cached tokens on the next turn (busting the cache), since messages are dropped from the beginning of the context. However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.<br><br>Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.<br>|
|prompt|[Prompt](#schemaprompt)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|realtime|
|object|realtime.session|
|output_modalities|text|
|output_modalities|audio|
|include|item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|turn_detection|object|false|none|Configuration for turn detection. Can be set to `null` to turn off. Server VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.<br>|
|input_audio_noise_reduction|object|false|none|Configuration for input audio noise reduction. This can be set to `null` to turn off.<br>Noise reduction filters audio added to the input audio buffer before it is sent to VAD and the model.<br>Filtering the audio can improve VAD and turn detection accuracy (reducing false positives) and model performance by improving perception of the input audio.<br>|

|input_audio_transcription|[AudioTranscription](#schemaaudiotranscription)|false|none|Configuration for input audio transcription. The client can optionally set the language and prompt for transcription, these offer additional guidance to the transcription service.<br>|
|include|[string]|false|none|The set of items to include in the transcription. Current available items are:<br>`item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs`<br>|

|*anyOf*|[RealtimeTranslationClientEventSessionUpdate](#schemarealtimetranslationclienteventsessionupdate)|false|none|Send this event to update the translation session configuration. Translation<br>sessions support updates to `audio.output.language`, `audio.input.transcription`,<br>and `audio.input.noise_reduction`.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeTranslationClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend](#schemarealtimetranslationclienteventinputaudiobufferappend)|false|none|Send this event to append audio bytes to the translation session input audio buffer.<br><br>WebSocket translation sessions accept base64-encoded 24 kHz PCM16 mono<br>little-endian raw audio bytes. Unsupported websocket audio formats return a<br>validation error because lower-quality audio materially degrades translation<br>quality.<br><br>Translation consumes 200 ms engine frames. For best realtime behavior, append<br>audio in 200 ms chunks. If a chunk is shorter, the server buffers it until it<br>has enough audio for one frame. If a chunk is longer, the server splits it into<br>200 ms frames and enqueues them back-to-back.<br><br>Keep appending silence while the session is active. If a client stops sending<br>audio and later resumes, model time treats the resumed audio as contiguous with<br>the previous audio rather than as a real-world pause.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[RealtimeTranslationClientEventSessionClose](#schemarealtimetranslationclienteventsessionclose)|false|none|Gracefully close the realtime translation session. The server flushes pending<br>input audio and emits any remaining translated output before closing the<br>session.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeTranslationClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend">RealtimeTranslationClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimetranslationclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeTranslationClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimetranslationclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimetranslationclienteventinputaudiobufferappend"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "type": "session.input_audio_buffer.append",
  "audio": "string"
}
```

Send this event to append audio bytes to the translation session input audio buffer.

WebSocket translation sessions accept base64-encoded 24 kHz PCM16 mono
little-endian raw audio bytes. Unsupported websocket audio formats return a
validation error because lower-quality audio materially degrades translation
quality.

Translation consumes 200 ms engine frames. For best realtime behavior, append
audio in 200 ms chunks. If a chunk is shorter, the server buffers it until it
has enough audio for one frame. If a chunk is longer, the server splits it into
200 ms frames and enqueues them back-to-back.

Keep appending silence while the session is active. If a client stops sending
audio and later resumes, model time treats the resumed audio as contiguous with
the previous audio rather than as a real-world pause.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, must be `session.input_audio_buffer.append`.|
|audio|string|true|none|Base64-encoded 24 kHz PCM16 mono audio bytes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|session.input_audio_buffer.append|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeTruncation">RealtimeTruncation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimetruncation"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeTruncation"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimetruncation"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimetruncation"></a>

```json
"auto"
```

When the number of tokens in a conversation exceeds the model's input token limit, the conversation be truncated, meaning messages (starting from the oldest) will not be included in the model's context. A 32k context model with 4,096 max output tokens can only include 28,224 tokens in the context before truncation occurs.

Clients can configure truncation behavior to truncate with a lower max token limit, which is an effective way to control token usage and cost.

Truncation will reduce the number of cached tokens on the next turn (busting the cache), since messages are dropped from the beginning of the context. However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.

Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|The truncation strategy to use for the session. `auto` is the default truncation strategy. `disabled` will disable truncation and emit errors when the conversation exceeds the input token limit.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Retain a fraction of the conversation tokens when the conversation exceeds the input token limit. This allows you to amortize truncations across multiple turns, which can help improve cached token usage.|
|type|string|true|none|Use retention ratio truncation.|
|retention_ratio|number|true|none|Fraction of post-instruction conversation tokens to retain (`0.0` - `1.0`) when the conversation exceeds the input token limit. Setting this to `0.8` means that messages will be dropped until 80% of the maximum allowed tokens are used. This helps reduce the frequency of truncations and improve cache rates.<br>|
|token_limits|object|false|none|Optional custom token limits for this truncation strategy. If not provided, the model's default token limits will be used.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|auto|
|*oneOf*|disabled|
|type|retention_ratio|

<h2 id="tocS_RealtimeTurnDetection">RealtimeTurnDetection</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarealtimeturndetection"></a>
<a id="schema_RealtimeTurnDetection"></a>
<a id="tocSrealtimeturndetection"></a>
<a id="tocsrealtimeturndetection"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "server_vad",
  "threshold": 0,
  "prefix_padding_ms": 0,
  "silence_duration_ms": 0,
  "create_response": true,
  "interrupt_response": true,
  "idle_timeout_ms": 5000
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|Configuration for turn detection, ether Server VAD or Semantic VAD. This can be set to `null` to turn off, in which case the client must manually trigger model response.<br><br>Server VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.<br><br>Semantic VAD is more advanced and uses a turn detection model (in conjunction with VAD) to semantically estimate whether the user has finished speaking, then dynamically sets a timeout based on this probability. For example, if user audio trails off with "uhhm", the model will score a low probability of turn end and wait longer for the user to continue speaking. This can be useful for more natural conversations, but may have a higher latency.<br><br>For `gpt-realtime-whisper` transcription sessions, turn detection must be<br>set to `null`; VAD is not supported.<br>|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Server-side voice activity detection (VAD) which flips on when user speech is detected and off after a period of silence.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of turn detection, `server_vad` to turn on simple Server VAD.<br>|
|threshold|number|false|none|Used only for `server_vad` mode. Activation threshold for VAD (0.0 to 1.0), this defaults to 0.5. A<br>higher threshold will require louder audio to activate the model, and<br>thus might perform better in noisy environments.<br>|
|prefix_padding_ms|integer|false|none|Used only for `server_vad` mode. Amount of audio to include before the VAD detected speech (in<br>milliseconds). Defaults to 300ms.<br>|
|silence_duration_ms|integer|false|none|Used only for `server_vad` mode. Duration of silence to detect speech stop (in milliseconds). Defaults<br>to 500ms. With shorter values the model will respond more quickly,<br>but may jump in on short pauses from the user.<br>|
|create_response|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to automatically generate a response when a VAD stop event occurs. If `interrupt_response` is set to `false` this may fail to create a response if the model is already responding.<br><br>If both `create_response` and `interrupt_response` are set to `false`, the model will never respond automatically but VAD events will still be emitted.<br>|
|interrupt_response|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to automatically interrupt (cancel) any ongoing response with output to the default<br>conversation (i.e. `conversation` of `auto`) when a VAD start event occurs. If `true` then the response will be cancelled, otherwise it will continue until complete.<br><br>If both `create_response` and `interrupt_response` are set to `false`, the model will never respond automatically but VAD events will still be emitted.<br>|
|idle_timeout_ms|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Server-side semantic turn detection which uses a model to determine when the user has finished speaking.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of turn detection, `semantic_vad` to turn on Semantic VAD.<br>|
|eagerness|string|false|none|Used only for `semantic_vad` mode. The eagerness of the model to respond. `low` will wait longer for the user to continue speaking, `high` will respond more quickly. `auto` is the default and is equivalent to `medium`. `low`, `medium`, and `high` have max timeouts of 8s, 4s, and 2s respectively.<br>|
|create_response|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to automatically generate a response when a VAD stop event occurs.<br>|
|interrupt_response|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to automatically interrupt any ongoing response with output to the default<br>conversation (i.e. `conversation` of `auto`) when a VAD start event occurs.<br>|
|*anyOf*|null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|eagerness|low|
|eagerness|medium|
|eagerness|high|
|eagerness|auto|

Output<br>token details and cached input counts can be omitted. An omitted cache<br>count means cache usage is unknown.<br><br>`web_search.num_requests` counts billable searches. Discounted searches<br>and actions such as opening a page are excluded. Use billing records to<br>reconcile final charges.<br>|

```json
      "token": "string",
      "logprob": 0
    }
  ]

```

A logprob is the logarithmic probability that the model assigns to producing 
a particular token at a given position in the sequence. Less-negative (higher) 
logprob values indicate greater model confidence in that token choice.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|string|true|none|A possible text token.|
|logprob|number|true|none|The log probability of this token.<br>|
|top_logprobs|[object]|false|none|The log probabilities of up to 20 of the most likely tokens.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerAcceptedEvent">ResponseSteerAcceptedEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteeracceptedevent"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerAcceptedEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteeracceptedevent"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteeracceptedevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer.accepted",
  "sequence_number": 0,
  "steer": {
    "id": "string",
    "previous_response_id": "string"
  },
  "stream_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when steering input has been validated and queued. Acceptance means
the server owns the input, not that it has been applied. The successor's
`response.created` event is the commit point. If accepted input cannot be
committed, `response.steer.failed` returns it with the same steering ID.

When the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, the input
remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after
`response.completed`. Fill the pending event's `required_input` stubs with
saved results and send one matching explicit `response.create` per parent.
Do not resend accepted input while it is still queued.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer.accepted`.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|steer|object|true|none|The accepted steering submission.|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event. This field is present when<br>the target response's `response.create` event supplied a `stream_id`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer.accepted|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerErrorCode">ResponseSteerErrorCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteererrorcode"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerErrorCode"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteererrorcode"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteererrorcode"></a>

```json
"response_not_found"
```

A machine-readable steering error code. Clients should handle unknown
values because additional codes may be introduced. Known values include:
- `response_not_found`: The target response is not available on this connection.
- `invalid_input`: The event or input failed validation.
- `steering_not_supported`: The model or response execution mode does not support steering.
- `too_many_pending_steers`: Too much steering input is pending for the response.
- `response_already_completed`: The response completed and is no longer accepting steering input.
- `response_not_active`: The response is no longer accepting steering input.
- `successor_creation_failed`: The successor response could not be created.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*anyOf*|response_not_found|
|*anyOf*|invalid_input|
|*anyOf*|steering_not_supported|
|*anyOf*|too_many_pending_steers|
|*anyOf*|response_already_completed|
|*anyOf*|response_not_active|
|*anyOf*|successor_creation_failed|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerEvent">ResponseSteerEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteerevent"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteerevent"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteerevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer",
  "previous_response_id": "string",
  "input": "string"
}
```

Queues user input to steer a response on this WebSocket connection. Input
can contain text, images, and files. Steering is supported only for
single-agent responses on models and execution modes that support steering.
Responses bound to a conversation or using automatic compaction do not
support steering.

A `response.steer.accepted` event acknowledges that the server owns the
queued input, not that it has been applied. The successor's `response.created`
event is the commit point. Input that cannot be committed is returned in
`response.steer.failed`.

Steering may cause the active response to finish at a safe output boundary
with `response.incomplete` and `incomplete_details.reason` set to `steered`,
followed automatically by a successor `response.created`. Normal completion
can also be followed by an automatic successor. Automatic successors inherit
the previous response's settings and continue from it with the queued input.

If the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, accepted
steering input remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after
`response.completed`. Fill the `required_input` stubs from that event with
saved tool results or approval decisions, and send one explicit
`response.create` per parent with the same `previous_response_id` and
WebSocket lane. Do not rerun tools or resend accepted steering input. The
queued input is prepended in submission order to that request's input, and
the explicit request retains its own settings.

This event accepts only `type`, `previous_response_id`, and `input`. Do not
send `stream_id`; the target response determines the WebSocket lane.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer`.|
|previous_response_id|string|true|none|The ID of the response to steer on this WebSocket connection.|
|input|[ResponseSteerInput](#schemaresponsesteerinput)|true|none|Input to queue for a continuation of the response. Uses the same string or<br>input-item shape as `response.create.input`, with a non-empty array when<br>supplying input items.<br><br>Steering accepts only messages with the `user` role. Each message may<br>contain only `type`, `role`, and `content`, with `content` as a string or an<br>array of `input_text`, `input_image`, and `input_file` parts. The optional<br>`type` must be `message`. Other roles, tool outputs, and item types are not<br>supported for steering.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerFailedEvent">ResponseSteerFailedEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteerfailedevent"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerFailedEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteerfailedevent"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteerfailedevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer.failed",
  "sequence_number": 0,
  "steer": {
    "id": "string",
    "previous_response_id": "string",
    "input": "string"
  },
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "response_not_found",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "stream_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when steering input is rejected or cannot be committed to a
successor response. Returns the original, uncommitted input so the client
can carry it into `response.create` when appropriate. Invalid input must
be corrected before retrying.

Failures after acceptance include the same steering ID. Failures before an
ID is allocated omit `steer.id`. A lost connection or missing acknowledgement
leaves the outcome unknown; it is not proof that the input was rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer.failed`.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|steer|object|true|none|The steering submission that could not be committed.|
|error|object|true|none|Information about why the input could not be committed.|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event, when the target response is<br>available and its `response.create` event supplied a `stream_id`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer.failed|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerPendingEvent">ResponseSteerPendingEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteerpendingevent"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerPendingEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteerpendingevent"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteerpendingevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer.pending",
  "sequence_number": 0,
  "steer": {
    "id": "string",
    "previous_response_id": "string"
  },
  "reason": "waiting_for_required_input",
  "required_input": [
    {
      "type": "function_call_output",
      "call_id": "string",
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "stream_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when accepted steering input remains queued after the target
response completes. The server still owns the input. Do not resend it.
The successor's `response.created` event is the commit point.

When `reason` is `waiting_for_required_input`, this event follows
`response.completed` while the response waits for the tool results or
approval decisions identified by `required_input`. Copy those stubs, fill
their result fields using the ordinary `response.create` input schemas,
and submit one continuation per parent with the same `previous_response_id`
and WebSocket lane. Use saved results without rerunning tools. The queued
steering input is prepended in submission order to the continuation's
input. That explicit request retains its own settings.

This notification is emitted at most once per steering submission. Multiple
submissions for the same parent can report the same required inputs; they
do not each require a separate continuation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer.pending`.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|steer|object|true|none|The steering submission that remains queued.|
|reason|[ResponseSteerPendingReason](#schemaresponsesteerpendingreason)|true|none|An extensible enum describing why accepted steering input is still queued.<br>Clients should handle unknown values because additional reasons may be<br>introduced. Known values include:<br>- `waiting_for_required_input`: The response is waiting for the tool results or approval decisions identified by `required_input`.<br>|
|required_input|[[ResponseSteerRequiredInput](#schemaresponsesteerrequiredinput)]|true|none|Input stubs identifying outstanding client-owned tool results or<br>approval decisions. Each stub contains identifying fields only; the<br>client supplies the result before including it in `response.create`.<br>|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event. This field is present when<br>the target response's `response.create` event supplied a `stream_id`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer.pending|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerPendingReason">ResponseSteerPendingReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteerpendingreason"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerPendingReason"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteerpendingreason"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteerpendingreason"></a>

```json
"waiting_for_required_input"
```

An extensible enum describing why accepted steering input is still queued.
Clients should handle unknown values because additional reasons may be
introduced. Known values include:
- `waiting_for_required_input`: The response is waiting for the tool results or approval decisions identified by `required_input`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*anyOf*|waiting_for_required_input|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseSteerRequiredInput">ResponseSteerRequiredInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsesteerrequiredinput"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseSteerRequiredInput"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsesteerrequiredinput"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsesteerrequiredinput"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "function_call_output",
  "call_id": "string",
  "name": "string"
}
```

An input stub identifying an outstanding client-owned tool result or
approval decision. Copy the stub and fill the result fields using the
corresponding `response.create` input schema. Use saved results without
rerunning the tool. The server does not supply results, approval decisions,
or safety acknowledgements in these stubs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `output` using the function tool call output input schema.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|call_id|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `output` using the custom tool call output input schema. The<br>original custom tool call supplies the tool's name.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|call_id|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `output` using the computer tool call output input schema,<br>including any required `acknowledged_safety_checks`.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|call_id|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `output` using the shell tool call output input schema. Each<br>output entry includes `stdout`, `stderr`, and `outcome`.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|call_id|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `status` and optional `output` using the apply patch tool call<br>output input schema.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|call_id|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `tools` using the tool search output input schema, retaining<br>`execution: "client"`.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|call_id|string|true|none|none|
|execution|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Supply `approve` using the MCP approval response input schema. An<br>optional `reason` can be supplied when denying the request. The original<br>approval request identifies the tool and server.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|approval_request_id|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|function_call_output|
|type|custom_tool_call_output|
|type|computer_call_output|
|type|shell_call_output|
|type|apply_patch_call_output|
|type|tool_search_output|
|execution|client|
|type|mcp_approval_response|

```json

  "format": {
    "type": "text"
  },
  "verbosity": "medium"
}
```

Configuration options for a text response from the model. Can be plain
text or structured JSON data. Learn more:
- [Text inputs and outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text)
- [Structured Outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|[TextResponseFormatConfiguration](#schematextresponseformatconfiguration)|false|none|An object specifying the format that the model must output.<br><br>Configuring `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables Structured Outputs,<br>which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the<br>[Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).<br><br>The default format is `{ "type": "text" }` with no additional options.<br><br>**Not recommended for gpt-4o and newer models:**<br><br>Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON mode, which<br>ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`<br>is preferred for models that support it.<br>|
|verbosity|[Verbosity](#schemaverbosity)|false|none|none|

Client events accepted by the Responses WebSocket server.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[ResponsesClientEventResponseCreate](#schemaresponsesclienteventresponsecreate)|false|none|Client event for creating a response over a persistent WebSocket connection.<br>This payload uses the same top-level fields as `POST /v1/responses`, plus<br>WebSocket-only envelope metadata.<br><br>Notes:<br>- `stream` is implicit over WebSocket and should not be sent.<br>- `background` is not supported over WebSocket.<br>- `stream_id` is WebSocket-only and is not part of `POST /v1/responses`.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[ResponseSteerEvent](#schemaresponsesteerevent)|false|none|Queues user input to steer a response on this WebSocket connection. Input<br>can contain text, images, and files. Steering is supported only for<br>single-agent responses on models and execution modes that support steering.<br>Responses bound to a conversation or using automatic compaction do not<br>support steering.<br><br>A `response.steer.accepted` event acknowledges that the server owns the<br>queued input, not that it has been applied. The successor's `response.created`<br>event is the commit point. Input that cannot be committed is returned in<br>`response.steer.failed`.<br><br>Steering may cause the active response to finish at a safe output boundary<br>with `response.incomplete` and `incomplete_details.reason` set to `steered`,<br>followed automatically by a successor `response.created`. Normal completion<br>can also be followed by an automatic successor. Automatic successors inherit<br>the previous response's settings and continue from it with the queued input.<br><br>If the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, accepted<br>steering input remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after<br>`response.completed`. Fill the `required_input` stubs from that event with<br>saved tool results or approval decisions, and send one explicit<br>`response.create` per parent with the same `previous_response_id` and<br>WebSocket lane. Do not rerun tools or resend accepted steering input. The<br>queued input is prepended in submission order to that request's input, and<br>the explicit request retains its own settings.<br><br>This event accepts only `type`, `previous_response_id`, and `input`. Do not<br>send `stream_id`; the target response determines the WebSocket lane.<br>|

Client event for creating a response over a persistent WebSocket connection.
This payload uses the same top-level fields as `POST /v1/responses`, plus
WebSocket-only envelope metadata.

Notes:
- `stream` is implicit over WebSocket and should not be sent.
- `background` is not supported over WebSocket.
- `stream_id` is WebSocket-only and is not part of `POST /v1/responses`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the client event. Always `response.create`.<br>|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane for this response. Requests with the same<br>`stream_id` are processed FIFO, and events for the response echo the<br>same `stream_id`.<br><br>`stream_id` controls routing; `previous_response_id` controls<br>conversation lineage, so a new lane can fork from a response created<br>on another lane.<br>|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|none|
|top_logprobs|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|none|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|none|
|user|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field is being replaced by `safety_identifier` and `prompt_cache_key`. Use `prompt_cache_key` instead to maintain caching optimizations.<br>A stable identifier for your end-users.<br>Used to boost cache hit rates by better bucketing similar requests and  to help OpenAI detect and prevent abuse. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).<br>|
|safety_identifier|string \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_cache_key|string \| null|false|none|none|
|prompt_cache_retention|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|prompt_cache_options|[PromptCacheOptionsParam](#schemapromptcacheoptionsparam)|false|none|Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.|
|top_logprobs|integer|false|none|An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the maximum number of most likely<br>tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log<br>probability. In some cases, the number of returned tokens may be fewer than<br>requested.<br>|
|previous_response_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|model|[ModelIdsResponses](#schemamodelidsresponses)|false|none|Model ID used to generate the response, like `gpt-6-astra`. OpenAI<br>offers a wide range of models with different capabilities, performance<br>characteristics, and price points. Refer to the [model guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)<br>to browse and compare available models.<br>|
|background|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|max_tool_calls|integer \| null|false|none|none|

Learn more:<br>- [Text inputs and outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text)<br>- [Structured Outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs)<br>|
|tools|[ToolsArray](#schematoolsarray)|false|none|An array of tools the model may call while generating a response. You<br>can specify which tool to use by setting the `tool_choice` parameter.<br><br>We support the following categories of tools:<br>- **Built-in tools**: Tools that are provided by OpenAI that extend the<br>  model's capabilities, like [web search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search)<br>  or [file search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search). Learn more about<br>  [built-in tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools).<br>- **MCP Tools**: Integrations with third-party systems via custom MCP servers<br>  or predefined connectors such as Google Drive and SharePoint. Learn more about<br>  [MCP Tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).<br>- **Function calls (custom tools)**: Functions that are defined by you,<br>  enabling the model to call your own code with strongly typed arguments<br>  and outputs. Learn more about<br>  [function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling). You can also use<br>  custom tools to call your own code.<br>|

|output_index|integer|true|none|The index of the output this event applies to.|
|item_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the API item associated with this event.|
|input|string|true|none|The complete input data for the custom tool call.|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event. This field is present<br>when the originating `response.create` event supplied a<br>`stream_id`.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[ResponseWsError](#schemaresponsewserror)|false|none|Emitted when an error occurs while processing a Responses WebSocket request.|
|*anyOf*|[ResponseSteerAcceptedEvent](#schemaresponsesteeracceptedevent)|false|none|Emitted when steering input has been validated and queued. Acceptance means<br>the server owns the input, not that it has been applied. The successor's<br>`response.created` event is the commit point. If accepted input cannot be<br>committed, `response.steer.failed` returns it with the same steering ID.<br><br>When the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, the input<br>remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after<br>`response.completed`. Fill the pending event's `required_input` stubs with<br>saved results and send one matching explicit `response.create` per parent.<br>Do not resend accepted input while it is still queued.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[ResponseSteerPendingEvent](#schemaresponsesteerpendingevent)|false|none|Emitted when accepted steering input remains queued after the target<br>response completes. The server still owns the input. Do not resend it.<br>The successor's `response.created` event is the commit point.<br><br>When `reason` is `waiting_for_required_input`, this event follows<br>`response.completed` while the response waits for the tool results or<br>approval decisions identified by `required_input`. Copy those stubs, fill<br>their result fields using the ordinary `response.create` input schemas,<br>and submit one continuation per parent with the same `previous_response_id`<br>and WebSocket lane. Use saved results without rerunning tools. The queued<br>steering input is prepended in submission order to the continuation's<br>input. That explicit request retains its own settings.<br><br>This notification is emitted at most once per steering submission. Multiple<br>submissions for the same parent can report the same required inputs; they<br>do not each require a separate continuation.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[ResponseSteerFailedEvent](#schemaresponsesteerfailedevent)|false|none|Emitted when steering input is rejected or cannot be committed to a<br>successor response. Returns the original, uncommitted input so the client<br>can carry it into `response.create` when appropriate. Invalid input must<br>be corrected before retrying.<br><br>Failures after acceptance include the same steering ID. Failures before an<br>ID is allocated omit `steer.id`. A lost connection or missing acknowledgement<br>leaves the outcome unknown; it is not proof that the input was rejected.<br>|

|object|string|true|none|The object type, which is always `thread.run`.|
|created_at|integer(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was created.|
|thread_id|string|true|none|The ID of the [thread](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) that was executed on as a part of this run.|
|assistant_id|string|true|none|The ID of the [assistant](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) used for execution of this run.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the run, which can be either `queued`, `in_progress`, `requires_action`, `cancelling`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `completed`, `incomplete`, or `expired`.|
|required_action|object \| null|true|none|Details on the action required to continue the run. Will be `null` if no action is required.|
|last_error|object \| null|true|none|The last error associated with this run. Will be `null` if there are no errors.|
|expires_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run will expire.|
|started_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was started.|
|cancelled_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was cancelled.|
|failed_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run failed.|
|completed_at|integer \| null(unixtime)|true|none|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was completed.|
|incomplete_details|object \| null|true|none|Details on why the run is incomplete. Will be `null` if the run is not incomplete.|
|model|string|true|none|The model that the [assistant](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) used for this run.|
|instructions|string|true|none|The instructions that the [assistant](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) used for this run.|
|tools|[[AssistantToolsCode](#schemaassistanttoolscode) \| [AssistantToolsFileSearch](#schemaassistanttoolsfilesearch) \| [AssistantToolsFunction](#schemaassistanttoolsfunction)]|true|none|The list of tools that the [assistant](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration) used for this run.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|true|none|none|
|usage|[RunCompletionUsage](#schemaruncompletionusage)|true|none|none|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|The sampling temperature used for this run. If not set, defaults to 1.|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|The nucleus sampling value used for this run. If not set, defaults to 1.|
|max_prompt_tokens|integer \| null|true|none|The maximum number of prompt tokens specified to have been used over the course of the run.<br>|
|max_completion_tokens|integer \| null|true|none|The maximum number of completion tokens specified to have been used over the course of the run.<br>|
|truncation_strategy|[TruncationObject](#schematruncationobject) \| null|true|none|none|
|tool_choice|[AssistantsApiToolChoiceOption](#schemaassistantsapitoolchoiceoption) \| null|true|none|none|
|parallel_tool_calls|[ParallelToolCalls](#schemaparalleltoolcalls)|true|none|Whether to enable [parallel function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#parallel-function-calling) during tool use.|
|response_format|[AssistantsApiResponseFormatOption](#schemaassistantsapiresponseformatoption) \| null|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_TextResponseFormatConfiguration">TextResponseFormatConfiguration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematextresponseformatconfiguration"></a>
<a id="schema_TextResponseFormatConfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocStextresponseformatconfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocstextresponseformatconfiguration"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "text"
}
```

An object specifying the format that the model must output.

Configuring `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables Structured Outputs,
which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the
[Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

The default format is `{ "type": "text" }` with no additional options.

**Not recommended for gpt-4o and newer models:**

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON mode, which
ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`
is preferred for models that support it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[ResponseFormatText](#schemaresponseformattext)|false|none|Default response format. Used to generate text responses.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[TextResponseFormatJsonSchema](#schematextresponseformatjsonschema)|false|none|JSON Schema response format. Used to generate structured JSON responses.<br>Learn more about [Structured Outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).<br>|
|*oneOf*|[ResponseFormatJsonObject](#schemaresponseformatjsonobject)|false|none|JSON object response format. An older method of generating JSON responses.<br>Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the<br>model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it<br>to do so.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ToolChoiceOptions">ToolChoiceOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematoolchoiceoptions"></a>

<a id="tocStoolchoiceoptions"></a>
<a id="tocstoolchoiceoptions"></a>

```json
"none"
```

Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.

`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.

`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or
more tools.

`required` means the model must call one or more tools.

<h2 id="tocS_ToolsArray">ToolsArray</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematoolsarray"></a>
<a id="schema_ToolsArray"></a>
<a id="tocStoolsarray"></a>
<a id="tocstoolsarray"></a>

```json
[
  {
    "type": "function",
    "name": "string",
    "async": true,
    "description": "string",
    "parameters": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "output_schema": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "strict": true,
    "defer_loading": true,
    "allowed_callers": [
      "direct"
    ]
  }
]
```

An array of tools the model may call while generating a response. You
can specify which tool to use by setting the `tool_choice` parameter.

We support the following categories of tools:
- **Built-in tools**: Tools that are provided by OpenAI that extend the
  model's capabilities, like [web search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search)
  or [file search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search). Learn more about
  [built-in tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools).
- **MCP Tools**: Integrations with third-party systems via custom MCP servers
  or predefined connectors such as Google Drive and SharePoint. Learn more about
  [MCP Tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).
- **Function calls (custom tools)**: Functions that are defined by you,
  enabling the model to call your own code with strongly typed arguments
  and outputs. Learn more about
  [function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling). You can also use
  custom tools to call your own code.

```json
  "type": "transcript.text.delta",

  "logprobs": [
    {
      "token": "string",
      "logprob": 0,
      "bytes": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ],
  "segment_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when there is an additional text delta. This is also the first event emitted when the transcription starts. Only emitted when you [create a transcription](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create) with the `Stream` parameter set to `true`.

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the event. Always `transcript.text.delta`.<br>|
|delta|string|true|none|The text delta that was additionally transcribed.<br>|
|logprobs|[object]|false|none|The log probabilities of the delta. Only included if you [create a transcription](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create) with the `include[]` parameter set to `logprobs`.<br>|
|segment_id|string|false|none|Identifier of the diarized segment that this delta belongs to. Only present when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|transcript.text.delta|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionChunkingStrategy">TranscriptionChunkingStrategy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptionchunkingstrategy"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptionChunkingStrategy"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptionchunkingstrategy"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptionchunkingstrategy"></a>

```json
"auto"
```

Controls how the audio is cut into chunks. When set to `"auto"`, the
server first normalizes loudness and then uses voice activity detection (VAD) to
choose boundaries. `server_vad` object can be provided to tweak VAD detection
parameters manually. If unset, the audio is transcribed as a single block.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Automatically set chunking parameters based on the audio. Must be set to `"auto"`.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[VadConfig](#schemavadconfig)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|auto|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h2 id="tocS_PromptCacheModeEnum">PromptCacheModeEnum</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapromptcachemodeenum"></a>
<a id="schema_PromptCacheModeEnum"></a>
<a id="tocSpromptcachemodeenum"></a>
<a id="tocspromptcachemodeenum"></a>

<h2 id="tocS_PromptCacheOptionsParam">PromptCacheOptionsParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="schema_PromptCacheOptionsParam"></a>
<a id="tocSpromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="tocspromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>

```json
{
  "ttl": "30m",
  "mode": "implicit"
}
```

Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ttl|[PromptCacheTTLEnum](#schemapromptcachettlenum)|false|none|The minimum lifetime applied to every implicit and explicit cache breakpoint written by the request. Defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. The backend may retain cache entries for longer.|
|mode|[PromptCacheModeEnum](#schemapromptcachemodeenum)|false|none|Controls whether OpenAI automatically creates an implicit cache breakpoint. Defaults to `implicit`. With `implicit`, OpenAI creates one implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest three explicit breakpoints in the request. With `explicit`, OpenAI does not create an implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest four explicit breakpoints. If there are no explicit breakpoints, the request does not use prompt caching.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ttl|30m|
|mode|implicit|
|mode|explicit|

<h2 id="tocS_PromptCacheBreakpointParam">PromptCacheBreakpointParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapromptcachebreakpointparam"></a>
<a id="schema_PromptCacheBreakpointParam"></a>
<a id="tocSpromptcachebreakpointparam"></a>
<a id="tocspromptcachebreakpointparam"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "explicit",
  "ttl": "30m"
}
```

Marks the exact end of a reusable prompt prefix. When `ttl` is omitted, the breakpoint inherits the request's `prompt_cache_options.ttl`; the boundary is not rounded to a token block.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|The breakpoint mode. Always `explicit`.|
|ttl|string|false|none|The minimum lifetime of this cache breakpoint. Defaults to the request TTL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|explicit|
|ttl|30m|
|ttl|12h|

<h2 id="tocS_IncludeEnum">IncludeEnum</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaincludeenum"></a>
<a id="schema_IncludeEnum"></a>
<a id="tocSincludeenum"></a>
<a id="tocsincludeenum"></a>

```json
"file_search_call.results"
```

Specify additional output data to include in the model response. Currently supported values are:
- `web_search_call.results`: Include the search results of the web search tool call.
- `web_search_call.action.sources`: Include the sources of the web search tool call.
- `code_interpreter_call.outputs`: Includes the outputs of python code execution in code interpreter tool call items.
- `computer_call_output.output.image_url`: Include image urls from the computer call output.
- `file_search_call.results`: Include the search results of the file search tool call.
- `message.input_image.image_url`: Include image urls from the input message.
- `message.output_text.logprobs`: Include logprobs with assistant messages.
- `reasoning.encrypted_content`: Includes an encrypted version of reasoning tokens in reasoning item outputs. This enables reasoning items to be used in multi-turn conversations when using the Responses API statelessly (like when the `store` parameter is set to `false`, or when an organization is enrolled in the zero data retention program).

```json
{
  "acknowledgement_delay_ms": 0,
  "type": "responses",
  "responses": {
    "model": "string",
    "instructions": "string",
    "max_output_tokens": 16,
    "service_tier": "auto",
    "reasoning": {
      "effort": "none",
      "summary": "concise"
    },
    "text": {
      "verbosity": "low"
    },
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {
          "property1": null,
          "property2": null
        },
        "strict": true
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "parallel_tool_calls": true
  }
}
```

Delegate tasks to a Responses model managed by the Live session.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledgement_delay_ms|integer|false|none|Milliseconds to wait before requesting an automatic spoken acknowledgement for a delegation. The model may still speak before this delay. Any commentary or thinking appended to the session cancels all pending acknowledgements, including those for other delegations. Defaults to 400 for Decisions sessions and 0 (request immediately) for other sessions. Omission in a session update preserves the current value. Updates apply to subsequent delegations.|
|type|string|true|none|The delegation owner. Always `responses` for tasks handled by the Responses API.|
|responses|[LiveResponsesDelegationSettingsInputParam](#schemaliveresponsesdelegationsettingsinputparam)|true|none|Backend model, prompt, and tools used when the Live session delegates a task to Responses.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|responses|


Control which Live events an untrusted WebRTC frontend can send and receive over its data channel. These restrictions do not apply to trusted sideband connections.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_client_events|string \| [string]|false|none|Client event types that the frontend data channel may send. Use 'all' to allow every client event; an empty array allows none. Omission preserves the existing allow-all behavior.|
|allowed_server_events|string \| [[LiveAllowedServerEventParam](#schemaliveallowedservereventparam)]|false|none|Server events that may be sent to the frontend data channel. Use 'all' to allow every server event; an empty array allows none. Omission preserves the existing allow-all behavior. Responses events use an object with type 'response.event' and a response_event selector.|
