### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledgement_delay_ms|integer|false|none|Milliseconds to wait before requesting an automatic spoken acknowledgement for a delegation. The model may still speak before this delay. Any commentary or thinking appended to the session cancels all pending acknowledgements, including those for other delegations. Defaults to 400 for Decisions sessions and 0 (request immediately) for other sessions. Omission in a session update preserves the current value. Updates apply to subsequent delegations.|
|type|string|true|none|The delegation owner. Always `responses` for tasks handled by the Responses API.|
|responses|[LiveResponsesDelegationSettingsUpdateInputParam](#schemaliveresponsesdelegationsettingsupdateinputparam)|false|none|Responses backend settings to update. Omitted settings keep their existing values.|

If omitted, the API resolves the program from the model's Cyber tier and your organization and project access, subject to model-specific eligibility restrictions. By default, models without a Cyber tier use Standard. Blue-tier models use Daybreak Blue when authorized; otherwise they fall back to Standard unless the model requires Daybreak access. Red-tier models use Daybreak Red and require authorization. Requests that require unavailable Daybreak access return 403. An implicit Standard fallback is represented by null in the response's access_programs field, rather than an explicit Standard selection.|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponsePromptCacheOptionsParam">ResponsePromptCacheOptionsParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsepromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponsePromptCacheOptionsParam"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsepromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsepromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>

```json
{
  "ttl": "30m",
  "mode": "implicit",
  "prewarm": true,
  "comparison_response_id": "resp_123"
}
```

Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ttl|[PromptCacheTTLEnum](#schemapromptcachettlenum)|false|none|The minimum lifetime applied to every implicit and explicit cache breakpoint written by the request. Defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. The backend may retain cache entries for longer.|
|mode|[PromptCacheModeEnum](#schemapromptcachemodeenum)|false|none|Controls whether OpenAI automatically creates an implicit cache breakpoint. Defaults to `implicit`. With `implicit`, OpenAI creates one implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest three explicit breakpoints in the request. With `explicit`, OpenAI does not create an implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest four explicit breakpoints. If there are no explicit breakpoints, the request does not use prompt caching.|
|prewarm|boolean|false|none|Prepares the prompt cache without generating output. Defaults to `false`. When set to `true`, overrides the `generate` field to `false`.|
|comparison_response_id|string \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ttl|30m|
|mode|implicit|
|mode|explicit|

<a id="schemadecisioninputjson"></a>
<a id="schema_DecisionInputJson"></a>
<a id="tocSdecisioninputjson"></a>
<a id="tocsdecisioninputjson"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "input_json",
  "data": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  }
}
```

A JSON object or an array of objects rendered as text. Nested values may be any JSON value. Limited to 32 container levels, 10,000 values, and 256 KiB of compact UTF-8 JSON.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|data|object \| [object]|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|input_json|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|The model to use. Only `gpt-6-luna` is supported.|
|input|[DecisionInput](#schemadecisioninput)|true|none|The input to evaluate for every question. Provide a text string or an ordered array of messages, function calls and outputs, or custom tool calls and outputs. Each tool output must identify a matching call by call ID.|
|questions|[[QuestionParam](#schemaquestionparam)]|true|none|Ask 1–400 questions about the input. Each question can be a predicate, choice, or score. Answers come back in the same order.|
|safety_identifier|string \| null|false|none|Opaque caller-provided end-user identifier, scoped by the verified org. Match Responses' limit; this is never the authenticated user identity.|
|prompt_cache_key|string \| null|false|none|Partition prompt cache reuse by caller-provided key.|
|prompt_cache_options|object \| null|false|none|Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.|

<h2 id="tocS_SessionAgentConfigParam">SessionAgentConfigParam</h2>

<a id="schemasessionagentconfigparam"></a>
<a id="schema_SessionAgentConfigParam"></a>
<a id="tocSsessionagentconfigparam"></a>
<a id="tocssessionagentconfigparam"></a>

```json
{
  "experimental": {
    "time_awareness": true
  },
  "model": "string",
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": "none",
    "summary": "concise"
  },
  "text": {
    "format": {
      "type": "text"
    },
    "verbosity": "low"
  },
  "service_tier": "auto",
  "instructions": "string",
  "multi_agent": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_concurrent_subagents": 1
  },
  "compaction": {
    "async": true
  },
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "parameters": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "defer_loading": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Agent configuration for a session. Omitted fields inherit from `agent_id` when supplied. Supplied objects and arrays replace the whole field, except experimental settings, which merge by key. Null resets nullable fields.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|experimental|[ExperimentalConfigOverridesParam](#schemaexperimentalconfigoverridesparam)|false|none|Experimental settings to merge by key. Omitted settings keep their current values.|
|model|string|false|none|The model to use for the agent. The requested model name is preserved.|
|reasoning|[ReasoningParam](#schemareasoningparam) \| null|false|none|Configuration for model reasoning. Omit to keep the current settings; pass `null` to reset to the model's default effort.|
|text|[TextParam](#schematextparam) \| null|false|none|Configuration for text generated by the agent.|
|service_tier|[ServiceTierParam](#schemaservicetierparam) \| null|false|none|The service tier used for model requests.|
|instructions|string \| null|false|none|Additional instructions appended to the agent's default base instructions. Omit to leave unchanged.|
|multi_agent|[MultiAgentConfigCurrentParam](#schemamultiagentconfigcurrentparam) \| null|false|none|Configuration for creating and coordinating subagents.|
|compaction|[CompactionParam](#schemacompactionparam) \| null|false|none|Context compaction settings. Omit to keep the current settings. A supplied object replaces the settings; null or an empty object enables background compaction.|
|tools|[[AgentToolConfigParam](#schemaagenttoolconfigparam)]|false|none|Tools available to the agent. Omit to inherit, or pass null to clear them. The resolved tool list must fit within 3 MiB (3,145,728 bytes) of compact UTF-8 JSON.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the object. Always `openai_hosted`.|
|packages|[EnvironmentPackagesParam](#schemaenvironmentpackagesparam) \| null|false|none|Packages to install in the environment. Defaults to empty package lists.|

|network|[NetworkPolicyParam](#schemanetworkpolicyparam) \| null|false|none|Network access policy for the environment. If omitted, the API version determines whether network access is enabled or disabled.|
|desktop|[DesktopParam](#schemadesktopparam) \| null|false|none|Desktop provisioning. Omission or null inherits the template setting, or defaults to disabled.|
|env|object \| null|false|none|Environment variables made available to the agent.|
|capability_directories|[string]|false|none|Directories that contain capabilities exposed to the agent. Defaults to an empty list.|
|skills|[[HostedSkillParam](#schemahostedskillparam)]|false|none|Skills referenced by ID or provided as inline ZIP archives. Defaults to an empty list.|
|plugins|[[HostedPluginParam](#schemahostedpluginparam)]|false|none|Plugins provided as inline ZIP archives. Defaults to an empty list.|
|files|[[HostedEnvironmentFileParam](#schemahostedenvironmentfileparam)]|false|none|Files available before the agent starts. Defaults to an empty list.|
|environment_id|string|false|none|An existing prewarmed environment. Cannot be combined with a template or inline configuration.|
|environment_template_id|string|false|none|A reusable hosted template applied before inline session configuration. Omitted fields inherit the template; network overrides cannot broaden its policy.|
|container_size|[ContainerSizeParam](#schemacontainersizeparam)|false|none|The hosted container size. Omission selects the medium tier.|

|Property|Value|

|container_size|small|
|container_size|medium|
|container_size|large|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateVaultCredentialAuthParamEnvironmentVariable">CreateVaultCredentialAuthParamEnvironmentVariable</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatevaultcredentialauthparamenvironmentvariable"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateVaultCredentialAuthParamEnvironmentVariable"></a>
<a id="tocScreatevaultcredentialauthparamenvironmentvariable"></a>
<a id="tocscreatevaultcredentialauthparamenvironmentvariable"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "environment_variable",
  "secret_name": "string",
  "secret_value": "string",
  "networking": {
    "type": "unrestricted"
  }
}
```

An HTTP credential for OpenAI-hosted environments only. The sandbox receives an environment variable containing a placeholder, not the secret. Use the placeholder unchanged in outgoing requests. The egress proxy replaces the placeholder with the secret for allowed HTTPS destinations on ports 443 and 8443. Sandbox code cannot read the real secret or use it for local computation, such as signing a request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the object. Always `environment_variable`.|
|secret_name|string|true|none|The environment variable name that receives the placeholder, such as `SERVICE_API_KEY`. Use ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. Names starting with `CODEX_` and managed proxy or certificate variable names are reserved.|
|secret_value|string|true|none|The write-only secret to store. Never returned in credential resources or supplied directly to sandbox code. Must be nonempty and must not contain carriage returns, newlines, or NUL bytes.|
|networking|[VaultCredentialNetworkingParam](#schemavaultcredentialnetworkingparam)|true|none|The destinations where the proxy can substitute this secret. The environment network policy must also allow them.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|environment_variable|

```json
{
```

```json
  },
```

```json
                "description": "string"

              {
                "value": "string",
                "description": "string"
              }

        ]

  ],

      "allowed_client_events": "all",
      "allowed_server_events": "all"
```

Initial configuration for a Live session, including its model, conversation instructions, audio, and delegated task handling.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|[ModelIdsLive](#schemamodelidslive)|true|none|The Live model. Required in the session configuration for every transport; do not pass it as a URL query parameter.|
|instructions|string \| null|false|none|none|
|input|[[LiveInitialItem](#schemaliveinitialitem)]|false|none|Ordered text-only history supplied before startup. Supports developer, user, and assistant messages with one text part each; at most 128 messages and a configured rendered-token limit (8,192 by default).|
|audio|[LiveInitialSessionAudioParam](#schemaliveinitialsessionaudioparam)|false|none|Startup audio configuration. Only primary WebSockets accept audio.format; WebRTC and SIP negotiate their media format. Voice and format are immutable after startup.|
|delegation|[LiveClientDelegationParam](#schemaliveclientdelegationparam) \| [LiveResponsesDelegationParam](#schemaliveresponsesdelegationparam) \| [LiveDecisionsDelegationParam](#schemalivedecisionsdelegationparam) \| null|false|none|none|
|triggers|[[LiveDecisionTriggerInputParam](#schemalivedecisiontriggerinputparam)]|false|none|At most one Decisions trigger per transcript event type. Triggers run independently of delegation. On update, omit triggers to keep the current configuration, send a list to replace it, or send an empty list to disable triggers.|
|store|boolean|false|none|Whether to store the session for later forking and recording download. Defaults to false for new sessions.|
|client|[LiveClientConfigParam](#schemaliveclientconfigparam)|false|none|Startup-only capabilities for an untrusted frontend attached to a unified WebRTC session. Trusted sideband connections are unaffected.|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayParam">LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplayparam"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayParam"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "session.output_audio.fixture.play",
  "event_id": "evt_play_001",
  "audio": "AAAAAA=="
}
```

Play one complete audio fixture through the session output. Send this event over the primary WebSocket or a server sideband. Audio must be raw mono PCM16 little-endian at 24 kHz, regardless of the session audio format, and at most 30 seconds. The entire payload is validated before model speech is interrupted and input is muted. Only one fixture can be active. fixture.playing acknowledges acceptance and fixture.played reports server mixer drain. These notifications are not exact transport-media boundaries. Input arriving during playback is dropped and not replayed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|audio|string|true|none|Base64-encoded raw mono PCM16 audio, little-endian, at 24 kHz. Do not include a WAV or other container header.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|session.output_audio.fixture.play|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveForkSessionConfigParam">LiveForkSessionConfigParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaliveforksessionconfigparam"></a>

<a id="tocsliveforksessionconfigparam"></a>

```json
{
  "audio": {
    "format": {
      "type": "audio/pcm",
      "rate": 16000
    }
  },
  "delegation": {
    "acknowledgement_delay_ms": 0,
    "type": "responses",
    "responses": {
      "model": "string",
      "instructions": "string",
      "max_output_tokens": 16,
      "service_tier": "auto",
      "reasoning": {
        "effort": "none",
        "summary": "concise"
      },
      "text": {
        "verbosity": "low"
      },
      "tools": [
        {
          "type": "function",
          "name": "string",
          "description": "string",
          "parameters": {
            "property1": null,
            "property2": null
          },
          "strict": true
        }
      ],
      "tool_choice": "auto",
      "parallel_tool_calls": true
    }
  },
  "store": true,
  "client": {
    "data_channel": {
      "allowed_client_events": "all",
      "allowed_server_events": "all"
    }
  }
}
```

Overrides for a stored session after connecting to the fork WebSocket. An empty object inherits the stored configuration; do not supply a new model. audio.format applies only to the new WebSocket connection. client overrides are only supported for WebRTC forks.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audio|[LiveForkAudioParam](#schemaliveforkaudioparam)|false|none|Audio format for a WebSocket fork. WebRTC forks negotiate their audio format and must omit this field.|
|delegation|[LiveResponsesDelegationUpdateParam](#schemaliveresponsesdelegationupdateparam)|false|none|Overrides for the stored session’s Responses backend. Only supported when the stored session already uses Responses delegation; the delegation type cannot change.|
|store|boolean|false|none|Whether to store the forked session. Omission inherits the stored session's setting.|
|client|[LiveClientConfigParam](#schemaliveclientconfigparam)|false|none|Frontend data-channel permissions for a WebRTC fork. Omitted permissions inherit the stored values. Not supported for WebSocket forks.|

```json
          {
```

```json
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ],

  "client": {

      "allowed_client_events": "all",

    }

  "id": "string",
  "expires_at": 0,
  "status": "active"

```

The resolved Live session configuration and server-assigned session metadata.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|[ModelIdsLive](#schemamodelidslive)|true|none|The Live model. Required in the session configuration for every transport; do not pass it as a URL query parameter.|
|instructions|string \| null|false|none|none|
|input|[[LiveInitialItem](#schemaliveinitialitem)]|false|none|Ordered text-only history supplied before startup. Supports developer, user, and assistant messages with one text part each; at most 128 messages and a configured rendered-token limit (8,192 by default).|
|audio|[LiveInitialSessionAudioParam](#schemaliveinitialsessionaudioparam)|false|none|Startup audio configuration. Only primary WebSockets accept audio.format; WebRTC and SIP negotiate their media format. Voice and format are immutable after startup.|
|delegation|[LiveClientDelegationParam](#schemaliveclientdelegationparam) \| [LiveResponsesDelegationParam](#schemaliveresponsesdelegationparam) \| [LiveDecisionsDelegationParam](#schemalivedecisionsdelegationparam) \| null|false|none|none|
|triggers|[[LiveDecisionTriggerInputParam](#schemalivedecisiontriggerinputparam)]|false|none|At most one Decisions trigger per transcript event type. Triggers run independently of delegation. On update, omit triggers to keep the current configuration, send a list to replace it, or send an empty list to disable triggers.|
|store|boolean|false|none|Whether to store the session for later forking and recording download. Defaults to false for new sessions.|
|client|[LiveClientConfigParam](#schemaliveclientconfigparam)|false|none|Startup-only capabilities for an untrusted frontend attached to a unified WebRTC session. Trusted sideband connections are unaffected.|
|id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the Live session. Use this ID for sideband connections, forking, and recording download.|
|expires_at|integer|true|none|The Unix timestamp, in seconds, at which the Live session expires.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the session snapshot. Always `active`, including the final snapshot in session.closed; use the event type to determine that the session has closed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|

<h2 id="tocS_LiveSessionClosed">LiveSessionClosed</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalivesessionclosed"></a>
<a id="schema_LiveSessionClosed"></a>
<a id="tocSlivesessionclosed"></a>
<a id="tocslivesessionclosed"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "session.closed",
  "event_id": "evt_closed_001",
  "client_event_id": "evt_close_001",
  "reason": "close_requested",
  "session": {
    "id": "live_abc123",
    "model": "gpt-live-1",
    "status": "active",
    "expires_at": 1788555600,
    "instructions": "Help the caller plan a restaurant reservation. Confirm details before booking.",
    "input": [],
    "audio": {
      "format": {
        "type": "audio/pcm",
        "rate": 24000
      },
      "output": {
        "voice": "marin"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "type": "client"
    }
  },
  "usage": {
    "seconds": 45.8
  }
}
```

Returned after the Live session finishes finalizing, with the close reason, final session snapshot, and cumulative audio usage. A connection closing without this event does not confirm successful finalization.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the Live server event.|
|client_event_id|string|false|none|The event_id of the client command associated with this server event, when supplied.|
|type|string|true|none|The event type, always `session.closed`.|
|reason|string|true|none|Why the Live session ended: `close_requested` for an application close or hangup request, `expired` for the session duration limit, `content` for a safety filter, `remote_hangup` for a graceful remote disconnect, or `connection_lost` for an unexpected primary or upstream disconnection.|
|session|[LiveSessionResourceParam](#schemalivesessionresourceparam)|true|none|The resolved Live session configuration and server-assigned session metadata.|
|usage|[LiveSessionUsage](#schemalivesessionusage)|true|none|The final cumulative Live audio usage after session finalization.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|session.closed|

```json
{
  "type": "session.started",

  "session": {
    "id": "live_abc123",

    "status": "active",

    "input": [],
    "audio": {
      "format": {
        "type": "audio/pcm",
        "rate": 24000
      },
      "output": {
        "voice": "marin"
      }
    },
    "delegation": {
      "type": "client"
    }
  }
}
```

An event sent by the Live API on a primary WebSocket or sideband connection.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionStarted](#schemalivesessionstarted)|false|none|Returned when a Live session has started. Contains the resolved session configuration, including server defaults.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUpdated](#schemalivesessionupdated)|false|none|Returned when a Live session update is accepted. Contains the resolved session configuration after the update.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioMuted](#schemaliveinputaudiomuted)|false|none|Acknowledges a session.input_audio.mute command. An independent input mute sends silence to the model and preserves sideband audio reflection. Fixture playback does not emit this event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioUnmuted](#schemaliveinputaudiounmuted)|false|none|Acknowledges a session.input_audio.unmute command, removing the independent input mute. An active audio fixture still pauses inference until playback finishes. Fixture playback does not emit this event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlaying](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplaying)|false|none|The existing playback path has accepted the validated audio fixture. This acknowledgment does not identify when the listener receives the first sample. The optional client_event_id echoes the play command.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayed](#schemaliveoutputaudiofixtureplayed)|false|none|The complete audio fixture has drained from the server mixer and normal inference has resumed. Transport buffers may still contain audio; this event does not prove listener-side completion. The optional client_event_id echoes the play command. This event is not emitted for canceled or failed playback.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInstructionsAppended](#schemaliveinstructionsappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.instructions.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the appended instructions without guaranteeing that the model has acted on them.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveThinkingAppended](#schemalivethinkingappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.thinking.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the added reasoning context without guaranteeing any spoken output.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveCommentaryAppended](#schemalivecommentaryappended)|false|none|Returned when a session.commentary.append command is accepted into the Live session timeline. Acknowledges the added commentary without guaranteeing exact wording or completed audio playback.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputAudioAppend](#schemaliveinputaudioappend)|false|none|Input audio received from the primary transport and reflected to a Live sideband connection before model-input muting.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputAudioDelta](#schemaliveoutputaudiodelta)|false|none|An audio chunk generated by the Live model. Decode and play primary WebSocket chunks in delivery order using the configured session audio format. Sideband connections receive reflected output audio with timestamps.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInputTranscriptDelta](#schemaliveinputtranscriptdelta)|false|none|A transcript fragment for user input audio in the Live session. Accumulate fragments in delivery order; these events do not define complete turns or include a transcript-done event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveOutputTranscriptDelta](#schemaliveoutputtranscriptdelta)|false|none|A transcript fragment for assistant output audio in the Live session. Accumulate fragments in delivery order; these events do not define complete turns or include a transcript-done event.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDelegationCreated](#schemalivedelegationcreated)|false|none|Returned when the Live model delegates work to your application, Responses, or Decisions. Contains delegation metadata and the position on the session timeline where the work was delegated.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionEvent](#schemalivedecisionevent)|false|none|A Decision API event for a Live delegation or transcript trigger. For a trigger, source_event_id identifies the transcript delta that caused this evaluation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemCreated](#schemalivedecisionitemcreated)|false|none|An input item was appended for future decisions.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveDecisionItemDeleted](#schemalivedecisionitemdeleted)|false|none|An input item was removed from future decisions.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveResponseEvent](#schemaliveresponseevent)|false|none|A streaming Responses API event from a backend delegated to by the Live session. Use the outer delegation_id to associate the nested stream with its Live delegation.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionUsageUpdated](#schemalivesessionusageupdated)|false|none|Reports cumulative Live audio usage and, when available, the most recent context-window usage. Delegated Responses token usage is reported separately in response.event events.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveSessionClosed](#schemalivesessionclosed)|false|none|Returned after the Live session finishes finalizing, with the close reason, final session snapshot, and cumulative audio usage. A connection closing without this event does not confirm successful finalization.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveErrorEvent](#schemaliveerrorevent)|false|none|Reports an error in the Live session, such as an invalid client command. Use error.client_event_id, when present, to identify the command that caused the error.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveInfoEvent](#schemaliveinfoevent)|false|none|An informational notice about the Live session, such as the event permissions applied to a frontend data channel.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFReceived](#schemalivetransportdtmfreceived)|false|none|A SIP DTMF keypress received from the caller. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportDTMFSent](#schemalivetransportdtmfsent)|false|none|A SIP DTMF keypress successfully sent to the SIP trunk. Delivered only to sideband observers; this is not a client command.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportRinging](#schemalivetransportringing)|false|none|The outbound SIP provider leg is ringing or providing early media. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportAnswered](#schemalivetransportanswered)|false|none|The outbound SIP provider leg answered and media is established. Delivered only to sideband observers.|
|*oneOf*|[LiveTransportFailed](#schemalivetransportfailed)|false|none|An asynchronous outbound SIP setup failure. Delivered only to sideband observers.|

```json
}
```

Send one DTMF keypress to the SIP trunk through a Live sideband connection. This command is supported only for SIP calls. A successful send emits `transport.dtmf.sent` on sideband. If you provide `event_id`, the success notification includes it as `client_event_id`; a failure includes it as `error.client_event_id`. Send separate events for multiple keypresses.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string \| null|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|event|string|true|none|The DTMF key to send: one of `0`–`9`, `A`–`D`, `*`, or `#`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|transport.dtmf.send|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaTextResponseFormatConfiguration">BetaTextResponseFormatConfiguration</h2>

```json
{
  "type": "text"
}
```

An object specifying the format that the model must output.

Configuring `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables Structured Outputs,
which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the
[Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

The default format is `{ "type": "text" }` with no additional options.

**Not recommended for gpt-4o and newer models:**

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON mode, which
ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`
is preferred for models that support it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaimagegentool"></a>

<a id="tocsbetaimagegentool"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "image_generation",
  "model": "string",
  "quality": "auto",
  "size": "auto",
  "output_format": "png",
  "output_compression": 100,
  "moderation": "auto",
  "background": "auto",
  "input_fidelity": "high",
  "input_image_mask": {
    "image_url": "string",
    "file_id": "string"
  },
  "partial_images": 0,
  "action": "generate"
}
```

A tool that generates images using the GPT image models.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the image generation tool. Always `image_generation`.<br>|
|model|string|false|none|none|
|quality|string|false|none|The quality of the generated image. The GPT image models support `low`,<br>`medium`, and `high`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`,<br>including their `2026-09-08` snapshots, also support `xhigh` and `max`.<br>Default: `auto`.<br>|
|size|string|false|none|The size of the generated images. For `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, arbitrary resolutions are supported as `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings, for example `1536x864`. Width and height must both be divisible by 16 and the requested aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Resolutions above `2560x1440` are experimental, and the maximum supported resolution is `3840x2160`. The requested size must also satisfy the model's current pixel and edge limits. The standard sizes `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, and `1024x1536` are supported by the GPT image models; `auto` is supported for models that allow automatic sizing.|
|output_format|string|false|none|The output format of the generated image. One of `png`, `webp`, or<br>`jpeg`. Default: `png`.<br>|
|output_compression|integer|false|none|Compression level for the output image. Default: 100.<br>|
|moderation|string|false|none|Moderation level for the generated image. Default: `auto`.<br>|
|background|string|false|none|Set the background of the generated image. One of `transparent`, `opaque`,<br>or `auto`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including<br>their `2026-09-08` snapshots, support `opaque` and `transparent`<br>backgrounds. Transparent backgrounds are available for supported GPT Image<br>models. For `gpt-image-2` and `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, this support is in<br>preview. When using `transparent`, set the output format to `png` or `webp`.<br>Default: `auto`.<br>|
|input_fidelity|[BetaInputFidelity](#schemabetainputfidelity) \| null|false|none|none|
|input_image_mask|object|false|none|Optional mask for inpainting. Contains `image_url`<br>(string, optional) and `file_id` (string, optional).<br>|
|partial_images|integer|false|none|Number of partial images to generate in streaming mode, from 0 (default value) to 3.<br>|
|action|[BetaImageGenActionEnum](#schemabetaimagegenactionenum)|false|none|Whether to generate a new image or edit an existing image. Default: `auto`.<br>|

|output_format|jpeg|

```json
{
  "type": "mcp",

  "connector_id": "connector_dropbox",
  "tunnel_id": "string",

    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },

  ],

    "direct"
  ],

  "defer_loading": true
}
```

Give the model access to additional tools via remote Model Context Protocol
(MCP) servers. [Learn more about MCP](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the MCP tool. Always `mcp`.|
|server_label|string|true|none|A label for this MCP server, used to identify it in tool calls.<br>|
|server_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL for the MCP server. One of `server_url`, `connector_id`, or<br>`tunnel_id` must be provided.<br>|
|connector_id|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Identifier for service connectors, like those available in ChatGPT. One of<br>`server_url`, `connector_id`, or `tunnel_id` must be provided. Learn more<br>about service connectors [here](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp#connectors).<br><br>This field is deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026.<br>Use `server_url` to connect to a remote MCP server, or `tunnel_id` to<br>connect through a Secure MCP Tunnel.<br><br>Currently supported `connector_id` values are:<br><br>- Dropbox: `connector_dropbox`<br>- Gmail: `connector_gmail`<br>- Google Calendar: `connector_googlecalendar`<br>- Google Drive: `connector_googledrive`<br>- Microsoft Teams: `connector_microsoftteams`<br>- Outlook Calendar: `connector_outlookcalendar`<br>- Outlook Email: `connector_outlookemail`<br>- SharePoint: `connector_sharepoint`<br>|
|tunnel_id|string|false|none|The Secure MCP Tunnel ID to use instead of a direct server URL. One of<br>`server_url`, `connector_id`, or `tunnel_id` must be provided.<br>|
|authorization|string|false|none|An OAuth access token that can be used with a remote MCP server, either<br>with a custom MCP server URL or a service connector. Your application<br>must handle the OAuth authorization flow and provide the token here.<br>|
|server_description|string|false|none|Optional description of the MCP server, used to provide more context.<br>|
|headers|object \| null|false|none|none|
|allowed_tools|[string] \| [BetaMCPToolFilter](#schemabetamcptoolfilter) \| null|false|none|none|
|allowed_callers|[[BetaCallableToolAllowedCaller](#schemabetacallabletoolallowedcaller)] \| null|false|none|none|
|require_approval|object \| string \| null|false|none|none|
|defer_loading|boolean|false|none|Whether this MCP tool is deferred and discovered via tool search.<br>|

for subsequent turns of a conversation if you are manually
[managing context](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|agent|[BetaAgentTag](#schemabetaagenttag) \| null|false|none|The agent that produced this item.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the object. Always `reasoning`.<br>|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the reasoning content.<br>|
|encrypted_content|string \| null|false|none|none|
|summary|[[BetaSummaryTextContent](#schemabetasummarytextcontent)]|true|none|Reasoning summary content.<br>|
|content|[[BetaReasoningTextContent](#schemabetareasoningtextcontent)]|false|none|Reasoning text content.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the item. One of `in_progress`, `completed`, or<br>`incomplete`. Populated when items are returned via API.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|status|incomplete|

<a id="schema_BetaMessagePhase"></a>
<a id="tocSbetamessagephase"></a>
<a id="tocsbetamessagephase"></a>

```json
"commentary"
```

Labels an `assistant` message as intermediate commentary (`commentary`) or the final answer (`final_answer`).
For models like `gpt-5.3-codex` and beyond, when sending follow-up requests, preserve and resend
phase on all assistant messages — dropping it can degrade performance. Not used for user messages.

<a id="schemabetaeasyinputmessage"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaEasyInputMessage"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaeasyinputmessage"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaeasyinputmessage"></a>

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "string",
  "phase": "commentary",
  "type": "message"
}
```

A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take
precedence over instructions given with the `user` role. Messages with the
`assistant` role are presumed to have been generated by the model in previous
interactions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|string|true|none|The role of the message input. One of `user`, `assistant`, `system`, or<br>`developer`.<br>|
|content|string \| [BetaInputMessageContentList](#schemabetainputmessagecontentlist)|true|none|Text, image, or audio input to the model, used to generate a response.<br>Can also contain previous assistant responses.<br>|
|phase|[BetaMessagePhase](#schemabetamessagephase) \| null|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the message input. Always `message`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|user|
|role|assistant|
|role|system|
|role|developer|
|type|message|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaPromptCacheOptionsParam">BetaPromptCacheOptionsParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetapromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaPromptCacheOptionsParam"></a>
<a id="tocSbetapromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="tocsbetapromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>

```json
{
  "ttl": "30m",
  "mode": "implicit"
}
```

Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ttl|[BetaPromptCacheTTLEnum](#schemabetapromptcachettlenum)|false|none|The minimum lifetime applied to every implicit and explicit cache breakpoint written by the request. Defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. The backend may retain cache entries for longer.|
|mode|[BetaPromptCacheModeEnum](#schemabetapromptcachemodeenum)|false|none|Controls whether OpenAI automatically creates an implicit cache breakpoint. Defaults to `implicit`. With `implicit`, OpenAI creates one implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest three explicit breakpoints in the request. With `explicit`, OpenAI does not create an implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest four explicit breakpoints. If there are no explicit breakpoints, the request does not use prompt caching.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ttl|30m|
|mode|implicit|
|mode|explicit|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaToolsArray">BetaToolsArray</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetatoolsarray"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaToolsArray"></a>
<a id="tocSbetatoolsarray"></a>
<a id="tocsbetatoolsarray"></a>

```json
[
  {
    "type": "function",
    "name": "string",
    "async": true,
    "description": "string",
    "parameters": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "output_schema": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "strict": true,
    "defer_loading": true,
    "allowed_callers": [
      "direct"
    ]
  }
]
```

An array of tools the model may call while generating a response. You
can specify which tool to use by setting the `tool_choice` parameter.

We support the following categories of tools:
- **Built-in tools**: Tools that are provided by OpenAI that extend the
  model's capabilities, like [web search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search)
  or [file search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search). Learn more about
  [built-in tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools).
- **MCP Tools**: Integrations with third-party systems via custom MCP servers
  or predefined connectors such as Google Drive and SharePoint. Learn more about
  [MCP Tools](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).
- **Function calls (custom tools)**: Functions that are defined by you,
  enabling the model to call your own code with strongly typed arguments
  and outputs. Learn more about
  [function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling). You can also use
  custom tools to call your own code.

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseLogProb">BetaResponseLogProb</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponselogprob"></a>

<a id="tocsbetaresponselogprob"></a>

```json
  "token": "string",
  "logprob": 0,
  "top_logprobs": [
    {
      "token": "string",
      "logprob": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

A logprob is the logarithmic probability that the model assigns to producing 
a particular token at a given position in the sequence. Less-negative (higher) 
logprob values indicate greater model confidence in that token choice.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|string|true|none|A possible text token.|
|logprob|number|true|none|The log probability of this token.<br>|
|top_logprobs|[object]|false|none|The log probabilities of up to 20 of the most likely tokens.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerFailedEvent">BetaResponseSteerFailedEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsesteerfailedevent"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponseSteerFailedEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsesteerfailedevent"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsesteerfailedevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer.failed",
  "sequence_number": 0,
  "steer": {
    "id": "string",
    "previous_response_id": "string",
    "input": "string"
  },
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "response_not_found",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "stream_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when steering input is rejected or cannot be committed to a
successor response. Returns the original, uncommitted input so the client
can carry it into `response.create` when appropriate. Invalid input must
be corrected before retrying.

Failures after acceptance include the same steering ID. Failures before an
ID is allocated omit `steer.id`. A lost connection or missing acknowledgement
leaves the outcome unknown; it is not proof that the input was rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer.failed`.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|steer|object|true|none|The steering submission that could not be committed.|
|error|object|true|none|Information about why the input could not be committed.|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event, when the target response is<br>available and its `response.create` event supplied a `stream_id`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer.failed|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerErrorCode">BetaResponseSteerErrorCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsesteererrorcode"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponseSteerErrorCode"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsesteererrorcode"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsesteererrorcode"></a>

```json
"response_not_found"
```

A machine-readable steering error code. Clients should handle unknown
values because additional codes may be introduced. Known values include:
- `response_not_found`: The target response is not available on this connection.
- `invalid_input`: The event or input failed validation.
- `steering_not_supported`: The model or response execution mode does not support steering.
- `too_many_pending_steers`: Too much steering input is pending for the response.
- `response_already_completed`: The response completed and is no longer accepting steering input.
- `response_not_active`: The response is no longer accepting steering input.
- `successor_creation_failed`: The successor response could not be created.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*anyOf*|response_not_found|
|*anyOf*|invalid_input|
|*anyOf*|steering_not_supported|
|*anyOf*|too_many_pending_steers|
|*anyOf*|response_already_completed|
|*anyOf*|response_not_active|
|*anyOf*|successor_creation_failed|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerInput">BetaResponseSteerInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsesteerinput"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponseSteerInput"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsesteerinput"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsesteerinput"></a>

```json
"string"
```

Input to queue for a continuation of the response. Uses the same string or
input-item shape as `response.create.input`, with a non-empty array when
supplying input items.

Steering accepts only messages with the `user` role. Each message may
contain only `type`, `role`, and `content`, with `content` as a string or an
array of `input_text`, `input_image`, and `input_file` parts. The optional
`type` must be `message`. Other roles, tool outputs, and item types are not
supported for steering.

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerPendingEvent">BetaResponseSteerPendingEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsesteerpendingevent"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponseSteerPendingEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsesteerpendingevent"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsesteerpendingevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer.pending",
  "sequence_number": 0,
  "steer": {
    "id": "string",
    "previous_response_id": "string"
  },
  "reason": "waiting_for_required_input",
  "required_input": [
    {
      "type": "function_call_output",
      "call_id": "string",
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "stream_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when accepted steering input remains queued after the target
response completes. The server still owns the input. Do not resend it.
The successor's `response.created` event is the commit point.

When `reason` is `waiting_for_required_input`, this event follows
`response.completed` while the response waits for the tool results or
approval decisions identified by `required_input`. Copy those stubs, fill
their result fields using the ordinary `response.create` input schemas,
and submit one continuation per parent with the same `previous_response_id`
and WebSocket lane. Use saved results without rerunning tools. The queued
steering input is prepended in submission order to the continuation's
input. That explicit request retains its own settings.

This notification is emitted at most once per steering submission. Multiple
submissions for the same parent can report the same required inputs; they
do not each require a separate continuation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer.pending`.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|steer|object|true|none|The steering submission that remains queued.|
|reason|[BetaResponseSteerPendingReason](#schemabetaresponsesteerpendingreason)|true|none|An extensible enum describing why accepted steering input is still queued.<br>Clients should handle unknown values because additional reasons may be<br>introduced. Known values include:<br>- `waiting_for_required_input`: The response is waiting for the tool results or approval decisions identified by `required_input`.<br>|
|required_input|[[BetaResponseSteerRequiredInput](#schemabetaresponsesteerrequiredinput)]|true|none|Input stubs identifying outstanding client-owned tool results or<br>approval decisions. Each stub contains identifying fields only; the<br>client supplies the result before including it in `response.create`.<br>|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event. This field is present when<br>the target response's `response.create` event supplied a `stream_id`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer.pending|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerPendingReason">BetaResponseSteerPendingReason</h2>

```json
"waiting_for_required_input"
```

An extensible enum describing why accepted steering input is still queued.
Clients should handle unknown values because additional reasons may be
introduced. Known values include:
- `waiting_for_required_input`: The response is waiting for the tool results or approval decisions identified by `required_input`.

|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*anyOf*|waiting_for_required_input|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerAcceptedEvent">BetaResponseSteerAcceptedEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsesteeracceptedevent"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponseSteerAcceptedEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsesteeracceptedevent"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsesteeracceptedevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer.accepted",
  "sequence_number": 0,
  "steer": {
    "id": "string",
    "previous_response_id": "string"
  },
  "stream_id": "string"
}
```

Emitted when steering input has been validated and queued. Acceptance means
the server owns the input, not that it has been applied. The successor's
`response.created` event is the commit point. If accepted input cannot be
committed, `response.steer.failed` returns it with the same steering ID.

When the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, the input
remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after
`response.completed`. Fill the pending event's `required_input` stubs with
saved results and send one matching explicit `response.create` per parent.
Do not resend accepted input while it is still queued.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer.accepted`.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|steer|object|true|none|The accepted steering submission.|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The WebSocket lane that emitted this event. This field is present when<br>the target response's `response.create` event supplied a `stream_id`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer.accepted|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponseSteerEvent">BetaResponseSteerEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsesteerevent"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponseSteerEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsesteerevent"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsesteerevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "response.steer",
  "previous_response_id": "string",
  "input": "string"
}
```

Queues user input to steer a response on this WebSocket connection. Input
can contain text, images, and files. Steering is supported only for
single-agent responses on models and execution modes that support steering.
Responses bound to a conversation or using automatic compaction do not
support steering.

A `response.steer.accepted` event acknowledges that the server owns the
queued input, not that it has been applied. The successor's `response.created`
event is the commit point. Input that cannot be committed is returned in
`response.steer.failed`.

Steering may cause the active response to finish at a safe output boundary
with `response.incomplete` and `incomplete_details.reason` set to `steered`,
followed automatically by a successor `response.created`. Normal completion
can also be followed by an automatic successor. Automatic successors inherit
the previous response's settings and continue from it with the queued input.

If the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, accepted
steering input remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after
`response.completed`. Fill the `required_input` stubs from that event with
saved tool results or approval decisions, and send one explicit
`response.create` per parent with the same `previous_response_id` and
WebSocket lane. Do not rerun tools or resend accepted steering input. The
queued input is prepended in submission order to that request's input, and
the explicit request retains its own settings.

This event accepts only `type`, `previous_response_id`, and `input`. Do not
send `stream_id`; the target response determines the WebSocket lane.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.steer`.|
|previous_response_id|string|true|none|The ID of the response to steer on this WebSocket connection.|
|input|[BetaResponseSteerInput](#schemabetaresponsesteerinput)|true|none|Input to queue for a continuation of the response. Uses the same string or<br>input-item shape as `response.create.input`, with a non-empty array when<br>supplying input items.<br><br>Steering accepts only messages with the `user` role. Each message may<br>contain only `type`, `role`, and `content`, with `content` as a string or an<br>array of `input_text`, `input_image`, and `input_file` parts. The optional<br>`type` must be `message`. Other roles, tool outputs, and item types are not<br>supported for steering.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.steer|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaIncludeEnum">BetaIncludeEnum</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaincludeenum"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaIncludeEnum"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaincludeenum"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaincludeenum"></a>

```json
"file_search_call.results"
```

Specify additional output data to include in the model response. Currently supported values are:
- `web_search_call.results`: Include the search results of the web search tool call.
- `web_search_call.action.sources`: Include the sources of the web search tool call.
- `code_interpreter_call.outputs`: Includes the outputs of python code execution in code interpreter tool call items.
- `computer_call_output.output.image_url`: Include image urls from the computer call output.
- `file_search_call.results`: Include the search results of the file search tool call.
- `message.input_image.image_url`: Include image urls from the input message.
- `message.output_text.logprobs`: Include logprobs with assistant messages.
- `reasoning.encrypted_content`: Includes an encrypted version of reasoning tokens in reasoning item outputs. This enables reasoning items to be used in multi-turn conversations when using the Responses API statelessly (like when the `store` parameter is set to `false`, or when an organization is enrolled in the zero data retention program).

|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseSteerAcceptedEvent](#schemabetaresponsesteeracceptedevent)|false|none|Emitted when steering input has been validated and queued. Acceptance means<br>the server owns the input, not that it has been applied. The successor's<br>`response.created` event is the commit point. If accepted input cannot be<br>committed, `response.steer.failed` returns it with the same steering ID.<br><br>When the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, the input<br>remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after<br>`response.completed`. Fill the pending event's `required_input` stubs with<br>saved results and send one matching explicit `response.create` per parent.<br>Do not resend accepted input while it is still queued.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseSteerPendingEvent](#schemabetaresponsesteerpendingevent)|false|none|Emitted when accepted steering input remains queued after the target<br>response completes. The server still owns the input. Do not resend it.<br>The successor's `response.created` event is the commit point.<br><br>When `reason` is `waiting_for_required_input`, this event follows<br>`response.completed` while the response waits for the tool results or<br>approval decisions identified by `required_input`. Copy those stubs, fill<br>their result fields using the ordinary `response.create` input schemas,<br>and submit one continuation per parent with the same `previous_response_id`<br>and WebSocket lane. Use saved results without rerunning tools. The queued<br>steering input is prepended in submission order to the continuation's<br>input. That explicit request retains its own settings.<br><br>This notification is emitted at most once per steering submission. Multiple<br>submissions for the same parent can report the same required inputs; they<br>do not each require a separate continuation.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseSteerFailedEvent](#schemabetaresponsesteerfailedevent)|false|none|Emitted when steering input is rejected or cannot be committed to a<br>successor response. Returns the original, uncommitted input so the client<br>can carry it into `response.create` when appropriate. Invalid input must<br>be corrected before retrying.<br><br>Failures after acceptance include the same steering ID. Failures before an<br>ID is allocated omit `steer.id`. A lost connection or missing acknowledgement<br>leaves the outcome unknown; it is not proof that the input was rejected.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseInjectCreatedEvent](#schemabetaresponseinjectcreatedevent)|false|none|Emitted when all injected input items were validated and committed to the<br>active response.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseInjectFailedEvent](#schemabetaresponseinjectfailedevent)|false|none|Emitted when injected input could not be committed to a response. The event<br>returns the uncommitted raw input so the client can retry it in another<br>response when appropriate.<br>|

Emitted when injected input could not be committed to a response. The event
returns the uncommitted raw input so the client can retry it in another
response when appropriate.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The event discriminator. Always `response.inject.failed`.|
|response_id|string|true|none|The ID of the response that rejected the input.|
|input|[[BetaInputItem](#schemabetainputitem)]|true|none|The raw input items that were not committed.|
|error|object|true|none|Information about why the input was not committed.|
|sequence_number|integer|true|none|The sequence number for this event.|
|stream_id|string|false|none|The multiplexed WebSocket stream that emitted the event. This field is<br>present only when WebSocket multiplexing is enabled separately.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|response.inject.failed|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponsesClientEventResponseCreate](#schemabetaresponsesclienteventresponsecreate)|false|none|Client event for creating a response over a persistent WebSocket connection.<br>This payload uses the same top-level fields as `POST /v1/responses`, plus<br>WebSocket-only envelope metadata.<br><br>Notes:<br>- `stream` is implicit over WebSocket and should not be sent.<br>- `background` is not supported over WebSocket.<br>- `stream_id` is WebSocket-only and is not part of `POST /v1/responses`.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseSteerEvent](#schemabetaresponsesteerevent)|false|none|Queues user input to steer a response on this WebSocket connection. Input<br>can contain text, images, and files. Steering is supported only for<br>single-agent responses on models and execution modes that support steering.<br>Responses bound to a conversation or using automatic compaction do not<br>support steering.<br><br>A `response.steer.accepted` event acknowledges that the server owns the<br>queued input, not that it has been applied. The successor's `response.created`<br>event is the commit point. Input that cannot be committed is returned in<br>`response.steer.failed`.<br><br>Steering may cause the active response to finish at a safe output boundary<br>with `response.incomplete` and `incomplete_details.reason` set to `steered`,<br>followed automatically by a successor `response.created`. Normal completion<br>can also be followed by an automatic successor. Automatic successors inherit<br>the previous response's settings and continue from it with the queued input.<br><br>If the response stops for client-owned tool output or approval, accepted<br>steering input remains queued and `response.steer.pending` is emitted after<br>`response.completed`. Fill the `required_input` stubs from that event with<br>saved tool results or approval decisions, and send one explicit<br>`response.create` per parent with the same `previous_response_id` and<br>WebSocket lane. Do not rerun tools or resend accepted steering input. The<br>queued input is prepended in submission order to that request's input, and<br>the explicit request retains its own settings.<br><br>This event accepts only `type`, `previous_response_id`, and `input`. Do not<br>send `stream_id`; the target response determines the WebSocket lane.<br>|
|*anyOf*|[BetaResponseInjectEvent](#schemabetaresponseinjectevent)|false|none|Injects input items into an active response over a WebSocket connection.<br>The items are validated and committed atomically. Currently, the server<br>accepts client-owned tool outputs that resume a waiting agent.<br>|

Client event for creating a response over a persistent WebSocket connection.
This payload uses the same top-level fields as `POST /v1/responses`, plus
WebSocket-only envelope metadata.

Notes:
- `stream` is implicit over WebSocket and should not be sent.
- `background` is not supported over WebSocket.
- `stream_id` is WebSocket-only and is not part of `POST /v1/responses`.

Configuration for server-hosted multi-agent execution.

### Properties

|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether to enable server-hosted multi-agent execution for this response.|
|max_concurrent_subagents|integer|false|none|`max_concurrent_subagents` sets the maximum number of subagents that can be active simultaneously across the entire agent tree. It includes all descendants—children, grandchildren, and deeper subagents—but excludes the root agent.<br>The API does not impose a fixed upper bound on this setting. The default is `3`, which is recommended for most workloads. Multi-agent runs also have no fixed limit on tree depth or the total number of subagents created during a run.|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaResponsePromptCacheOptionsParam">BetaResponsePromptCacheOptionsParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaresponsepromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaResponsePromptCacheOptionsParam"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaresponsepromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaresponsepromptcacheoptionsparam"></a>

```json
{
  "ttl": "30m",
  "mode": "implicit",
  "prewarm": true,
  "comparison_response_id": "resp_123"
}
```

Options for prompt caching. Supported for `gpt-5.6` and later models. By default, OpenAI automatically chooses one implicit cache breakpoint. You can add explicit breakpoints to content blocks with `prompt_cache_breakpoint`. Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. See the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) for current details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ttl|[BetaPromptCacheTTLEnum](#schemabetapromptcachettlenum)|false|none|The minimum lifetime applied to every implicit and explicit cache breakpoint written by the request. Defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value. The backend may retain cache entries for longer.|
|mode|[BetaPromptCacheModeEnum](#schemabetapromptcachemodeenum)|false|none|Controls whether OpenAI automatically creates an implicit cache breakpoint. Defaults to `implicit`. With `implicit`, OpenAI creates one implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest three explicit breakpoints in the request. With `explicit`, OpenAI does not create an implicit breakpoint and writes up to the latest four explicit breakpoints. If there are no explicit breakpoints, the request does not use prompt caching.|
|prewarm|boolean|false|none|Prepares the prompt cache without generating output. Defaults to `false`. When set to `true`, overrides the `generate` field to `false`.|
|comparison_response_id|string \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ttl|30m|
|mode|implicit|
|mode|explicit|

<h2 id="tocS_BetaAccessProgramsParam">BetaAccessProgramsParam</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabetaaccessprogramsparam"></a>
<a id="schema_BetaAccessProgramsParam"></a>
<a id="tocSbetaaccessprogramsparam"></a>
<a id="tocsbetaaccessprogramsparam"></a>

```json
{
  "cyber": "standard"
}
```

Domain-specific access programs to use for this request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cyber|[BetaCyberAccessProgramEnum](#schemabetacyberaccessprogramenum)|false|none|The Cyber access program to use for this request. Supported values are `standard`, `daybreak_blue`, and `daybreak_red`. If omitted, the API resolves the program from the model's Cyber tier and your organization and project access, subject to model-specific eligibility restrictions. By default, models without a Cyber tier use Standard. Blue-tier models use Daybreak Blue when authorized; otherwise they fall back to Standard unless the model requires Daybreak access. Red-tier models use Daybreak Red and require authorization. Requests that require unavailable Daybreak access return 403. An implicit Standard fallback is represented by null in the response's access_programs field, rather than an explicit Standard selection.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cyber|standard|
|cyber|daybreak_blue|
|cyber|daybreak_red|
